a_rows_sample.anchor: T-K6 (Evidence pipeline: possibility and impossibility). (a) Raw-level impossibility ... There is no aggregator F: Multiset([0,1]) -> (Q,<=) satisfying both duplicate invariance and independent corroboration ... Consequence. Duplicate/dependency safety cannot be an operator property ... This upgrade
a_rows_sample.statement: T-K6a (raw-level impossibility), PROVEN: no aggregator F from multisets of strengths to any ordered codomain can satisfy both duplicate invariance and independent corroboration, since a duplicate-vs-independent addition of the same strength value is indistinguishable as a multiset (proved by the explicit counterexample M={0.7}, M1=M2={0.7,0.7} yet (A) demands F(M1)=F(M) while (B) demands F(M2)>F(M)); consequence: duplicate/dependency safety cannot be a raw-operator property, must instead belong to a normalization stage N with access to identity/dependency structure -- upgrading GN-46's informal observation to a theorem and showing EXP-01's raw-operator failures were inevitable. T-K6b (pipeline-level I-5/I-6), PROVEN UNDER ASSUMPTIONS KA3: if N's output depends only on ~-class structure and <-reduced support, then any operator composed after N is duplicate-invariant and dependency non-inflating by construction; the entire proof load transfers onto the unconstructed identity calculus (LB-2) -- 'I-5 is exactly as sound as ~ is well-defined'. T-K6c (signed monotonicity per operator, extending TV-F-001), PROVEN by direct per-operator computation: SATURATING and MAX aggregators are non-decreasing under admissible-independent addition, BAYES-odds is non-decreasing under the supporting-item LR>=1 convention, but WEIGHTED MEAN is NOT (counterexample mean(0.9,0.1)=0.5<0.9), so step-004 sec.6's monotonicity axiom is satisfiable and discriminating, correctly ruling weighted mean out as an admissible aggregation policy -- consistent with and explaining its EXP-01 failures.

a_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-010 proves (class B) exactly which identity relations the theory forces and what structure each must have: evidence content-equivalence ~ must be a full equivalence relation (needed for N's quotient construction, T-K6b); evidence dependency < must be a strict partial order/DAG (a cycle would make the discount ill-founded, upgrading 025a-5's previously-PROPOSED AcyclicDerivationGraph to REQUIRED-BY the evidence pipeline); evidence token identity needs only syntactic/registration identity finer than ~; event identity needs only payload equality (no semantic identity); requirement identity needs stable identifiers plus a version poset; state equality (K_t=K_t') is needed by NO rim theorem at all, dispensable except at the verification-report level; frame equivalence is blocked behind the still-underspecified measurement layer, off the critical path. Key structural result: the theory forces a two-sorted identity structure on evidence (content-class via ~, provenance-node via <) because its own axioms must simultaneously distinguish duplicates and derived items, which T-K6a's impossibility (S1443, this batch) shows strengths alone cannot do -- this structural requirement IS derivable from A1-A4 plus the executed tests, but the concrete ~ and < constructions themselves are NOT derivable (a domain/semantic judgment, echoing the corpus's own 'cannot be Hash(Text)').

Zadeh pathology:
a_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-014-A audits Dempster-Shafer combination: the rule itself is mathematically valid (standard, PROVEN) but requires three assumptions the corpus never states and which actively conflict with corpus doctrine -- a fixed exhaustive mutually-exclusive frame (closed-world, colliding with the corpus's open-hypothesis discipline), independence of belief sources (exactly the property the corpus's own central hazard, I64, says cannot be assumed), and normalization by 1-K which discards conflict mass, colliding with the corpus's contradiction-preservation doctrine (A3/E-K6, 'Conflict retained'). Constructs two explicit counterexamples for KnowledgeOS-style use: a duplicate-inflation case where combining a source m({A})=0.6 with its own exact copy yields Bel(A)=1-0.4^2=0.84>0.6 (the Dempster-Shafer analogue of T-K6a's aggregation-impossibility theorem, S1443 this batch); and the classic Zadeh pathology where two near-totally-conflicting sources combine to Bel(C)=1, resolving near-total conflict into false certainty about the very alternative both sources almost excluded. Verdict: the rule is PROVEN but its KnowledgeOS use is UNVERIFIED-to-CONTRADICTED, confirming C-039 as 'an assumption gap with teeth'; Dempster-Shafer remains legitimate only as an ignorance-representation structure ([Bel,Pl] intervals), the combination rule specifically being the defective import.

a_rows_sample.statement: TV-F-015 compares five uncertainty taxonomies pairwise (T1: an 8-vector over a proposition's uncertainty types; T2: 5 additive contributions to decision uncertainty; T3: 7 tags including governance; T4: an epistemic/aleatory reducibility split; T5: SNF's semantic/representational/epistemic compiler-stage classification) and finds T1-T4 compatible as a granularity coarsening, T1-T3 overlapping with 6 shared tags but incompatible as partitions, T1-T2 incompatible as classifications of the same thing (mixing source-typed and phenomenon-typed axes), T2-T3 partially overlapping, and T5 orthogonal in scope to all others (classifying pipeline stages, not uncertainty kinds). Key result: the five taxonomies classify five genuinely different constructs sharing one English word ('uncertainty'), not one contested concept -- reclassifying C-007 from a 'conflict' to a G11 terminology-overload gap, with the residual defect being unqualified cross-references that never state which construct is meant. Explicitly answers whether the corpus requires one universal uncertainty representation: NO, it explicitly requires the opposite (a universal scalar is named as an anti-pattern; bounded-context-relative representations are called for) -- any future unification would be at most a tag algebra with a declared construct per tag, offered only as a PROPOSED direction, not performed here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Let the goal be G. The goal induces a set of required knowledge conditions: R_G={r_1,r_2,...,r_n}. For Nexus migration ... r_1=CurrentVersionKnown ... r_7=GovernanceApprovalObtained. This is crucial: Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone. We need the Epistemic Contract that tells us what must
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge Requirement set R_G induced by a goal G (worked with seven Nexus-migration requirements r1-r7), establishing that Zero cannot be computed from the goal alone and requires an Epistemic Contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Define EC_G=(R_G,Gamma_G) where R_G = required conditions; Gamma_G = rules determining sufficiency. So EC_G = what must be established + how sufficiency is judged. This gives Zero a formal input.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Epistemic Contract EC_G=(R_G,Γ_G) — required conditions plus sufficiency rules — as Zero's formal input.

b_rows_sample.anchor: For each requirement r_i, we evaluate its status against K_t. Define Sat(K_t,r_i). Initially I propose the following state set: S={Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable}. This is already much richer than Boolean logic.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a nine-value requirement-satisfaction status set (Satisfied, PartiallySatisfied, Unknown, Insufficient, Conflicted, Stale, Invalid, Prohibited, NotApplicable), explicitly richer than Boolean logic.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Sat(K,r)=False. That could mean: we know it is false; we don't know; evidence conflicts; evidence is stale; evidence was invalidated; governance prohibits the action. These are operationally very different. Therefore Sat != Boolean.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Sat≠Boolean: a bare False collapses six operationally distinct situations (known-false, unknown, conflicting, stale, invalidated, prohibited) into one indistinguishable value.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We can define Z_i=Status(K_t,r_i,EC_G). Then Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i) | r_i in R_G}. This gives us a Zero vector. For example Z(K)=[Satisfied,Satisfied,Unknown,Insufficient,Conflicted,Satisfied,Missing]. Now Zero is computationally representable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Zero(K_t,G,EC_G)={(r_i,Z_i)} as a computationally representable 'Zero vector' of per-requirement statuses.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Case A: No evidence exists: Evidence(r)=empty. Status: Unknown. Case B: Governance requires approval, and no approval exists. That is Missing. These are different. So I recommend Missing as a separate status where the requirement itself is an expected governed artifact/action.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Unknown (no evidence exists at all) from Missing (an expected governed artifact/action, such as an approval, that does not exist) as two different status values.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose current KnowledgeState contains A_1: NexusVersion=3.69, A_2: RepositoryCount=43, but nothing about rollback. Then Status(r_1)=Satisfied but Status(r_3)=Unknown. If Architecture Board approval is explicitly required and has not been issued: Status(r_7)=Missing. Therefore Zero(K)={r_3:Unknown,
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked Nexus example computing a concrete Zero(K)={r3:Unknown, r7:Missing} from partial knowledge state evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We can therefore define Zero(K,G,EC)=R_G \ Satisfied(K,R_G) but this is only a shorthand. The real result must retain why each requirement is not satisfied. So Zero={Requirement, Status, Evidence, Reason, Dependencies}.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a shorthand set-difference definition of Zero (R_G minus satisfied requirements) into the fuller structured form Zero={Requirement,Status,Evidence,Reason,Dependencies}, retaining why each requirement is unsatisfied.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zero item should look conceptually like: Requirement: RollbackVerified; Status: Unknown; SupportingEvidence: none; BlockingReason: no successful restore test; RequiredAction: perform restore test; DecisionCriticality: high. This is already implementable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a concrete implementable structured-Zero-item template with six fields (Requirement, Status, SupportingEvidence, BlockingReason, RequiredAction, DecisionCriticality).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_1 supports RollbackVerified=True. Is that enough? Not necessarily. The epistemic contract may require 2 independent tests. Or 1 test witnessed by a designated authority. Or Probability(success)>=0.99. Therefore Satisfied = ContractSpecific.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that satisfaction of a requirement is ContractSpecific — the same supporting evidence may or may not count as satisfied depending on the epistemic contract's own sufficiency rule (independent-test count, witness authority, or probability threshold).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We therefore need Satisfied(K,r,EC) which may invoke the appropriate reasoning model. For example Satisfied(K,r,EC)=RuleEngine(K,r,EC) or =StatisticalCriterion(K,r,EC) or =HumanAuthorization(K,r). This is another reason Zero must not contain one universal inference mechanism.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the satisfaction predicate Satisfied(K,r,EC) as potentially delegating to RuleEngine, StatisticalCriterion, or HumanAuthorization — reinforcing that Zero must not embed one universal inference mechanism.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero should not calculate everything itself. Instead: Zero -> RequirementEvaluation -> AppropriateReasoningModel. ... Zero aggregates the results.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Zero as an orchestrator that dispatches requirement evaluation to the appropriate reasoning model (Rules/Statistics/Authority) and aggregates results, rather than being an inference engine itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Operational Zero: Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) where W* is the target world state. Epistemic Zero: Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC) where K*_EC is the knowledge required by the epistemic contract. These are fundamentally different.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally splits Operational Zero Z_W=Distance(W_t,W*) from Epistemic Zero Z_K=Distance(K_t,K*_EC), reaffirming the two are fundamentally different quantities.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Target: Nexus Pro running in target environment. Current world: Nexus OSS 3.69 running. Operational gap: Z_W>0. But suppose Target architecture known, Current version known, Backup status unknown, Firewall status unknown, Approval missing. Then Z_K>0. Even if an engineer knows exactly how to perform
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing Z_K (epistemic gap) can independently block execution even when the operational how-to is fully known, illustrating Z_W and Z_K as genuinely separate blocking gaps.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I recommend Zero=(Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision) at the conceptual level. Z_world: What differs in reality? Z_knowledge: What required facts are unknown/uncertain? Z_governance: What required approvals/rules are missing? Z_decision: What prevents a defensible decision? This is much
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes Zero into four conceptual dimensions (Z_world, Z_knowledge, Z_governance, Z_decision), each answering a distinct question, stronger than a single scalar distance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Z_knowledge=5 and Z_governance=1. Can we say Zero=6? No. The six missing items are not necessarily comparable. One missing governance approval could be more blocking than five low-priority informational gaps. Therefore Zero is primarily a structured object, not a scalar.
b_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample against summing dimension counts into a scalar Zero=6: a single governance gap can outweigh five informational gaps in blocking severity, so Zero must remain primarily a structured object, not a scalar.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Once the structured Zero exists, we may calculate: GapCount. Or CriticalGapCount. Or WeightedGapScore. Or ContractCoverage. For example Coverage(K) = satisfied required conditions / total required conditions. But these are projections of Zero, not Zero itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines four derivable scalar projections of the structured Zero object (GapCount, CriticalGapCount, WeightedGapScore, ContractCoverage), explicitly distinguished as projections, not Zero itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Each requirement can have Criticality(r) such as {Critical,High,Medium,Low}. But again, we should be careful with arbitrary scores. A critical requirement might be RollbackVerified. If Status=Unknown, then migration could be blocked regardless of all other results. This gives us BlockingCondition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces per-requirement Criticality with a caution against arbitrary scoring, deriving the concept of a BlockingCondition — a single unresolved critical requirement that blocks regardless of all other results.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) extends First-Degree Entailment (FDE / Belnap-Dunn 4-valued logic) to eliminate the structural distinction collapses identified in prior kernel evaluations ... ABK-1 resolves these deficiencies by embedding the standard 4-valued truth space BF_4 into an Annotated Bilattice Frame B_ABK. Each proposition is represented as an annotated truth tuple that pairs an FDE valuation with a justification graph, a temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ABK-1: an architecture that embeds standard 4-valued FDE (BF_4) into an Annotated Bilattice Frame, pairing each proposition's FDE valuation with a justification graph, temporal validity window, and modal/scope metadata, explicitly targeting the lineage/temporal/underdetermined collapses previously measured against bare FDE (this batch's r-req-fde-kernel-test-vectors-result).

a_rows_sample.anchor: State(phi) = <nu(phi), J(phi), tau(phi), mu(phi)> ... FDE Truth Valuation nu in BF_4 ... Justification Graph J = <V_J, E_J, m> ... Temporal Validity Window tau = <t_start, t_end, v_D, TTL> ... Modal and Boundary Metadata mu = <Type, Modality, ScopeMask>
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition of the ABK-1 state 4-tuple State(phi)=<nu,J,tau,mu>: nu is the FDE truth valuation in the powerset of {T,F}; J=<V_J,E_J,m> is a justification DAG (premise nodes, derivation edges, justification mode in {Evidenced,Inferred,Reported,Assumed}); tau=<t_start,t_end,v_D,TTL> is a temporal validity window with a dependency version vector; mu=<Type,Modality,ScopeMask> carries Analytic/Synthetic, Necessary/Contingent, and a scope bitmask.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Order (<=_k): S1 <=_k S2 iff (nu1 subseteq nu2) and (J1 sqsubseteq_DAG J2) ... Truth Order (<=_t): S1 <=_t S2 iff (T in nu1 implies T in nu2) and (F in nu2 implies F in nu1) ... Conjunction (x_t) ... Disjunction (+_t) ... combining FDE valuation, justification-DAG union, temporal intersection, and metadata AND (mu1 (dot) mu2).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ABK-1's algebraic lattice structure over B_ABK = BF_4 x J x T x M: a Knowledge Order (<=_k, comparing valuation-subset and DAG-substructure) and a Truth Order (<=_t, standard FDE truth ordering), plus lattice conjunction and disjunction operators that combine FDE valuations via standard FDE meet/join, union justification DAGs, intersect temporal validity windows, and combine modal metadata via a metadata-AND operator.

type_signature.codomain: boolean order relations, or a combined ABK-1 state

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suite 1.2 Underdetermined vs. Unknown | FAIL | PASS (via J.nodes.length > 0) | PASS ... Suite 2.1 Inferred vs. Assumed | FAIL | PASS (via J.mode) | PASS ... Suite 3.1 Stale vs. Expired | FAIL | PASS (via tau.tEnd and v_D) | PASS ... The Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) achieves a 100% Pass Rate across all Tier P1 and Tier P2 distinction verification suites, qualifying it for ratification as a fully R_req-compliant KnowledgeOS kernel engine.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that ABK-1, re-run against the SPEC-RREQ-TEST-2026-V1 suite, converts all three of the bare-FDE test failures found earlier in this batch (Underdetermined-vs-Unknown via presence of justification-graph nodes; Inferred-vs-Assumed via J.mode; Stale-vs-Expired via temporal window and dependency-version comparison) into PASSes, alongside the two bare-FDE PASSes it retains (Contradiction-vs-Unknown; Absence-vs-Evidence-of-Absence), yielding a claimed 100% pass rate across Tier P1/P2 and a recommendation to ratify ABK-1 as R_req-compliant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export class ABKState { public val: FDEValue; public justification: JustificationGraph; public temporal: TemporalWindow; public metadata: ModalMetadata; ... resolveKnowledgeStatus(currentTime, upstreamVersions): KnowledgeStatus { if (this.resolveCurrency(...) === 'Expired') return 'NotAssessed'; switch(this.val) { case 'B': return 'Contradictory'; ... case 'N': { if (this.justification.nodes.length > 0) return 'Underdetermined'; return 'Unknown'; } } }
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a full TypeScript reference implementation of ABK-1: an ABKState class carrying val/justification/temporal/metadata fields with resolveKnowledgeStatus (currency-checks first, then value-switches, distinguishing Underdetermined from Unknown by non-empty justification nodes), resolveCurrency (Expired if past tEnd, Stale if any dependency version has advanced, else Current), and resolveJustificationMode methods; and an ABKAlgebra class with a hard-coded FDE conjunction truth table and a meet() operation merging justification DAGs (node/edge union), temporal windows (intersection), and metadata (conjunctive AND, scope-mask bitwise AND).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architectural Specification: ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Interface (ABK-CONTR-INT-v1) ... The Contr Isolation Module operates directly on top of the Annotated Bilattice Kernel (ABK-1) to handle non-explosion, contradiction trap frames, and resolution state tracking for paraconsistent evaluations. ... When an inbound assertion or lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu(phi)=B), the ABK-1 engine delegates contradiction containment to ABKContrBridge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a bridge architecture (SPEC-ABK-CONTR-2026-V1) between ABK-1 and a Contr contradiction-isolation engine: whenever an ABK-1 lattice operation produces a contradictory valuation (nu=B), the engine delegates containment to an ABKContrBridge that traps the state in a local frame, sets ResolutionStatus=Unresolved, and initializes an evidential polarity edge graph, ensuring downstream inference cannot propagate the contradiction beyond a bounded contextual scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: export interface IABKContrBridge { shouldIsolate(state): boolean; isolateContradiction(...): ContrIsolationPayload; updateResolutionStatus(...): ContradictionTrapFrame; evaluateResolution(frameId): ABKState; } ... evaluateResolution ... if (totalWeight > 0.5) { resolvedVal='T'; resolution='Resolved'; } else if (totalWeight < -0.5) { resolvedVal='F'; resolution='Resolved'; } else { resolvedVal='B'; resolution='Irresolvable'; }
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the IABKContrBridge TypeScript interface (shouldIsolate, isolateContradiction, updateResolutionStatus, evaluateResolution) and its ABKContrBridge implementation: contradiction resolution sums signed evidential-polarity weights across conflicting sources and resolves to True (Resolved) if the sum exceeds +0.5, False (Resolved) if below -0.5, or remains contradictory (Irresolvable) if the weights are near-balanced -- a simple threshold-based weighted-voting resolution rule for the contradiction lifecycle.

type_signature.domain: a contradiction trap frame with polarity-weighted evidence edges
type_signature.codomain: a resolved (or still-contradictory) ABKState plus a ResolutionStatus

a_rows_sample.anchor: describe('ABK-1 / Contr Bridge Integration Suite' ... it('should detect contradictory valuations (B) and trigger isolation' ... it('should mark frame as Irresolvable when evidence weights cancel out' ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Provides a runnable Jest end-to-end integration test suite (abk-contr-integration.test.ts) covering contradiction detection and trap-frame creation, non-explosion verification (an isolated contradictory proposition does not pollute an unrelated proposition's algebra), and resolution-lifecycle management (transition through InProgress/Resolved, resolving to True when positive evidence dominates, and remaining Irresolvable when weights cancel).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Documents: RREQ-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-1-SPEC-v1.0, ABK-CONTR-v1.0 ... The Governing Insight: R_req is the semantic contract. ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle. ABK-1 achieves 100% compliance across all Tier P1 and P2 distinctions. The Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executive summary frames the package's governing insight: R_req is the semantic contract, ABK-1 is the implementation vehicle achieving claimed 100% compliance across Tier P1/P2, and the Contr Bridge provides non-explosive contradiction isolation -- packaging three previously-separate documents (R_req, ABK-1, ABK-Contr) plus a test-verification document for joint ratification.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 5.2 What Remains OPEN: Contr Now has a concrete implementation path via ABK-1/Contr Bridge; Zero Now has formal definition via R_req compliance; delta Still open -- ABK-1 provides state representation but not transition semantics; Equality Still open -- D-1.4 provides identity distinctions but not full equality semantics; Kernel Selection Now has a candidate (ABK-1) that is R_req-compliant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the open-items status but with softer framing than the ratification-package file: Contr and Zero are treated as no longer fully open (Contr 'now has a concrete implementation path', Zero 'now has formal definition via R_req compliance'), delta and Equality remain explicitly open (delta lacks transition semantics over ABK-1 states; Equality's D-1.4 lacks full equality semantics), and Kernel Selection is reframed from BLOCKED to 'now has a candidate (ABK-1) that is R_req-compliant' -- a softer status than the immediately preceding file's BLOCKED classification for the same item.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evaluation: the tuple is promising, but not yet proven ... nu positive/negative standing Strong candidate; J justification/lineage Strong candidate; tau temporal qualification Candidate; mu modal/context scope Candidate; Product tuple as the canonical EVal OPEN. EVal != just a tuple of everything useful. We need to prove that each component is semantically necessary for the declared evaluation questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Grades each component of the proposed EVal=<nu,J,tau,mu> tuple by separate epistemic status: nu (strong candidate), J (strong candidate), tau (candidate), mu (candidate), with the product tuple itself as the canonical EVal rated OPEN; states EVal is not merely a tuple of everything useful -- each component must be shown semantically necessary for the declared evaluation questions, or the exercise degenerates into constructing a database schema rather than deriving a kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 6 test cases (R-INV-01 through R-INV-06), each a Python function asserting the corresponding distinction is preserved (e.g. test_R_INV_01_standing_distinction asserts standing.S_plus != standing.S_minus and 'Failed R-INV-01: Standing collapsed to net scalar'; test_R_INV_03_state_distinction asserts eval_contr.state != eval_unknown.state) ... ABK-1 Compliance Status: 6/6 Tests Passed implies Adequacy(R_ABK-1, R_req) = 1.0
a_rows_sample.statement: SPEC-TEST-ABK1-2026-v1.0 provides a six-test Python compliance suite (one per R-INV, each with a test fixture using Context/Provenance/agent-id objects), reporting the ABK-1 representation passes all six (6/6), concluding Adequacy(R_ABK-1, R_req)=1.0 -- notably applying the SPEC-R-REQ-2026-v1.0 six-invariant taxonomy (Standing/Boundary/State/Provenance/Temporal/Reasoning) to the SAME ABK-1 architecture that earlier in this batch was tested and rated compliant against a different, D-1.x-numbered R_req taxonomy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ABK-1 -- representation candidate can be closed ... this does not prove: 'ABK-1 is the KnowledgeOS kernel.' It proves only: ABK-1 is adequate for the tested R_req. So: ABK-1 representation: CLOSED as a validated candidate. ABK-1 kernel: NOT CLOSED. This distinction is extremely important.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the scope of ABK-1's six-test PASS result: it proves ABK-1 is adequate for the TESTED R_req distinctions, not that 'ABK-1 is the KnowledgeOS kernel' -- ABK-1-as-representation is CLOSED as a validated candidate, but ABK-1-as-kernel remains NOT CLOSED, a distinction judged extremely important.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is one additional missing bridge ... Adequacy -> Executability ... we need one more formal relation: ExecutableAdequacy. EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) meaning: the representation and operations together can answer the required questions while preserving every required distinction and producing an auditable transition. This is the real bridge from representation theory to kernel theory. Without it, ABK-1 can be perfectly adequate as a representation while still being insufficient as a kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Executable Adequacy EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) as a proposed missing formal relation between representation-adequacy theory and kernel theory: the representation K and operations O together must be able to answer the required questions Q while preserving every required distinction AND producing an auditable transition; without EA, a representation (e.g. ABK-1) could be perfectly Adequate(R,Q,Gamma) while still being insufficient as a kernel.

type_signature.domain: (representation K, operations O, question Q, context Gamma)

a_rows_sample.anchor: C1 Required Distinction Framework: CLOSED (with wording correction) R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D, not 'the non-negotiable subset of distinctions required by the system kernel' ... C2 Representation Adequacy: CLOSED ... C3 ABK-1 as Representation Candidate: CLOSED (as candidate, not kernel) ... C4 Non-Explosion Principle: CLOSED (principle only).
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally records four items as CLOSED (no further action needed): the Required Distinction Framework R_req (with the earlier circularity wording corrected to R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D), Representation Adequacy (Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq Preserved(R,Gamma)), ABK-1 as a validated representation candidate (explicitly not as the kernel), and the Non-Explosion principle (as a principle only, not its exact isolation-boundary algorithm).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The ABK-1 '100% proof' is not actually a proof ... 6/6 tests passed implies Adequacy=1.0. That implication does not follow. Six tests demonstrate: adequate on six tested scenarios. They do not establish: forall x in R_req, Preserve(x). And the supplied tests are pseudocode against a hypothetical KnowledgeOSKernel, not evidence of an executed implementation. Therefore replace Adequacy=1.0 with: ABK1 passed all declared tests in the tested scope, and Adequacy_tested(ABK1,R_test)=1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a statistical/mathematical fallacy in ABK-1's compliance claim: '6 of 6 tests passed implies Adequacy(R_ABK-1,R_req)=1.0' is an invalid generalization from finitely-tested scenarios to a universal quantifier over all of R_req; additionally notes the supplied tests are pseudocode against a hypothetical KnowledgeOSKernel class, not results from an executed implementation. Proposes the defensible replacement Adequacy_tested(ABK1,R_test)=1, explicitly scoped to the tested distinction set R_test rather than claiming universal Adequacy=1.0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **What evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the distinctions the KnowledgeOS programme has already declared important?**
b_rows_sample.statement: W-KR-CONTR-2026-09 reframes the Contr question from 'three vs four values' to the deeper question of what evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the programme's already-declared-important distinctions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: * Candidate A — fourth value: **7/12** * Candidate B — delegation: **7/12** * Candidate C — exclusive construction: **7/12** * Candidate D — structured evaluation: **12/12**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the core scoring result: A/B/C each pass only 7/12 required distinctions, failing on the identical seven; D (structured evaluation) passes all 12. The seven common failures collapse the unknown family (Unobservable≡InsufficientEvidence≡Underdetermined≡TheoryIncomplete≡...→U), meaning adding a contradiction value does not address distinctions lying outside the contradiction dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\chi(G)=3.
$$... **Given this particular required-distinction set and this adequacy criterion, at least three distinguishable flat classes are required.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\min |\text{representation}|=2
$$

with the two minimum representations: $$
\{\text{value},\text{reason}\}
$$

and $$
\{\text{polarity},\text{reason}\}.
$$

And: **reason is indispensable.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The exhaustive minimum-representation search finds min|representation|=2, with two minimum representations {value,reason} and {polarity,reason}, establishing that reason is indispensable -- evaluation outcome is not value alone, EVal=(v,r) is the minimum representation found in the tested search space, kept explicitly [EXP]/[PROP] not a new KnowledgeOS primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate C maps contradiction to `T`. Yet it passes invariants I1–I5. Why? Because those invariants test contradiction against the **unknown family**, rather than against satisfaction itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate C (exclusive construction) maps Contradiction to T (Satisfied) yet passes invariants I1-I5, because those invariants only test Contr≠Unknown-family, not Contr≠Satisfied -- exposing a genuine coverage gap in the invariant suite itself, not merely a bad candidate; proposes I11: Contr≠Satisfied as a legitimate but not-yet-ratified [PROP] test-protocol addition, explicitly preserving the historical conflict (I1-I5 pass, capability guard fails) rather than retroactively declaring the suite complete.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
### R_A

The first implementation unfairly returned `T` for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases... ### E7

The literal `"C"` detector accidentally matched context identifiers such as `C1/C2`.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records two implementation self-corrections during the experiment: R_A, an initial implementation unfairly returned T for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases, corrected so all nine no-determinate-value conditions return U; E7, a literal 'C' contradiction detector accidentally matched context identifiers like C1/C2, corrected -- both classified as test-implementation defects, not candidate properties, caught by investigating rather than forcing expected results (E9).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **The experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar evaluation value. The tested adequacy requirement is satisfied by a structured representation in which at least one reason-like dimension is indispensable. The precise evaluation semantics, including the role of contradiction, remains OPEN.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the accepted formulation of the current Contr finding: the experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar value; a structured representation with an indispensable reason-like dimension satisfies the tested adequacy requirement; the precise evaluation semantics including contradiction's role remains OPEN -- explicitly weaker and safer than 'structured evaluation is the answer', since D is the surviving candidate, not yet the final theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AuthoritativeKnowledge → Provenance; CurrentKnowledge → Validity; Inference ≠ Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Knowledge as BC candidate 1: strong semantics (knowledge object, claim, source, provenance, validity, version, supersession, authoritative/inferred state), strong invariants (AuthoritativeKnowledge->Provenance, CurrentKnowledge->Validity, Inference≠Authority), a lifecycle Observed->Imported->Proposed->Verified->Approved->Authoritative->Superseded, but an unresolved ownership question — since ArchitectureKnowledge and OperationalKnowledge may have different owners, 'Knowledge' may be a domain concept rather than one BC; verdict: Strong Candidate, ConfirmedBC=NotYetEstablished.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence → Provenance; Evidence → Producer; Verification → Evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Evidence as BC candidate 2: strong identity (answers 'what supports this claim'), invariants (Evidence->Provenance, Evidence->Producer, Verification->Evidence; historical evidence must not silently disappear), lifecycle Generated->Captured->Validated->Associated->Retained->Superseded/Expired; notes Evidence is consumed by nearly everything (Knowledge/Governance/Assurance/Agents) but high consumption does not itself imply a separate BC — whether it owns an independent consistency boundary remains open; verdict: Strong Candidate, ConfirmedBC=Unknown.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision → Authority; Authority → Scope; Decision → Validity; Exception → Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Governance as BC candidate 3: very strong DDD characteristics — distinct language (policy, authority, decision, approval, delegation, exception, escalation, effective date, supersession), strong invariants, a coherent lifecycle Request->Assessment->Review->Decision->Approval->Effective->Superseded, and likely organizational ownership (GovernanceAuthority belongs to defined roles/bodies) — stronger evidence than mere tables; verdict: Very Strong BC Candidate, potentially Confirmed once ownership/implementation boundaries verified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verification → Rule; Verification → Evidence; DeterministicCheck → ReproducibleResult.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Assurance as BC candidate 4: own language (rule, check, verifier, test, result, evidence, conformance, violation, verification), purpose DetermineConformance, lifecycle Rule->Check->Execution->Result->Evidence->Finding->Verification (noting Finding could belong to Assurance or Governance depending on ownership); distinguishes Assurance ≠ Governance via example 'dependency violates architecture rule' — Assurance determines Violation=True, Governance determines what to do about it; verdict: Strong BC Candidate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EngineeringState = Supporting Domain, not necessarily BC
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Engineering State (candidate 5: runtime/deployment/implementation state/infrastructure/observations/actions) as problematic because it belongs to many external systems (Git, Kubernetes, Nexus, CI/CD, Monitoring) — KnowledgeOS likely consumes rather than owns it, potentially owning only ObservationRecord/EvidenceReference; verdict: Supporting Domain, not necessarily BC, explicitly to prevent KnowledgeOS becoming an accidental replacement for Git/Kubernetes/monitoring.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentInteraction = Supporting Context
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Agent Interaction (candidate 6: agent, session, task, tool, recommendation, execution, delegation) asking whether this is KnowledgeOS domain semantics or AI infrastructure; concludes AgentIdentity may belong to KnowledgeOS-facing integration while PromptManagement belongs to the agent harness; verdict: Supporting Context, not a core KnowledgeOS bounded context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Policy = What must/should happen; Decision = What was decided in a particular case.
b_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes Policy (candidate 7: rules, constraints, applicability, scope, exceptions, effective dates) distinguishing Policy (what must/should happen) from Decision (what was decided in a particular case), Policy->DecisionContext, leaving open whether Policy deserves its own BC independent of GovernanceDecision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A relation always requires: Entity + Property Boundary + Context Boundary + Relation Mode
a_rows_sample.statement: Avacchedaka (the delimitor/scope of a property in Navya-Nyaya) is presented as 'the Missing Type System': a database-style {entity, attribute, value} triple (e.g. {System, Status, Active}) is insufficient because a bare property like 'Active' is meaningless without a bounding context (software lifecycle vs user account vs legal contract vs infrastructure context). b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity_{BC_1}(x) may differ from: Identity_{BC_2}(x). ... The question is not 'What is the one true identity?' The question is: 'Identity according to which domain model?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Identity is context-dependent: the same real-world thing can have distinct identities in different bounded contexts (e.g. a VM in Infrastructure BC, the Nexus service in Application BC, 'Artifact Repository Service' in Business BC), connected by explicit typed relations (Represents, Hosts) rather than collapsed into one universal identity; the migration example (is Nexus_B the same system as Nexus_A?) has no universally correct answer, only a context-dependent one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x\equiv_C y means: x and y are considered the same entity under context C's identity rules. ... Reflexivity ... Symmetry ... Transitivity ... identity equivalence forms equivalence classes.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a per-bounded-context identity equivalence relation x=_C y satisfying reflexivity, symmetry, and transitivity, forming equivalence classes; a reconciliation system producing a contradictory triple (A=B, B=C, A!=C) is an identity consistency violation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I_48: Identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context.
b_rows_sample.statement: New invariant I_48: identity equivalence must be transitive within a defined identity context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(x=y\mid E)=0.98 does not mean: x=y with probability 0.98 in a metaphysical sense. It is an epistemic assessment.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identity reconciliation is itself an epistemic process: an identity assertion x=_C y can carry attached Evidence (migration record, certificate, registry, configuration, ownership, architectural decision), and a probabilistic identity-match score P(x=y|E) is an epistemic confidence, not a metaphysical probability of equality; some domains (e.g. passport numbers under a defined authority) support deterministic identity instead, so KnowledgeOS should support both deterministic and probabilistic identity assessment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Representation \rightarrow CandidateMatch \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow IdentityAssessment \rightarrow IdentityDetermination. This is structurally identical to the epistemic pipeline we derived earlier.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an identity-resolution pipeline structurally identical to the earlier general epistemic pipeline, taken as a sign of architectural coherence; an AI's identity claim ('these two repositories are the same system') should initially be a CandidateIdentityClaim requiring evidence, never an automatic silent merge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DomainEntityIdentity \neq AggregateBoundary. An entity can participate in relationships with entities outside its aggregate.
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD safeguard: an aggregate root must have a domain identity and its invariants apply within that identity's boundary, but Identity does not dictate the TransactionBoundary -- an aggregate must not automatically absorb every representation of the same real-world thing, and identity does not equal aggregate boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I_51: Domain identity must be defined by domain semantics, not inferred solely from technical representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: New broader invariant I_51: domain identity must be defined by domain semantics, never inferred solely from technical representation -- summarizing the chapter's central DDD argument.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Communication is two capabilities wearing one name. C-10 Knowledge Distribution -- a genuine, evidenced, unowned MECHANISM ... C-19 Communication Composition -- a STEWARDSHIP
a_rows_sample.statement: 'Communication' as commonly discussed is proposed to be two distinct capabilities: C-10 Knowledge Distribution (a genuine unowned mechanism, evidenced by EKS-01) and C-19 Communication Composition (a stewardship, failing the bounded-context test on language and reason-to-change); a single 'Communication Engineer' role would wrongly bind a mechanism gap and a reporting duty into one actor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: fails on 6 of 10 => a STEWARDSHIP / cross-cutting expression concern ... the only state that could make a Communication context real -- delivery-with-acknowledgement -- is C-10's receipt, not C-19's. building C-10 would REDUCE the case for a Communication context.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-19 fails a ten-part bounded-context test on six of ten criteria (own language, independent lifecycle, independent authority, authoritative state, distinct reason to change, audience/consent/channel concepts) and is classified a stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern; the one property that could give it authoritative state (delivery-with-acknowledgement) actually belongs to C-10, so realizing C-10 reduces rather than increases the case for a Communication bounded context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD does not define a bounded context by noun category or organizational role ... Communication becomes a bounded context when it has its own domain language ... a reason to evolve separately.
a_rows_sample.statement: Challenges creating a Communication bounded context merely because a Communication Engineer role exists; a Communication context is defensible only if messages/audiences/consent/delivery/retention carry independent domain invariants and lifecycle, not merely presentation/rendering.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four unowned capabilities (corrected state)
a_rows_sample.statement: Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). Flagged as a proposal finding, not adopted architecture; C-10/C-14 existence remain UNDECIDED.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
b_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-ATTR-2/G-2: separation is Declared, NOT attestable. No mechanism can establish who performed an act; assurance rests entirely on where the human starts the session.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One process occupied verification -> architecture-review -> architecture-drafting -> domain roles in sequence, and in each lane recorded its own START -- a governance act -- because no separate governance process was present
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the C-14 correction moved onto the C-5 row while C-14 still displayed the falsified "absent / NO OWNER" ... shared the look-alike cell ... and the first match was C-5.
b_rows_sample.statement: Correction #2 (finding W-2) discovers the Amendment 1 pointer correcting C-14's status was applied by a scripted first-match string replace and accidentally landed on the C-5 row instead, because both capabilities shared an identical look-alike table cell -- and it proposes extending the existing 'no automated search-and-replace on source code' rule's scope to any artifact with look-alike sites.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence of a C-5-owned aggregate may disqualify a separate bounded context but must NOT be used as proof that the capability itself does not exist.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refinement applied to C-5: absence of a C-5-owned authoritative aggregate/state disqualifies it from being its own bounded context but must not be read as evidence against the capability's existence -- an existence/category conflation the original analysis had committed for C-14 most clearly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not treat organizational independence as established in a single-operator environment. ... Single-operator constraint -- six separations, distinguished explicitly: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, external attestation.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-5's separation dimensions must distinguish six kinds: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, and external attestation; organizational independence must never be treated as established in a single-operator environment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Material participation in producing the evidence being verified? YES, and this is decisive ... my Verification #2 findings W-1...W-6 fed the correction chain that runs into this artifact's lineage
b_rows_sample.statement: An independence gate is extended beyond mere non-authorship to material participation: a verifier whose own prior findings materially shaped a later correction chain is disqualified from verifying that chain's output, even without direct authorship of the artifact under review.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a unifying invariant candidate falls out of it: both control-plane capabilities are defeated by the SAME failure -- self-assertion by the gated party. C-5 is defeated by self-declared separation; C-14 by self-declared compliance.
b_rows_sample.statement: A unifying control-plane invariant candidate (proposed, not adopted): a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party the gate constrains; observed support: G-1 already enforces this for closure, and CAP-09's write-paths are deliberately closed, so the invariant is already implemented twice but never stated as a general rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
b_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

b_rows_sample.anchor: organizational independence NOT_ESTABLISHED (not NOT_APPLICABLE) ... in a single-operator environment organizational independence is not among the achievable separations, and it MUST NOT be represented as established.
b_rows_sample.statement: A four-state model for separation dimensions is adopted (NOT_APPLICABLE, NOT_ESTABLISHED, ESTABLISHED, EXTERNALLY_ATTESTED); organizational independence is corrected from the original 'not applicable / undefined' to NOT_ESTABLISHED, because NOT_APPLICABLE risks collapsing into PASS while NOT_ESTABLISHED correctly states a real, currently unsuppliable assurance gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: intra-platform third-party != external attestation ... A different process under the same operator, on the same filesystem -- that is evidence of process separation, not of externality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Correction #3 adds external attestation as a sixth separation dimension at NOT_ESTABLISHED, and sharpens the distinction that a different process under the same operator establishing a fact (as Verification #3 did for SB-1) is process separation, never external attestation -- no party outside the platform has attested any separation claim in this estate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is C-5 -- separation attestation -- failing in production, on the very work item that is analysing it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding I-2, an explicit analogy: the estate's identity-attribution mechanism has produced both a false negative and a false positive on the same question within one day, on the exact work item studying separation attestation (C-5) -- framed as C-5 failing in production, recorded as evidence, with no ownership or OQ-A conclusion drawn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Producing a fresh analysis would create a second, competing C-5 model -- while the first is mid-verification (S5 ACTIVE, outstanding). That forks the subject under assurance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Search-before-modelling (ES-005.4) applied concretely: a commission to define C-5 fresh is refused because a 922-line canonical analysis already treats C-5 across four sections, and producing a competing model while the canonical one is mid-verification would fork the subject under active assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If I author this analysis I become a producer on the item I govern ... C-5 operating correctly forbids its own analysis being written by the party that governs the record it rests on. This refusal is itself C-5 evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential separation argument: Governance for the work item refuses to author a C-5 analysis because doing so would make it a producer on the item it governs -- the exact shape of defect §4 of the provenance reconciliation had just recorded -- and the refusal is offered as a third, live instance of C-5 evidence on the very work item studying C-5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLASSIFICATION: HISTORICAL VERIFICATION EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT / PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED ... ca6039a8 is neither deleted nor rewritten. Its substantive findings F-1...F-7 were separately adopted as verified findings by PO/ARB act and are not disturbed by this classification
b_rows_sample.statement: A defective-provenance classification vocabulary is introduced: an artifact can be classified HISTORICAL EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT while its substantive content (findings) remains adopted and undisturbed -- only the assurance/independence claim is refused, not the content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ca6039a8 was reclassified as HISTORICAL EVIDENCE + NOT INDEPENDENT/PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED -- not deleted, findings intact, only its ASSURANCE STATUS refused. That is exactly the shape of receipt invalidation ... invalidation is PURPOSE-SCOPED, not global.
b_rows_sample.statement: The earlier reclassification of the AMD2 verification artifact (ca6039a8) as historical-but-not-independent is offered as a real, worked instance of what 'receipt invalidation' should look like: invalidation is purpose-scoped (it removes assurance standing while leaving the content usable as evidence), not a global deletion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not import C-5's existence test automatically. Do not assume 'adopted invariant + performed capability' is a universal rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: The two-limb existence test derived from C-5's evidence (adopted invariant + performed capability) is explicitly declared not a universal rule to be imported automatically for other capabilities; C-10 must construct its own establishment test rather than inherit C-5's.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 4 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Theory 13 §1: 'KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier. Every result was produced on r=(value,source,tag,time) with |D|<=6.' Measured against the code, both halves of that sentence need correction. 'no declared carrier' -> THREE code estates run on three declared carriers ... The carrier is not missing. It exists twice, in two shapes, and Theory 13 UNDERSTATES the one it names. OQ-1 is therefore a RECONCILE-or-RATIFY decision, not a choose-from-nothing decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects Theory 13's claim of 'no declared mathematical carrier' by measuring code estates that actually run on declared carriers, reframing OQ-1 from a choose-from-nothing decision into a reconcile-or-ratify decision over carriers that already exist and already run experiments.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Carrier A -- the zero-algebra estate: verification/zero-algebra/, 59 .py, 53 .json, 50 .md, 22 experiment directories. @dataclass Item: token, source, uncertainty, scope, polarity, node, edge_to (7 fields). @dataclass Rep: cls (R1|R2|R3|R4), items. Carrier A = Rep=(cls,(Item_1,...,Item_n)), Item has 7 fields. And it is a LADDER, not a single level: R1 token only (old generator violated its own R1 declaration in 40.2% of cases), R2 token+within-case rank in {1,2,3}, R3 token+2-significant-digit value (rounding creates ties; ranks cannot), R4 fuller representation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Carrier A precisely from verbatim code: a Rep(cls, Item-tuple) with a 7-field Item dataclass, organized as an R1-R4 representation ladder (token-only through fuller representation), noting the old generator itself violated its R1 declaration in 40.2% of cases.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Consequence already proven on this carrier: E_S(D) = D\S is invalid at R2 -- removing an item from a rank vector leaves ranks {2,3}, which is not a valid rank vector. Set subtraction is not the elimination primitive. (PROGRAMME-STATUS-2026-09-03, Correction 1.) What runs on it: the Zero, representation-reduction, bridge and zoom families -- the [EXP] results Theory 13 describes, including the three separations, FR-001, and the 2026-09-07 finding that Zero is not an element property.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates a previously-proven consequence specific to Carrier A: plain set subtraction E_S(D)=D\S is invalid at level R2 because removing an item from a rank vector produces an invalid rank vector, confirming set subtraction is not the correct elimination primitive; lists the whole Zero/reduction/bridge/zoom experimental family, including this same batch's OQ-4 witness finding, as running on Carrier A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Carrier B -- the v1.2 simulation estate: research/knowledgeos-sim/, 55 .py, 109 .json, verified to run this session. No single record type. Per-concern frozen dataclasses: EVal(value,reason,evaluator,dependencies,contradiction,provenance_state,temporal_state,operational_state,theory_status,domain_restricted,trace); Arg(id,rel [a typed relation, not a signed scalar],weight,source,derived_from,about); State(args,hypotheses,admissible,truth [truth=ORACLE ONLY]); Boundary(kind,cls,reason,remediable_by,blocking); plus Situation/ActionTheory/World/Regime for the Reiter/multiplicity/distinguishability families.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Carrier B as a set of per-concern typed dataclasses (EVal, Arg, State, Boundary, plus Situation/ActionTheory/World/Regime) rather than a single record type, explicitly noting Arg.rel is a typed relation (not a signed scalar) and State.truth is oracle-only.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Field frequency across the estate: provenance 41, source 37, context 28, time 27, status 23, content 19, evidence 14, value 10. That field set is 37's structured epistemic object k=(id,content,context,evidence,provenance,uncertainty,status) -- the correction the corpus made to itself on 2026-09-01, already implemented in code on 2026-09-02. Carrier B is not a proposal; it is running. What runs on it: the 26 named v1.2 experiments -- Sat, Zero readings, factivity, Contr/FDE, closure, history, multiplicity, N_eff, distinguishability, Hilbert, composition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Measures Carrier B's actual field frequency across the codebase and shows it matches a previously-recorded structured epistemic object k=(id,content,context,evidence,provenance,uncertainty,status) from a 2026-09-01 self-correction, demonstrating that correction was already implemented in code by 2026-09-02 rather than remaining a proposal; lists 26 named v1.2 experiments running on Carrier B.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The one seam -- and it is narrow: Carrier A (Rep(cls,Item...), a REPRESENTATION being transformed/reduced) feeds Carrier B (EVal/Arg/State, an EVALUATION over content, with reasons) -- the seam: what does an evaluator receive? Carries a REASON? Carrier A: no. Carrier B: yes -- reason, remediable_by, trace. The seam is the reason channel. Carrier A can say WHAT was removed. Only Carrier B can say WHY.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the single narrow seam between Carrier A and Carrier B as a pipeline relationship (A produces representations, B evaluates them) whose only missing link is a 'reason channel': Carrier A can state what was removed but has no field for why, while Carrier B carries reason/remediable_by/trace.

a_rows_sample.anchor: And that is the same channel three independent results demanded: KR-CONTR-FDE's two boundary collapses ('Standing has no channel for why') · KR-CONTR-EVAL's theorem that no flat domain of any cardinality is adequate and the minimum is a pair with an indispensable reason/boundary component · and Boundary.remediable_by itself. A carrier decision that keeps A and B separate must declare the seam's contract. A carrier decision that unifies them must give Rep a reason channel. Those are the two shapes of OQ-1, and this paper does not choose between them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the reason-channel seam is independently corroborated by three separate prior results (KR-CONTR-FDE's boundary collapses, KR-CONTR-EVAL's minimum-adequate-domain theorem, and Boundary.remediable_by itself), and frames OQ-1 as reducing to exactly two shapes: declare the seam contract (keep A/B separate) or add a reason channel to Rep (unify them), without choosing between them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Carriers DEFINED but carrying no executed result (10-row table): KS=(X,A) measurable epistemic state space, 20 files, none executed; K=(A,R) the verification lane's kernel, 98 files, kos_kernel.py 29 experiments -- executed; ratified K_t over 8 primitives, 41 files, no code; K_t=(A_t,E_t,R_t,C_t,H_t,Gamma_t) 6 fields, 7 files, none; Theory-01 D,T,R,Q,Pi,O,C,E_S, 121 files, = Carrier A's vocabulary -- executed; Sigma 5-axis 2240 states, 112 files, partly executed, 0 of 5 axes ordered; D_t varying dimension set, 18 files, none, population rule blocked; G_t=(V,E,Phi) attributed multigraph, 5 files, none, its convergence theorem found invalid; h_Lambda=(H,R_sem,Lambda,Sigma_Lambda) FR-001's [PROP] successor, 7 files, none; Hilbert-space representation KR-HILBERT, 37 files, negative result (PARTIALLY CONFIRMED weakest sense, H1/H3/H7/H8 refuted). Ten candidates. THREE carry executed results. Two of those three are Carriers A and B.
a_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates ten total carrier candidates found across the corpus, of which only three carry any executed result (K=(A,R)/Carrier A's kernel, Theory-01's vocabulary matching Carrier A, and the negative Hilbert-space result), with the ratified K_t itself among the seven with no executed result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What each existing result would inherit: ratify Carrier A inherits the whole Zero/reduction/bridge/zoom family, orphans the v1.2 evaluation family's reason channel; ratify Carrier B inherits the 26 v1.2 experiments, orphans the reduction ladder (R2's proven E_S!=\ has nowhere to live); ratify both and declare the seam inherits everything currently executed, nothing orphaned but the seam contract becomes a new obligation; ratify KS=(X,A) inherits a clean measure-theoretic frame but orphans every executed result since no code runs on it; ratify the 8 primitives as the carrier inherits the ratified surface and C-022's 50 attack classes -- CORRECTED 2026-09-07, '0 lines of code' is WITHDRAWN, verification/**/exec/ (54 .py, 5723 LOC) implements class K, Assertion, Proposition, Observation, Evidence -- the ratified vocabulary IS implemented, orphaning only the two experimental families.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the full inheritance/orphaning consequences of five possible carrier decisions, with an explicit same-day withdrawal of the '0 lines of code' claim about the ratified-8-primitives option once verification/**/exec/ was measured (54 .py, 5723 LOC implementing class K, Assertion, Proposition, Observation, Evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: |D|<=6 is a DESIGN BOUND, not a property. Theory 13 §OQ-6 says so of eliminability, and the results record n_cases=1200 per family at that bound. Any carrier ratified today inherits the bound as a scope limit, and OQ-3 (transfer) is the only thing that lifts it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that the |D|<=6 domain-size figure is a design bound (matching the recorded n_cases=1200 per family), not an inherent property of any carrier, and that only the separate OQ-3 (transfer) decision can lift this scope limit.

Correction of record, 2026-09-07: Building the OQ-4 witness required reading KR-REP-REDUCTION's carrier.py, which shows Rec(v,s,t,rank) -- the record Theory 13's r=(value,source,tag,time) paraphrases. §0's second row is corrected above. This paper's conclusion is unaffected -- two implemented carriers, OQ-1 is reconcile-or-ratify -- and it gains a finding: the zero-algebra estate is itself not single-carriered.
a_rows_sample.statement: Records an in-place same-day correction made while building the OQ-4 witness experiment (S2871-S2874): the exact record Theory 13 paraphrased as r=(value,source,tag,time) is identified as KR-REP-REDUCTION's Rec(v,s,t,rank), and the zero-algebra estate itself is found to run on at least two distinct record types (Item in KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA, Rec in KR-REP-REDUCTION), a new finding this paper's original two-carrier conclusion did not anticipate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What this paper does not do: does not recommend a carrier -- OQ-1 is a governance decision and 'no experiment can decide it'; does not claim Carriers A and B are equivalent -- §3 states the seam and leaves it open; does not resolve whether Theory 13's r=(value,source,tag,time) is a simplification or a reference to code I did not find. a_rows_sample.statement: States three explicit non-actions of this paper: no carrier recommendation, no claimed A/B equivalence, and no resolution of whether Theory 13's exact 4-tuple wording is simplification or an undiscovered reference -- recorded as a discrepancy for governance rather than an error.

b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that the three-way script distinction (K-script/K-blackboard/plain-K) among the nine ranked definitions is itself undeclared, so any governance ruling must name the specific script to avoid leaving the referent ambiguous.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q3: two seams, and only two: A<->B, what does an evaluator receive from a representation? -- the reason channel -- A says what was removed, only B says why; demanded independently by KR-CONTR-FDE's two boundary collapses and KR-CONTR-EVAL's 'no flat domain of any cardinality is adequate; the minimum is a pair with an indispensable reason component.' C<->(A,B): is K=(A,R) the state that A's representations represent and B's evaluations evaluate? (A,R)=_semantic pi_K(K_t) -- lossy, definable-not-computable; replay/policy-eval/authorize unanswerable in (A,R). A ratification that names a carrier and leaves these two seams undeclared produces a formally ratified carrier whose relationship to every executed result is unstated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies exactly two seam contracts requiring explicit declaration regardless of which carrier arrangement is chosen: the A<->B 'reason channel' seam (evaluators need why, not just what, per two independently-demanded findings) and the C<->(A,B) projection seam ((A,R)=_semantic pi_K(K_t), a lossy, definable-but-not-computable projection under which replay/policy-eval/authorize are unanswerable); warns that leaving either seam undeclared produces a ratified carrier disconnected from its own executed results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q4 -- not decided: kernel selection (O_core present in 51% of 66 worlds; any minimality claim inherits a coin flip; both registers put selection last); O_core (NOT FROZEN, membership rule absent); Theory v1.3 (governance order is EXPERIMENT->AUDIT->ADJUDICATION->v1.3, adjudication has not happened); OQ-2/DECISION-02 (a separate decision, gates composition and delta, not the carrier); the five conflict records (Contr, >=, delta, ≡_sem, Qualify); any new algebra (negative results; Zero is not an element property); Gita candidacy (closed, Theory 13 §6); every glyph collision (explicitly out of scope per Governance -- only the carrier vocabulary and citations needed to identify the ratified object; the remaining ~45 definitions across 15 glyphs are a subsequent normalization task, H1).
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates eight items OQ-1 must explicitly NOT decide (kernel selection, O_core freezing, Theory v1.3, OQ-2/DECISION-02, five named conflict records, any new algebra, Gita candidacy, and the broader glyph-collision normalization task H1), each with the reason it must not ride along with the carrier decision, so the decision cannot silently widen its scope.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What the decision needs to state, minimally: 1. the carrier arrangement (Q1); 2. one canonical referent for K, with the script named, and each of the other eight mapped to retained/historical/local/rejected (Q2); 3. the two seam contracts, or an explicit statement that they remain open and results are cited as scope-bound until declared (Q3); 4. the non-decisions (Q4), so OQ-1 cannot become a kernel-selection exercise.
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the four minimal elements any OQ-1 governance decision must state: the chosen carrier arrangement, one canonical scripted K referent with the other eight classified, disposition of the two seam contracts (or explicit deferral), and the non-decision boundary.

V2 is frozen. It ran on Carrier A at R5 and is scope-bound to it; it is listed under Q1's inheritance for Carrier A only, which is a fact about where it ran, not an argument for ratifying A.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly disclaims recommending Q1, assigning Q2 status, or declaring a seam, and clarifies that the OQ-4/V2 witness experiment (S2871-S2874 in this same batch) is scope-bound to Carrier A and its listing under Carrier A's inheritance is a factual note about where it ran, never an argument in favor of ratifying Carrier A.

Ten candidates. THREE carry executed results. Two of those three are Carriers A and B.
