a_rows_sample.anchor: S_t = (K_t, U_t, X_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, P_t, G_t) ... G_t = (Z_t, L_t, d_t, a_t) ... This is the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Complete System State as a nine-tuple including Knowledge, Understanding, Domain, Ideal, Inquiry, Context, Knower, Policy, and a Guidance State G_t bundling Zero findings, Lord candidates, distance vectors, and the last Sarathi recommendation into the persistent state itself, then declares this the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do Not Put Guidance Into the Fundamental State... Z_t=Zero(S_t), L_t=Lord(S_t,Z_t), a_t=Sarathi(S_t,Z_t,L_t) are derived outputs. If we put them back into the state, we create S_t -> G_t -> S_t and risk a circular definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects embedding the Guidance State (Zero/Lord/Sarathi outputs) inside the persistent System State as a circular definition (state depends on guidance which depends on state); replaces it with a strict functional layering State->Analysis->Guidance, where analysis and guidance are pure projections over state, never stored as state fields unless explicitly persisted as an independent domain object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Complete' Does Not Mean 'Everything'... the minimum sufficient state required to determine the system's valid future behavior under the defined transition semantics. If two histories produce the same S_t and the same relevant transition semantics, then they are operationally equivalent from that point onward.
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines 'Complete System State' away from 'everything KnowledgeOS could possibly know' toward a precise systems-theoretic notion: the minimum sufficient information to determine the system's valid future behavior, with the corollary that two histories yielding the same S_t under the same transition semantics are operationally equivalent going forward.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N_t should not be 'The human Knower'... may be a person, a team, an organization, an authorized role, an institution... Identity != Values != Authority != Preferences.
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes the Knower (N_t) from 'the human Knower with identity, values, and preferences' to an Epistemic Actor that may be a person, team, organization, authorized role, or institution, further decomposing Identity, Values, Authority and Preferences as four distinct properties that must not be collapsed into one primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ideal State Does Not Automatically Evolve... The system should not autonomously revise the Ideal State merely because new knowledge appears... Discovery may motivate Ideal revision but Discovery not=> Ideal revision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the deterministic Ideal-State evolution equation I_{t+1}=Revision(I_t,K_t,U_t,X_t,N_t) as too permissive at the system-state level (it would let the system autonomously mutate its own evaluation target from new knowledge alone); replaces it with I_{t+1}=ReviseIdeal(I_t,r_t) requiring an explicitly authorized revision event r_t -- Discovery may motivate but never automatically implies an Ideal-State revision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Context / Evaluation Context / Inquiry Context / Guidance Context / Governance Context ... This prevents the entire KnowledgeOS model from becoming one giant aggregate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Produces a five-bounded-context DDD partition of the entire KnowledgeOS model (Knowledge Context: Observation/Proposition/Assertion/Evidence/EpistemicState/KnowledgeState; Evaluation Context: IdealState/Gap/Conflict/Discrepancy/Coherence; Inquiry Context: Question/Purpose/Intent/Context; Guidance Context: Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Candidate/Recommendation; Governance Context: Policy/Authorization/Decision), explicitly to prevent the entire theory collapsing into one undifferentiated aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would not yet say that Q20 gives the 'complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS.' ... What we have after Q20 is better described as: the core formal state-and-transition model of KnowledgeOS. There are still important formal questions around priority, action selection, decision theory, observability, provenance, temporal semantics, identity/authority, policy semantics, and convergence/stability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the document's closing claim to have produced 'the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS', downgrading it to 'the core formal state-and-transition model', and enumerates nine still-open formal areas (priority, action selection, decision theory, observability, provenance, temporal semantics, identity/authority, policy semantics, convergence/stability) left unresolved at the end of this 20-question investigation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State -> Comparison -> Discrepancy -> Diagnosis -> Possibility -> Guidance -> Decision -> Transition. This is the complete formal model of KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the final synthesized eight-stage KnowledgeOS architecture chain (State -> Comparison -> Discrepancy -> Diagnosis -> Possibility -> Guidance -> Decision -> Transition) as the closing formulation of this entire 20-question phase_measure_theory investigation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question subset-of Inquiry. ... Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma): target, purpose, context, requirements, adequacy rules.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Inquiry as a first-class epistemic object distinct from a linguistic question (a question is one possible surface representation of an inquiry): Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma), specifying what must be determined (target), why (purpose), under what circumstances (context), what constitutes an adequate answer (requirements), and adequacy constraints (Gamma) -- an epistemic demand rather than a sentence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: World -> Information -> Knowledge (bottom-up) and Inquiry -> Requirements -> Investigation (top-down) ... Inquiry -> Required Knowledge -> Investigation -> Knowledge -> Answer.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the whole KnowledgeOS system as a duality of a bottom-up direction (World->Information->Knowledge) and a top-down direction (Inquiry->Requirements->Investigation), closing the loop as Client->Inquiry->InquirySpecification->RequiredKnowledge->Investigation->Evidence->InformationState->SemanticRepresentation->K_t->Zero->Determination, with K_t+Inquiry->Answer->SmallestAdequateAnswer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q -> I_Q. The inquiry determines what knowledge would be sufficient. ... The Ideal State is therefore inquiry-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Makes the Ideal State inquiry-relative rather than a free-floating construct: I_Q=IdealState(Q), derived from a specific inquiry (e.g. a migration-feasibility inquiry generates I_Q={OS,CPU,RAM,storage,network,ports,DNS,certificates,backup,dependencies,repository-compatibility,security} rather than requiring all possible knowledge about the observation).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) ... Zero=0 does not mean we know everything. It means we know enough for this inquiry.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Zero to Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC), i.e. whether the current Knowledge State satisfies the epistemic requirements generated by a SPECIFIC inquiry, explicitly correcting the interpretation of Zero=0 from 'we know everything' to 'we know enough for this inquiry.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_Q* = argmin_{A in A(Q,K_t)} Complexity(A) subject to Adequate(A,Q)=true.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Smallest Adequate Answer A_Q* as the minimum-complexity candidate answer, drawn from the set of candidate answers derivable from K_t for inquiry Q, subject to satisfying an Adequate(A,Q) predicate (conjunction of target/evidence/certainty/context/provenance/decision-condition satisfaction, left as unresolved research work); explicitly distinguishes this from ordinary summarization since the inquiry, not linguistic brevity, determines what may be discarded (a 500-word answer can be more minimal than a 20-word one that omits a required qualification).

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t^* = smallest sufficient representation ... A_Q^* = smallest sufficient answer. They are not the same thing. We could have K_t = very large while A_Q^* = very small.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes two independent minimization problems -- knowledge-representation minimization (K_t*, the smallest sufficient internal representation) versus answer minimization (A_Q*, the smallest sufficient externally-given answer) -- which can diverge arbitrarily, illustrated with a worked example where full server knowledge collapses to a single-value answer ('RHEL 9.8') for a narrow inquiry.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_Q in {Determined, PartiallyDetermined, Undetermined, Conflicting, NotApplicable, Unknown} ... Migration cannot yet be determined. The missing information is the firewall configuration for the Nexus host.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the smallest adequate answer may legitimately be an epistemic negative drawn from the corpus's existing status vocabulary (Determined/PartiallyDetermined/Undetermined/Conflicting/NotApplicable/Unknown) rather than a completion, worked through a migration-feasibility example where only firewall configuration is missing: the correct smallest-adequate-answer names the specific missing item rather than answering 'yes' -- explicitly preferable to hallucinating a completion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inquiry therefore controls investigation ... only g3 affects the answer. Then investigating g1,g2,g4,g5 is unnecessary. ... d_Q* = argmax_d [adequacy improvement for Q | investigate(d)] / Cost(d)
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives Inquiry an investigation-control role: rather than closing all gaps in G_Q, KnowledgeOS should investigate only the subset that affects the answer to the current inquiry, formalized as an inquiry-relative dimension-discovery objective d_Q*=argmax_d [E(adequacy improvement for Q | investigate d)]/Cost(d), refining the earlier inquiry-agnostic dimension-discovery objective from a prior file in this arc.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stop iff Adequacy(A_Q,Q), or internally Stop iff Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC)=0. ... Without Inquiry, the system has no principled reason to stop learning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies Inquiry as supplying KnowledgeOS's principled stopping condition for investigation/learning (Stop iff the current answer is adequate for the inquiry, or equivalently Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC)=0), noting that without an inquiry there is always more information to gather and no principled reason to halt.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inquiry defines the destination. Knowledge State defines what has been established. Zero identifies what is still missing. Investigation reduces the relevant gap. Answer is the smallest adequate projection of the resulting knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes with a five-line summary framing the whole architecture around two boundaries -- the Knowledge boundary (what can currently be known/determined, K_t) and the Inquiry boundary (what needs to be known, Q/I_Q) -- with Zero as the gap between them, and Answer as the minimal projection of adequate knowledge onto the inquiry; connects Dretske's semantic-selection chain and Cover-Thomas's sufficiency/distortion apparatus as the mathematical foundations for, respectively, what content matters and how much of it must be preserved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_Q* = argmin_A Complexity(A) s.t. Adequate(A,Q) is becoming a natural synthesis. ... their structures converge on the same design question.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the 'smallest adequate answer' concept is a natural synthesis point where Cover-Thomas (minimal sufficient representation), Dretske (relevant semantic selection), Gita (discrimination between what is rightly understood and what is not) and KnowledgeOS all converge on the same underlying design question, without any source stating the formula A_Q*=argmin Complexity(A) s.t. Adequate(A,Q) itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inquiry is not simply collecting random new information. It is a deliberate attempt to obtain particular information in response to a particular question or gap in existing knowledge. ... Knowledge acquisition is therefore recursive. You use existing knowledge to search for new knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinforces Inquiry as deliberate and question-driven (not random information gathering), and adds that inquiry is recursive -- framing a question requires prior beliefs about what the question means, what counts as an answer, what terms mean, and what counts as relevant evidence, so K_t is used to search for K_{t+1}.

b_aliases: Inquiry as the missing top-level entry point

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'inquiry-first-class-object-and-smallest-adequate-answer' POSSIBLY relates to 'complete-system-state-formalization' (batch B0056). Note: Introduces Inquiry as a first-class KnowledgeOS object distinct from a linguistic question (Question subset-of Inquiry): Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma) -- target, purpose, context, requirements, adequacy rules -- specifying an epistemic demand rather than a sentence. Reframes the whole system around a duality of bottom-up (World->Information->Knowledge) and top-down (Inquiry->Requirements->Investigation) directions, closing the loop Inquiry->RequiredKnowledge->Investigation->Knowledge->Answer. Makes the Ideal State INQUIRY-RELATIVE (Q->I_Q=IdealState(Q), not a free-floating construct) and refines Zero to Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC) meaning 'we know enough for THIS inquiry', not 'we know everything.' Defines a Smallest Adequate Answer A_Q*=argmin_{A in candidate-answers(Q,K_t)} Complexity(A) subject to Adequate(A,Q)=true, where Adequate is a conjunction of target/evidence/certainty/context/provenance/decision-condition satisfaction (predicate left as research work); explicitly separates two distinct minimization problems -- knowledge-representation minimization (K_t*) versus answer minimization (A_Q*), which can diverge arbitrarily (large K_t, tiny A_Q*). Establishes that the smallest adequate answer may legitimately be an epistemic negative (Determined/PartiallyDetermined/Undetermined/Conflicting/NotApplicable/Unknown), explicitly preferable to hallucinating a completion (worked example: a migration-feasibility inquiry with only firewall configuration missing should answer 'migration cannot yet be determined; missing firewall configuration', not 'yes'). Uses this to give Inquiry an investigation-control role (search only for gaps that affect THIS inquiry's answer, an inquiry-relative dimension-discovery objective d_Q*=argmax_d [adequacy-improvement-for-Q | investigate(d)]/Cost(d)) and a principled stopping condition (Stop iff Zero(K_t,I_Q,EC)=0), addressing the 'when does the system stop learning' problem. Distinguishes answer minimality as semantic (inquiry-determined relevance), not merely linguistic compression (a 500-word answer can be more minimal than a 20-word one that omits a required qualification). Connects to Dretske's semantic-selection chain (Information->SemanticContent->InquiryRelevance->Knowledge->Answer) and to Cover-Thomas's sufficiency/distortion apparatus (Inquiry->relevance->sufficiency->minimal representation) as the mathematical foundation for the compression step. Concludes with a five-line summary framing: Inquiry defines the destination; Knowledge State defines what has been established; Zero identifies what is missing; Investigation reduces the relevant gap; Answer is the minimal adequate projection of knowledge onto the inquiry. Possibly a re-derivation of the corpus's much earlier Inquiry-as-first-class-object proposals (inquiry-question-layer-refinement B0011, inquiry-context-doubt-to-settlement B0012, the Q_t component of complete-system-state-formalization B0019) rather than a genuinely new discovery -- not reconciled against those within this batch.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Computable ≠ Implementable in principle but Computable = effective, typed, terminating procedure with defined semantics. It also explicitly forbids calling something computable merely because a program could approximate it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Precise computability criterion: a predicate/function/relation/operation is computable only if it is an effective, typed, terminating procedure with defined semantics (defined inputs/types, termination, deterministic result; for transformations, also a defined domain and codomain) — explicitly distinct from and stronger than mere in-principle implementability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Class A — directly computable ... Class B — computable only after semantic parameters are supplied ... Class C — not computable as currently defined ... Authoritative(x) Relevant(x) Correct(x) Adequate(x) when no operational decision procedure or authoritative source is defined.
a_rows_sample.statement: The theory's predicates/operations are sorted into three computability classes: Class A directly computable (structural parsing, identifier lookup, hashing, canonical serialization, deterministic transformation on fixed inputs), Class B computable only once semantic parameters are supplied (ValidOperation(D,o) needs a scale/type registry; Resolve(pi) needs a provenance registry), and Class C not computable as currently defined (Authoritative(x), Relevant(x), Correct(x), Adequate(x) — predicates with no operational decision procedure, exposing hidden human judgment).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity membership = UNDER-SPECIFIED unless an explicit ontology/registration boundary is introduced. ... Entity definition is conceptually clear but Entity membership is not universally decidable. ... Dimension: StructuralValidDimension(D) is computable ... but Structural validity ≠ Semantic adequac
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-object computability audit for Entity, Dimension, Value and Proposition: Entity's semantic definition ('subject of knowledge') is conceptually clear but membership is not universally decidable without an explicit ontology/registration boundary; Dimension's structural validity is computable but semantic adequacy is not; Value membership is computable only where its value space V_D has an effective representation, ranging from trivially decidable (finite sets) through grammar-parseable (formal version strings) to fundamentally undecidable (open-ended conceptual domains); Proposition well-formedness is therefore CONDITIONALLY COMPUTABLE, contingent on all three membership predicates being computable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralValidation(A) can be computable, while Truth(A) cannot be assumed computable. ... Finite Status Algebra ⇒ Computable transition validation. But that does not make the assignment of the status computable. ... TransitionValidity ≠ StatusAssignment. This is one of the most important hidden bo
a_rows_sample.statement: Two of the audit's sharpest distinctions: (1) an Assertion's structural validation is computable while its Truth is not assumed computable; (2) given a finite epistemic-status algebra, mechanically validating whether a status TRANSITION is legal is computable, but this does NOT make the ASSIGNMENT of a status to an assertion (whether evidence actually warrants that status) computable — TransitionValidity != StatusAssignment is named one of the most important hidden boundaries in the whole theory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: StructuralEquality = COMPUTABLE under canonical representation. ... SemanticEquality = CONDITIONAL not universally established [3m/300cm needs unit normalization; conceptual entities may need an ontology/identity registry]. ... IdentityConstruction can be computable, while IdentityResolution may rem
a_rows_sample.statement: Equality, identity, and provenance are each split into a computable mechanical half and a conditional/non-computable semantic half: structural equality is computable via canonicalization+hashing while semantic equality is only conditionally computable (domain-dependent, e.g. unit normalization for 3m vs 300cm); identity CONSTRUCTION (deterministic hashing of canonical data) is computable while identity RESOLUTION (whether two independently-supplied references denote the same real-world entity) may remain externally supplied or human-governed; provenance-reference LOOKUP is computable under three infrastructure assumptions, but this never establishes ProvenanceTruth — lookup is not validation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay = Conditionally Computable [K0 persisted; every Ti defined; every input available; operation versions fixed; preconditions satisfied; operations deterministic]. ... Replayability ⇒ Immutable or versioned transformation semantics. ... Replay ≠ Reversal. Replay means reconstructing the forward
a_rows_sample.statement: Replay is conditionally computable under six named preconditions, and is proven to REQUIRE operation versioning (since changing an operation's semantics between (T1^2026) and (T1^2027) could replay the same history to different states, replayability implies immutable-or-versioned transformation semantics); Replay is also proven distinct from Reversal — if T is many-to-one (K1!=K2 but T(K1)=T(K2)), no inverse can uniquely reconstruct the original state, so Replay only reconstructs the forward computation, it does not recover an original state from an output.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K* = coarsest sufficient state abstraction. But can we compute K*? In general, this is not automatically decidable. ... Minimality = NOT YET COMPUTABLY ESTABLISHED. This is not a defect in the theory. It is a correct research status. ... TestMinimal(K) [testing removals can discover counterexamples]
a_rows_sample.statement: Minimality (computing the coarsest sufficient K*) is found NOT YET COMPUTABLY ESTABLISHED, explicitly classified as a correct research status rather than a defect, requiring five unmet conditions (candidate abstraction, complete operation set, defined equivalence relation, sufficiency proof, strict-reduction-breaks-sufficiency proof); a further distinction is drawn between TestMinimal(K) (removal testing, which can find counterexamples) and ProveMinimal(K) (a full proof), since finite removal testing can never prove no future operation will require a removed component — empirical minimality evidence is not a mathematical minimality proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Governance decision = possibly non-computable input. ... Evidence handling is computable in layers [Retrieve(e), Hash(e), Link(A,e) computable; Assess(e,A) may require a human or statistical model]. ... StatisticalFormula ≠ ComputableKnowledgeOSQuantity ... Probability claims = UNDER-SPECIFIED unles
a_rows_sample.statement: Policy/authority, evidence, statistics and uncertainty are each shown to contain a non-computable normative core: Authorize(actor,action,policy) is decidable only if policy is fully formalized as rules, otherwise it is a possibly non-computable governance-decision input; evidence handling is computable in layers (retrieval/hashing/linkage computable, but Assess(e,A) may require a human or statistical model); a statistical formula's mere existence (e.g. Bayes' rule) does not make a KnowledgeOS quantity computable — a probability claim is UNDER-SPECIFIED without an explicit probability space (Omega,F,P); and Uncertainty is not computable until its semantics are fixed, since a bare number like U(A)=0.2 could mean probability, confidence, epistemic strength, error bound, entropy, or subjective belief — mathematically different things.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Concept | Current computability | Canonical serialization 🟢 ... Authority determination 🔴 unless formalized ... Policy interpretation 🔴 unless formalized ... Truth of arbitrary assertion 🔴 ... Relevance 🔴 ... Correctness 🔴 ... Adequacy 🔴 ... Minimality proof 🔴 ... Uncertainty semantics 🔴 ... Stati
a_rows_sample.statement: A 23-row 'hidden human judgment map' rates every major KnowledgeOS concept's current computability from green (canonical serialization, structural equality, hash identity, registry lookup, finite status membership) through yellow (typed proposition validation, value-space membership, provenance lookup, deterministic replay, transition validation, semantic equality) to red (entity identity resolution, status assignment, evidence assessment, authority determination, policy interpretation, truth, relevance, correctness, adequacy, minimality proof, uncertainty semantics, statistical quantities without a model) — presented as the step's most valuable single output.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL / DETERMINISTIC CORE [typing, identity references, canonicalization, equality, membership, transition validation, replay, hashing] ... EXTERNAL / PARAMETRIC SEMANTICS [policy, evidence, time, provenance store, authority, measurement regime] ... NORMATIVE / ASSESSMENT BOUNDARY [truth assessmen
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-layer architecture is derived from the audit: a FORMAL/DETERMINISTIC CORE (typing, identity references, canonicalization, equality, membership, transition validation, replay, hashing), an EXTERNAL/PARAMETRIC SEMANTICS layer (policy, evidence, time, provenance store, authority, measurement regime), and a NORMATIVE/ASSESSMENT BOUNDARY (truth assessment, relevance, adequacy, authority assignment, epistemic judgment, unresolved statistical assumptions) — explicitly not excluding the bottom layer from KnowledgeOS, only forbidding it from being falsely represented as purely deterministic without an actual decision procedure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ValueObject from DomainDecision from ExternalPolicy from Assessment. A DDD system should not hide a human governance decision inside a method named isValid() if the result actually depends on an unmodeled authority judgment. That would violate the Ubiquitous Language boundary.
a_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation of the three-layer architecture: the domain model must distinguish ValueObject from DomainDecision from ExternalPolicy from Assessment, and must never hide a human governance decision inside an innocuously-named method like isValid() when the result actually depends on unmodeled authority judgment, which would violate the Ubiquitous Language boundary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS can be computationally rigorous without claiming that all knowledge judgment is computable. This is actually stronger than attempting to make everything deterministic. ... ComputableCore ... JudgmentBoundary. The deterministic core can then guarantee: given the same formal inputs, the sa
a_rows_sample.statement: The step's most important finding: KnowledgeOS can be computationally rigorous WITHOUT claiming all knowledge judgment is computable — a stronger, more defensible architecture than attempting universal determinism; the theory should explicitly separate a ComputableCore (guaranteeing the same result from the same formal inputs) from a JudgmentBoundary (guaranteeing only that a decision is recorded, attributed, contextualized, and auditable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate: Computability Boundary Principle. Let T:X×C→Y ... If [effective representations; decidable preconditions; terminating algorithm; deterministic external interfaces] then T is computable relative to C. But if T depends on an undefined judgment predicate J(x), then T is not established as co

b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly acknowledges that the same equality-typing defect just identified and praised in a different artifact (D285-5, reviewed in S2070) was present, unnoticed, in the author's own earlier K-projection claim -- an unusually direct self-audit that validates the general applicability of the equality-typing principle by successfully turning it on its own author.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Every D285 hypothesis must be typed before it can be tested. In particular, an equality-dependent hypothesis must explicitly state which equality relation it uses. b_rows_sample.statement: States and elevates the typing/equality-naming requirement to the status of the single most important methodological finding of the entire Gita-integration effort, generalizing beyond the single artifact (D285-5) where it was first observed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Every future proposition involving state equality, operation equality, transition equality or projection equality must declare its equality relation.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes/elevates the D285-5 equality-typing lesson (delta(K,o1)=delta(K,o2) does not imply o1=o2, meaningful only once an equality relation is named; under structural equality — which includes provenance H(P,e,c,t,Pi) — the antecedent is false, while under semantic equality it is true) into a standing rule: every future proposition involving state/operation/transition/projection equality must declare its equality relation, or the research risks generating technically true but scientifically vacuous propositions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Action and result must remain distinct**, but the non-injectivity claim is only meaningful under a specifically chosen equality/quotient. This is an important methodological correction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Independently confirms the D285-5 equality-typing correction: action and result must remain distinct, but the claim that delta is non-injective is meaningful only under a specifically chosen equality/quotient — called an important methodological correction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Do not ask whether two formulations are "the same" until the equality relation has been specified.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States what is called the most important methodological lesson of the whole D285 package: do not ask whether two formulations are 'the same' until the equality relation has been specified — this principle is claimed to resolve several apparently contradictory D285 findings into a coherent result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Typed result:** `δ(K,o₁) =_semantic δ(K,o₂) ⇏ o₁ = o₂`. **Stating the property without naming the equality makes it vacuous.** ... the Gītā framing — *"do not define the action by its fruit"* — does not by itself supply the qualification. **Philosophy asked the question; the equality typing answered it.**

b_rows_sample.statement: Applies equality-typing discipline to itself: this matrix's comparison relation is only set equality on primitive names (a weak relation) — the 3 'shared' primitives are shared by name only, and conceptual identity between name-sharing primitives is a separate, untested claim; the matrix therefore establishes vocabulary disjointness, not conceptual disjointness.

a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the implicit assumption 'most probable outcome => best action' as mathematically wrong in general, establishing the correct chain Knowledge->Prediction->Consequences->Utility/Risk->Decision, plus a Decision<->ValueOfInformation relationship.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Decision is not inference ... S=\{s_1,\ldots,s_n\} ... A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\} ... decision theory evaluates a\in A under uncertainty about s\in S
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes inference ('what do we believe?') from decision ('what should we do?'), formalizing state space S and action space A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U(a,s) ... EU(a\mid E)=\sum_s P(s\mid E)U(a,s) ... a^*=\arg\max_a EU(a\mid E)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines utility U(a,s), expected utility EU(a|E)=sum_s P(s|E)U(a,s), and the rational-choice rule a*=argmax_a EU(a|E).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(Outage\mid Upgrade)=0.05 ... tells us almost nothing ... U(Upgrade,Outage) and U(DoNothing,Outage) ... the decision emerges from the whole consequence structure
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example/table showing a bare 5% outage probability tells almost nothing about whether to upgrade absent the full action/outcome/consequence structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Risk=Probability ... ExpectedLoss=\sum_s P(s\mid E)L(a,s) ... real risk can involve multiple outcomes; uncertainty intervals; catastrophic tails; irreversibility; regulatory consequences; opportunity costs
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects reducing Risk to Probability, defining ExpectedLoss=sum_s P(s|E)L(a,s) and listing six additional real-risk dimensions beyond a single probability number.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Action A: P(Loss=10000)=0.10 ... Action B: P(Loss=1000000)=0.001 ... same expected loss ... TailRisk is dramatically larger ... ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked tail-risk example: two actions with identical expected loss (1000) but vastly different catastrophic-tail severity may be rationally treated differently — 'ExpectedValue alone may be insufficient'; risk policy must specify how severe/irreversible outcomes are treated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U(\euro x)=\sqrt{x} ... UtilityFunction is a normative choice. KnowledgeOS should not secretly invent one
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes utility functions (e.g. sqrt(x)) can encode risk aversion but are a normative organizational choice that KnowledgeOS must not secretly invent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord may choose between Action and InformationAcquisition ... Option 1 make decision now ... Option 4 ask human expert ... the system therefore performs meta-decision-making
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Lord's role as choosing between Action and InformationAcquisition, worked with a four-option example (decide now, collect observation, run simulation, ask human expert) — 'the system performs meta-decision-making.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: VOI=EU(\text{best decision after information})-EU(\text{best decision now}) ... VOI(E)=E_e[\max_a EU(a\mid E,e)]-\max_a EU(a\mid E) ... one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines Value of Information via two equivalent expressions, called 'one of the most powerful mathematical ideas for the KnowledgeOS architecture.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(Upgrade)=100, EU(DoNothing)=95 ... VOI(Inspection)=20, Cost(Inspection)=5 ... NetVOI=20-5=15>0 ... AcquireInformation is itself the rational action ... gives Zero a mathematical foundation
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: given EU(Upgrade)=100 vs EU(DoNothing)=95, a candidate inspection with VOI=20 and Cost=5 yields NetVOI=15>0, making AcquireInformation itself rational — 'gives Zero a mathematical foundation.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{epistemic} from Zero_{decision} ... a missing fact matters only if resolving it could change something important ... DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines Zero into Zero_epistemic vs Zero_decision: a knowledge gap matters only if resolving it could change something important — DecisionRelevantKnowledgeGap is more important than arbitrary missing information.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Which Linux kernel version is installed on a test server? ... VOI\approx0 ... Lord should do nothing ... prevents KnowledgeOS from endlessly trying to make itself complete
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a genuine knowledge gap with VOI≈0 for the current decision means Lord should take no action — prevents pursuing exhaustive completeness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: should not optimize for CompleteKnowledge. We should optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision ... much more realistic
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle: optimize for SufficientKnowledge for the decision, not CompleteKnowledge — 'both computationally and operationally much more realistic.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: I=\{i_1,\ldots,i_k\} ... ReadConfiguration, AskHumanExpert, RunTest, QueryAPI, RunSimulation ... i^*=\arg\max_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] ... a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes information-gathering actions as a candidate set I with per-action Cost and VOI, giving i*=argmax_i[VOI(i)-Cost(i)] as 'a beautiful mathematical formulation of the Lord loop.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Restart production server to verify configuration ... Risk(Restart)>0 ... NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) ... Lord cannot blindly maximize information
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing an information-gathering action (production restart) can itself carry risk, extending net value to NetValue(i)=VOI(i)-Cost(i)-RiskCost(i) — 'Lord cannot blindly maximize information.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord = selects the next useful action ... Sarathi = determines what decision should be made
b_rows_sample.statement: Opens by distinguishing Lord ('selects the next useful action,' e.g. 'perform a restore test') from Sarathi ('determines what decision should be made,' e.g. migrate/postpone/change plan/stop given resulting knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: D=\{Migrate,Postpone,ChangePlan,Reject\} ... Decision\neq Action
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the decision set D (e.g. {Migrate, Postpone, ChangePlan, Reject}) as distinct from the executable action set A (e.g. a single decision d=Migrate may require several actions {Backup, RestoreTest, FirewallValidation, Approval, Migration}) — Decision ≠ Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Lord: (K,Z,G,C)\rightarrow A ... Sarathi: (K,G,D,C,P)\rightarrow d
b_rows_sample.statement: States the precise operator distinction: Lord: (K,Z,G,C)->A (chooses what to do next to advance the process); Sarathi: (K,G,D,C,P)->d (chooses which decision is justified given current knowledge and decision model P).

type_signature.domain: KnowledgeState x Goal x DecisionSet x Constraints x Policy

b_rows_sample.anchor: Consequences(d_1) ... OutcomeModel(d,K)
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision reasoning requires knowing Consequences(d) (e.g. for d1=Migrate: Success, Failure, DataLoss, Downtime, Rollback), formalized as requiring an OutcomeModel(d,K).

b_rows_sample.anchor: U(Success)=+100, U(Failure)=-50, U(DataLoss)=-1000 ... illustrative only ... must never be invented by the AI and presented as organizational truth
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a utility function U(o) over outcomes with illustrative example values, explicitly warning these numbers 'must never be invented by the AI and presented as organizational truth.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(d\mid K)=\sum_o P(o\mid d,K)U(o) ... d^*=\arg\max_d EU(d\mid K) subject to governance and safety constraints
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines expected utility EU(d|K)=sum_o P(o|d,K)U(o) and d*=argmax_d EU(d|K), explicitly subject to governance and safety constraints — 'a mathematically well-defined decision mechanism.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(o\mid d,K) cannot reasonably be established. We must not invent it ... Preference(d_1,d_2) or Dominates(d_1,d_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: When probability cannot reasonably be established, prohibits inventing it and instead allows qualitative Preference(d1,d2) or Dominates(d1,d2) (e.g. 'if migration is unauthorized, postponement dominates migration' — no probability necessary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Feasible(d,K,C) ... Migrate requires RollbackVerified=True ... Feasible(Migrate)=False ... should not matter how attractive migration appears economically
b_rows_sample.statement: Before utility calculation, Sarathi must determine Feasible(d,K,C); e.g. Migrate requiring RollbackVerified=True is Feasible=False when RollbackVerified=Unknown, regardless of economic attractiveness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Hard constraint C(d)=True ... Preference d_1\succ d_2 ... Constraints filter; Utility/preferences select
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hard constraints (must hold, e.g. ProductionChangeAuthorized) from preferences among permissible decisions (e.g. prefer lower expected downtime): 'Constraints filter; Utility/preferences select.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(Migrate)=95 ... EU(Postpone)=60 ... Authorized(Migrate)=False ... Migrate is eliminated before utility optimization ... Utility cannot override governance
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example showing higher expected utility (Migrate=95 vs Postpone=60) does not matter once Authorized(Migrate)=False eliminates it before optimization — 'Utility cannot override governance.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionModel=(Outcomes,Constraints,Preferences,Utilities,Uncertainty,Policy) ... Sarathi(K,D,DecisionModel)\rightarrow DecisionResult
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-component DecisionModel=(Outcomes, Constraints, Preferences, Utilities, Uncertainty, Policy) and Sarathi(K,D,DecisionModel)->DecisionResult.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision: POSTPONE ... Reason: rollback capability not established ... Blocking requirements: RollbackVerified ... Evidence basis: E17,E22,E31 ... Now the decision is auditable
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked full auditable DecisionResult record for a POSTPONE decision containing reason, blocking requirements, alternative feasibility, evidence basis, decision model version, and authorization status — contrasted with returning a bare 'MIGRATE' label.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionProvenance(d) ... K_t+Contract+Policy+Model+Evidence\rightarrow d ... Decision must be reproducible
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires DecisionProvenance(d) tracing K_t+Contract+Policy+Model+Evidence -> d, so 'Decision must be reproducible.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Decision_t remains associated with K_t ... Decision_{t+1} is calculated from K_{t+1} ... Decision is time-indexed
b_rows_sample.statement: A historical decision (e.g. today's Postpone) must not be rewritten when tomorrow's new evidence would produce Migrate; Decision_t stays tied to K_t, and Decision_{t+1} is separately computed from K_{t+1} — 'Decision is time-indexed.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stability(d,K) as sensitivity to plausible changes in the knowledge state
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines decision Stability(d,K) conceptually as sensitivity to plausible changes in the knowledge state, motivated by the concern that small evidence changes flipping Migrate<->Postpone indicate an unstable decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(Success)=0.91 ... threshold 0.90 ... Migrate ... if a small uncertainty could make P(Success)=0.88 ... DecisionFragility=High
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a decision that barely clears its threshold (P(Success)=0.91 vs threshold 0.90) but could plausibly drop to 0.88 under small uncertainty should be reported as DecisionFragility=High rather than simply 'Migrate.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(Success)\ge\theta ... \theta must come from governance/domain policy. The AI cannot invent it
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes threshold decisions P(Success)>=theta (e.g. theta=0.95: P=0.97=>Migrate, P=0.72=>Postpone), explicitly requiring theta to come from governance/domain policy — 'the AI cannot invent it.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Probability=Unknown ... We should not substitute P=0.5 ... Unknown+CriticalRisk\rightarrow Postpone
b_rows_sample.statement: When P(Success) cannot be estimated, prohibits substituting an arbitrary P=0.5 as 'unjustified'; instead records Probability=Unknown and lets the decision policy handle uncertainty (e.g. Unknown+CriticalRisk -> Postpone).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence of evidence \neq evidence of failure ... Required evidence absent \Rightarrow decision may be blocked
b_rows_sample.statement: States a named KnowledgeOS principle: Absence of evidence ≠ evidence of failure, distinct from Required evidence absent => decision may be blocked — 'these are different.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Risk(d)=P(Loss\mid d,K)\times Impact(Loss) ... only appropriate where the probabilistic model is justified
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Risk (consequences under uncertainty) from Uncertainty (what we do not know), giving a common quantitative formalization Risk(d)=P(Loss|d,K) x Impact(Loss), qualified as appropriate only where the probabilistic model is justified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DerivabilityStatus ... DS(p)\in\{Provable,Refutable,Undecidable,Unestablished\} but these labels must not be confused with truth or epistemic standing. ... The reasoning system itself has a boundary. Representation Limit, Epistemic Access Limit, Formal Derivability Limit. These are different.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces DerivabilityStatus DS_S(p) in {Provable, Refutable, Undecidable, Unestablished} as a dimension independent of truth/epistemic standing, distinct from Unknown_evidence/Unknown_access/Unknown_structural (Williamson); argues the reasoning system itself has a boundary, distinguishing Representation Limit, Epistemic Access Limit, and Formal Derivability Limit as three different limits -- described as probably the biggest missing dimension revealed by Godel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gamma=(S,C,T,P,...) ... Eval_c(K,r,Gamma_1) may differ from Eval_c(K,r,Gamma_2) because S_1\neq S_2. ... TheoryIncomplete \neq SystematicallyUndecidable
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes folding the reasoning system S into the evaluation context Gamma=(S,C,T,P,...), formally justifying context-relative evaluation (Eval_c may differ purely because S differs); also splits 'theory incomplete' into two distinct causes -- merely missing axioms (resolvable by a modest extension S') versus Godel-type structural incompleteness -- giving TheoryIncomplete != SystematicallyUndecidable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVal = (Standing, Boundary, Derivability, Accessibility, Context, Provenance) ... Gods suggests adding DerivabilityStatus as a separate factor. This is not adopted. It is the next representation hypothesis to test.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes extending the running FDE-factor series into a six-factor EVal = (Standing, Boundary, Derivability, Accessibility, Context, Provenance), building on the prior five-factor hypothesis (Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance x Accessibility from S2528) by adding DerivabilityStatus; explicitly 'not adopted', flagged as the next representation hypothesis to test.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Godel does not justify KnowledgeOS = formal system ... Contr = Inconsistency ... Unknown = Undecidable ... Truth = Provability ... Verification = Consistency ... Godel incompleteness = AI limitation. Those would all be category errors.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit rejection list: KnowledgeOS=formal-system, KnowledgeOS=theorem-prover, Contr=Inconsistency, Unknown=Undecidable, Truth=Provability, Verification=Consistency, and 'Godel incompleteness = AI limitation' -- all called category errors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DistributedInconsistency ≠ EpistemicConflict
a_rows_sample.statement: 18.24: a distributed system's temporary State_A≠State_B from replication delay is a technical consistency condition, distinct from an epistemic contradiction where p and ¬p both hold relevant epistemic standing; eventual consistency must never be used as an excuse to erase epistemic conflict, and technical synchronization must not be read as evidence that two propositions are semantically equivalent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Distributed replica divergence is legitimate propagation delay, not corruption; DataConsistency != DecisionSufficiency; domain-specific consistency policy
b_rows_sample.statement: States two nodes with different knowledge (node A has E1, node B has not yet received it) is not automatically corruption -- may simply reflect PropagationDelay>0. Experiment 10: temporary replica divergence yields TemporarilyDifferentViews, not Corruption -- PASS. Requires nodes to track LastUpdated/Staleness so a decision policy can judge sufficiency. Experiment 11: a safety-critical decision requiring Freshness<5min against a 20-min-stale replica is DecisionBlocked -- PASS, giving DataConsistency != DecisionSufficiency (a replica can be internally consistent yet too stale for a given decision). States consistency requirements are domain-specific (e.g. Eventual for EvidenceContext, Strong for AuthorizationContext); experiment 12: applying strong consistency to every operation is OverEngineering with unnecessary performance/availability cost -- explicitly FAIL.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TransactionBoundary≈InvariantBoundary heuristic (oversized-transaction FAIL); saga-like cross-context workflows with partial state
b_rows_sample.statement: States a transaction should normally correspond to an invariant boundary: artifacts A,B,C connected by an invariant belong in one transaction; unconnected D,E may commit independently -- TransactionBoundary ~= InvariantBoundary ('an excellent DDD heuristic', not always exact). Experiment 13: putting the entire KnowledgeOS state into one global transaction yields PoorScalability and BoundedContextViolation -- explicitly FAIL. For cross-context workflows (Decision -> Authorization -> Execution -> Outcome) that cannot share one ACID transaction, requires WorkflowState and compensating actions (saga pattern). Experiment 14: Authorization succeeding while Execution fails correctly records AuthorizationSucceeded / ExecutionFailed as partial workflow state -- PASS, reinforcing Authorization != Execution and Decision != Outcome under distributed execution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ConcurrencyConflict != EpistemicConflict (five distinct causes of differing agent outputs); mandatory KnowledgeSnapshotVersion for reproducibility
b_rows_sample.statement: Two agents concluding P(p)=0.8 vs P(p)=0.6 from the same evidence under different models are both potentially valid; the correct merge preserves both Model_A and Model_B rather than arbitrarily choosing one. Experiment 15: two valid models producing different predictions yields CompetingModelOutputs -- PASS, giving ConcurrencyConflict != EpistemicConflict: agents may differ because they truly conflict, use different models, see different knowledge versions, have different context, or one has additional evidence. Requires every derived artifact to potentially record a KnowledgeSnapshotVersion since agents seeing K^(10) vs K^(12) may legitimately diverge. Experiment 16: a claim generated with no recorded knowledge version becomes irreproducible once the underlying knowledge changes -- ReproducibilityFailure -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI computation as y=f_θ(x,K_t,C); three-way determinism distinction; reproducibility via metadata, not bitwise identity
b_rows_sample.statement: States a prompt alone is insufficient to reproduce an AI result; formalizes Output = f(Prompt, Model, ModelVersion, Tools, KnowledgeSnapshot, Parameters), i.e. y = f_theta(x, K_t, C) (task, model/config, knowledge snapshot, context/tools) -- two executions may differ because any of these differ. Experiment 17: identical prompt but different K_t yields PotentiallyDifferentOutput, 'not necessarily nondeterministic failure' -- PASS. Distinguishes DeterministicAlgorithm, DeterministicExecution, and ReproducibleResult as three non-identical notions: a probabilistic model (P(Y|X)>0 for multiple outputs) can still be approximately reproduced by recording model version, parameters, seed where supported, input, tool results, and knowledge snapshot. Experiment 18: running an identical task twice with complete execution metadata improves reproducibility without requiring bitwise-identical output for all AI systems -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS concurrency model (Versioned State + Concurrent Events + Semantic Merge + Invariant Validation); five new invariants
b_rows_sample.statement: Formulates KnowledgeOS = Versioned State + Concurrent Events + Semantic Merge + Invariant Validation, 'more appropriate than simply Database+Locks'. Adds five invariants: I_Concurrency (concurrent operations must not silently destroy valid epistemic information); I_ConcurrentConflict (concurrent contradictory updates become explicitly represented conflicts or are resolved by explicit domain policy); I_Version (derived artifacts retain the relevant knowledge and model versions used to produce them); I_Freshness (decisions requiring fresh knowledge must evaluate freshness explicitly); I_Order (receipt order must not be silently treated as causal order).
