a_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization boundary. This lane is not authorized to canonize a KnowledgeOS kernel. No result below may be promoted to invariant, theorem, ADR or standard by this document.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's binding authorization boundary: it is explicitly research-only, not authorized to canonize a kernel, and no result may be promoted to invariant/theorem/ADR/standard by the document itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What this experiment is NOT: a naming exercise ... a retrofit of the current architecture: Part XXIV "existing class != domain primitive" — no architectural circularity ... a canonization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates six things the experiment explicitly is not (naming exercise, aesthetic minimization, a vote, a universal-necessity proof, an architectural retrofit/circularity, or a canonization), each tied to a concrete safeguard already built into the executed model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They disagree for Select, Discriminate, and Revise. Those disagreements are results, not defects.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports, as an executed finding, that the three distinct necessity notions (empirically necessary, formally necessary via the reach algebra, and DDD-necessary as a distinct domain responsibility) disagree for the operators Select, Discriminate, and Revise, explicitly framing the disagreement itself as a valid experimental result rather than a flaw in the model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment targets B + C. A result that improves A while worsening B/C is reported as a worse result, per the protocol's final principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms semantic minimality (B) and compositional minimality (C) as the experiment's primary targets, with cardinality (A) explicitly subordinate: an improvement in operator count that worsens semantic or compositional minimality is scored as a worse result overall.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Modification M-1 — C25 added [CORPUS]. ... Without C25, C10 is unrealizable in any model where a Verdict requires evidence ... This modification enlarges the required capability set and therefore makes minimization harder, not easier.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a new capability C25 ('admit an observation as evidence under a policy') to the protocol's original 24-item list, justified because the corpus's Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence gap (G1) combined with prior constraint 9 (information != evidence) means no capability in C1-C24 covers the observation-to-evidence transition, making C10 (validate) unrealizable without it -- explicitly noted as making minimization harder, not more convenient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C18 reclassified as NON-DISCRIMINATING [NEG]. ... no operator set can fail C18 in this simulator. ... This is a limitation of the instrument, not a finding about the kernel.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies capability C18 (preserve provenance) as non-discriminating because the reach engine structurally guarantees provenance via its derivation DAG for every artifact regardless of operator set, making it untestable by leave-one-out -- explicitly reported as a limitation of the measuring instrument, not a substantive finding about the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C20 given an explicit failure mode: the system must be able to hold >=2 hypotheses and return an UNDECIDED discrimination. It can then fail by overreach — producing a Determination while unable to represent the alternatives it is determining between.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operationalizes the under-specified capability C20 (support non-identifiability) with a concrete, falsifiable failure mode (overreach: producing a Determination without being able to represent >=2 held alternatives with an UNDECIDED verdict), preventing the capability from being trivially 'supported' by doing nothing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: merge C2 and C3 (meaning + representation) | corpus explicitly separates Observation != Proposition != Knowledge; merging is tested instead as robustness variant V1 ... merge C12 and C13 (determine + select) | different carriers, different inputs (Inquiry vs Objective); tested as V5
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports two considered-and-rejected capability-model modifications (merging meaning-construction with representation; merging determination with action-selection), each rejected on corpus-grounded or type-grounded reasons but retained as explicit robustness variants (V1, V5) to be tested rather than silently discarded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An operator IS its declared set of semantic atoms ... 'redefine Y so that Y also does X' is mechanically detectable — it is a change to Y's atom set, i.e. a change to the model, not a composition within it -> SMUGGLING = TRUE.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the anti-circularity device at the heart of the executed experiment: an operator is identified purely by its declared set of semantic atoms, consulted by the reach engine to the exclusion of operator names, so that redefining one operator to secretly absorb another's function becomes a detectable change to the atom-set model itself (SMUGGLING=TRUE) rather than a legitimate composition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Atoms are deliberately allowed to be shared. A 1:1 operator->atom assignment would make every operator irreducible by construction and the experiment vacuous. Two atoms are shared ... and that sharing is where all the interesting results live.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explains why two atoms (difference-decision, norm-comparison) are deliberately shared between operators rather than assigning each operator a unique atom: a strict 1:1 mapping would make every operator trivially irreducible by construction, rendering the whole ablation experiment vacuous -- the shared atoms are identified as the source of the experiment's most interesting results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Structural concerns (context, time, uncertainty, assumption, provenance, alternatives) are modelled as invariants checked over the reach closure ... not as ownable powers. Making them ownable would have handed one operator a monopoly on, e.g., provenance, and rigged the result.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that structural concerns (context/time/uncertainty/assumptions/provenance/alternatives) are deliberately modelled as invariants checked over the whole reach closure rather than as atoms any single operator could own, to avoid rigging the ablation result by handing one operator an artificial monopoly on a cross-cutting concern.

a_rows_sample.anchor: difference-decision ∈ {Discriminate, DetectGap}; norm-comparison ∈ {DetectGap, Determine}. DetectGap holds no atom exclusively. ... it is the assumption most responsible for the headline result, and it is therefore attacked directly by robustness variant V4.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies DetectGap as the only operator in C0-union-Qualify holding no atom exclusively (both its atoms, difference-decision and norm-comparison, are shared with Discriminate and Determine respectively), flagging this modelling choice as the single assumption most responsible for the experiment's headline redundancy result, and explicitly scheduling it for direct attack under robustness variant V4.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observe | world-contact | the sole channel for empirical content; nothing downstream may create it | STRONG ... Represent | symbolic-encoding | make semantic content manipulable without asserting it | WEAK ... Qualify | evidential-qualification | admit an observation as evidence under a policy | STR
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports the full per-operator contract table (13 C0 operators plus Qualify), each with its claimed atom(s), non-reducible responsibility, and a corpus-support grade from STRONG (Observe, Discriminate-as-family, Validate, Revise, Qualify) through MODERATE (Interpret, Infer, DetectGap, Challenge, Determine) to WEAK (Represent, Hypothesize, Relate, Select).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discriminate and DetectGap are all-zero rows. Neither is required by any capability under leave-one-out, because each covers the other's shared atoms. That is not evidence that the capabilities are unneeded — it is evidence that the operator packaging is redundant.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the experiment's headline finding: Discriminate and DetectGap are both all-zero rows in the leave-one-out operator-capability matrix, since each can cover the other's shared atoms when the other is removed -- explicitly interpreted not as evidence the underlying capabilities are unneeded but as evidence that the CURRENT OPERATOR PACKAGING of those capabilities is redundant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C5 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} both removed | the atom difference-decision. C8 | {Discriminate, DetectGap} or {DetectGap, Determine} removed | difference-decision + norm-comparison. A leave-one-out matrix alone would have declared C5 and C8 unnecessary. They are not.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports that capabilities C5 (discriminate alternatives) and C8 (detect epistemic insufficiency) are all-zero columns under leave-one-out and become irreducible only under pairwise ablation (C5 lost only when both Discriminate and DetectGap are removed together; C8 lost when either {Discriminate,DetectGap} or {DetectGap,Determine} are removed together), concretely demonstrating that a leave-one-out-only analysis would have wrongly certified both capabilities as unnecessary.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A carrier kind is not stamped by the operator that produced it. It is derived from (multiset of input kinds, atoms introduced by this step) -> kind ... Otherwise 'only DetectGap can make a Gap' would be true by fiat and the ablation rigged.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a second anti-circularity device: a derived carrier's kind is determined purely by its input-kind multiset and the atoms introduced, never by which operator produced it, so that any operator set capable of introducing the required atoms over the required inputs can produce a given carrier -- preventing the ablation from being rigged by fiat operator-carrier ownership.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim is producible only via entailment — so its warrant kind is DEDUCTIVE by construction. A Verdict produced by generate-and-test is not a Claim. This is what keeps Infer =?= Validate-compose-Hypothesize an honest question rather than a definitional trick.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes, from the carrier-derivation table's type rules, that a Claim can only be produced via the entailment atom (making its warrant kind deductive by construction) while a Verdict produced by generate-and-test (Hypothesize then Validate) is a structurally different carrier -- keeping the composition question 'is Infer equivalent to Validate composed with Hypothesize' a genuinely open, honest question rather than one settled by definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Verdict requires Evidence. This is where the absence of Qualify from C0 becomes fatal. ... Determination requires both NormDelta (hence IdealState) and Inquiry — encoding prior constraint 5, that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Derives from the type system that a Verdict carrier requires an Evidence input, making the corpus's unimplemented Qualify operator (excluded from C0) fatal to realizing validation without it; separately derives that a Determination carrier requires both a NormDelta (itself requiring IdealState) and an Inquiry, formally encoding the prior constraint that the Ideal State is inquiry-relative directly into the type system rather than merely asserting it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reach(S) = mu A . AMBIENT union {k | exists o in S : k in derive(A, o.atoms)}. Monotone, terminating (finite carrier set), and independent of operator names.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Reach(S) as the least fixpoint (over a finite carrier set, hence terminating and monotone) of applying available operators' atoms to the ambient carriers, with a capability achieved iff its required carrier kinds and atoms are both covered by Reach(S) and the atom pool of S -- the operational definition of formal necessity used throughout the experiment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No helper functions. ... No helper performs the work of a removed operator — a claim that is mechanically checkable, since helpers cannot introduce atoms.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the reach engine's implementation contains only domain-operator applications plus generic data-structure operations (set union, fixpoint computation), with every helper function classified per the protocol's requirement, and that no helper can perform the work of a removed operator because helpers structurally cannot introduce atoms -- making the no-semantic-smuggling guarantee mechanically checkable rather than merely asserted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-1] Knowledge ... $$Knows(s,p,c,t)$$ ... $$Knows(s,p,c,t)\Rightarrow True(p,c,t)$$ ... deliberately stronger and cleaner than defining knowledge as probability, data, evidence or belief.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-1] Knowledge: Knows(s,p,c,t) as a factive epistemic relation between participant s, proposition p, context c and time t, with Knows(s,p,c,t) => True(p,c,t) when the epistemic contract is factive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [AX-1] Category non-collapse: Distinct semantic categories may not be identified merely because one can be represented by another. O!=K, Evidence!=Knowledge, Claim!=Truth, Probability!=Knowledge, Proposal!=Decision, Representation!=Identity.
b_rows_sample.statement: [AX-1] Category non-collapse: distinct semantic categories may not be identified merely because one can be represented by another, giving six named non-collapses: Observation!=Knowledge, Evidence!=Knowledge, Claim!=Truth, Probability!=Knowledge, Proposal!=Decision, Representation!=Identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Domain ontology: $$\mathfrak O=\{W,S,O,E,P,C,Q,K,I,\Delta,Pr,Dc,A,H,EC,R\}$$ ... These are **semantic sorts**, not necessarily database tables or classes.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a sixteen-sort domain ontology (World, participant/knower, observation, evidence, proposition, context, inquiry, knowledge state, ideal state, epistemic gap, proposal, decision, action, history, epistemic contract, representation/regime), explicitly semantic sorts, not database tables or classes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-2] World state: $$W_t\not\equiv O_t$$ ... [DEF-3] Observation: $$O_t^s=Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t)$$ ... Observation != Reality and Observation != Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-2] World state W_t (KnowledgeOS does not require complete access to it, W_t not-equivalent O_t); [DEF-3] Observation O_t^s=Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t) as a method-mediated relation between participant and reality, giving Observation != Reality and Observation != Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-4] Knower: $$F_s=(G_s,C_s,Q_s,EC_s,M_s)$$ ... [AX-2] Knower-frame ownership: $$Frame(K,s)=F_s$$ KnowledgeOS may calculate, extract, compare or propose, but it may not silently redefine: the purpose, context, acceptance criteria, inquiry, or epistemic contract.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-4] Knower: a participant with an epistemic frame F_s=(G_s,C_s,Q_s,EC_s,M_s) (purpose, context, inquiry, epistemic contract, admissible methods); [AX-2] Knower-frame ownership: the frame belongs to the knower or explicitly authorized epistemic authority, and KnowledgeOS may calculate/extract/compare/propose but may never silently redefine the purpose, context, acceptance criteria, inquiry, or epistemic contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-5] Proposition ... Proposition != Claim. [DEF-6] Claim: Claim=(p,c,t,s) ... supported, unsupported, uncertain, challenged, accepted, rejected, superseded. But: Claim != Truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-5] Proposition: semantic content capable of being true or false under an interpretation and context, explicitly Proposition != Claim; [DEF-6] Claim=(p,c,t,s), a proposition presented for epistemic evaluation, admitting seven possible statuses (supported/unsupported/uncertain/challenged/accepted/rejected/superseded), with Claim != Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-7] Evidence ... Supports(e,p) is directional. Therefore: Supports(e,p) not=> Truth(p) and Evidence != Knowledge. ... prov(e)=(source,method,agent,time,context,integrity) ... Knowledge <- Evidence <- Provenance.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-7] Evidence: a directional support relation Supports(e,p) between information and proposition, giving Supports(e,p) does not imply Truth(p) and Evidence != Knowledge; evidence provenance is defined as prov(e)=(source,method,agent,time,context,integrity), giving the dependency chain Knowledge <- Evidence <- Provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-8] Extraction: Extract:E->X ... [DEF-9] Determination: Determine(X,EC)->Status ... [AX-3] Extraction-Determination separation: Extraction != Determination. Therefore an extraction mechanism cannot silently become epistemic authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-8] Extraction: Extract:E->X (retrieves/transforms information from evidence); [DEF-9] Determination: Determine(X,EC)->Status (establishes epistemic status warranted by evidence under standards); [AX-3] Extraction-Determination separation: Extraction != Determination, so an extraction mechanism cannot silently become epistemic authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-10] Knowledge atom: the smallest independently meaningful epistemic assertion that contributes to the semantic state under a declared representation. $$k_i$$ ... Sentence != Dimension != KnowledgeAtom automatically. The semantic independence must be established.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-10] Knowledge atom k_i: the smallest independently meaningful epistemic assertion contributing to the semantic state under a declared representation, defined semantically (since its exact tuple is representation-dependent) rather than syntactically, giving Sentence != Dimension != KnowledgeAtom automatically -- semantic independence must be separately established for any candidate atom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-11] Semantic Knowledge State: $$K_t\in\mathbb K$$ ... We deliberately do **not** initially require: K_t={k_1,...,k_n} nor K_t=(p,e,c,t,...) as a universal implementation tuple. Instead: K = space of admissible semantic epistemic states ... a concrete representation r provides: r(K_t)=x_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-11] Semantic Knowledge State: K_t is an element of an abstract space K of admissible semantic epistemic states, deliberately NOT initially required to be a specific tuple (neither a bare atom-set nor a fixed (p,e,c,t,...) record); a concrete representation r maps it to a carrier value r(K_t)=x_t -- explicitly resolving the earlier conflict between multiple candidate K_t tuples by keeping the type abstract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: v1.0 requires that a sufficiently expressive state preserve at least the following semantic dimensions: $$K_t=(Content_t,Support_t,Uncertainty_t,Model_t,Alternatives_t,History_t,Identity_t,Context_t,Inquiry_t,Status_t)$$ This is a **semantic decomposition**, not a mandatory storage tuple.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that any sufficiently expressive v1.0-conformant state preserve at least ten named semantic dimensions (Content, Support, Uncertainty, Model, Alternatives, History, Identity, Context, Inquiry, Status), explicitly a semantic decomposition (a minimum expressiveness requirement) rather than a mandatory storage tuple.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-12] Knowledge projection: $$K_t^s=Projection_s(W_{\leq t})$$ conceptually. Therefore: K_t != W_t and K_t != CompleteReality.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-12] Knowledge projection: a participant's knowledge state K_t^s is conceptually a bounded projection of accumulated world history K_t^s=Projection_s(W_{<=t}), giving K_t != W_t and K_t != CompleteReality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-13] Semantic Knowledge Space: (K,Sem) is the space of admissible semantic epistemic states. [DEF-14] Representation space: for representation r, (X_r,A_r) is its mathematical carrier. This distinction is crucial. ... [DEF-15] Semantic equivalence: r1=_sem r2 iff [[r1(x)]]=[[r2(y)]] for corresponding semantic states ... r1=_sem r2 iff B_r1=B_r2 over the admissible test domain.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-13] Semantic Knowledge Space (K,Sem) kept distinct from [DEF-14] a specific Representation space (X_r,A_r) for representation r; [DEF-15] Semantic equivalence r1=_sem r2 defined via matching semantic interpretation of corresponding states, or more generally via matching observable behaviour B_r1=B_r2 over the admissible test domain -- explicitly named as the missing concept that explains the 13-vs-8 kernel result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Measurable Knowledge Space = (X,A) and probability is an additional structure. ... [DEF-16] An epistemic observable is a measurable function Y_j:Omega->V_j. ... A = sigma(Y_j: j in J). ... Infinite-dimensional Knowledge Space X=prod X_j, A=bigotimes A_j ... |X|=infinity is **not** a v1.0 axiom. It is an admissible model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Fixes Measurable Knowledge Space = (X,A) != Probability Space; [DEF-16] epistemic observable Y_j:Omega->V_j generating the measurable structure A=sigma(Y_j:j in J); infinite-dimensional Knowledge Space X=product of X_j with product sigma-field, explicitly noted as an ADMISSIBLE MODEL, not a v1.0 axiom (infinite dimensionality is not mandated).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Partial knowledge as a measurable region: cylinder C=A1xA2xA3x(prod j>3 X_j). ... Unknown = Unconstrained in the representation, not a fabricated value. Therefore: Unknown != False != ProbabilityZero. ... [DEF-17] $$\mathcal F_t$$ ... filtration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes partial knowledge as a finite-dimensional cylinder set, giving Unknown=Unconstrained (not a fabricated value) and reinforcing Unknown != False != ProbabilityZero; [DEF-17] epistemic filtration F_t (the sigma-field of all epistemically available measurable information through t), non-decreasing F_0 subset F_1 subset ....

b_rows_sample.anchor: F_t != K_t. F_t describes **available information**. K_t describes **semantic epistemic state**. Hence: $$K_t=\Phi(\mathcal F_t,S_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t,M_t,H_t)$$ for an epistemic determination function Phi. This is a **theoretical construction**, not a theorem that measure theory supplies.
b_rows_sample.statement: States F_t != K_t (available information vs semantic epistemic state) as a formal distinction, with K_t = Phi(F_t,S_t,Q_t,C_t,EC_t,M_t,H_t) for an epistemic determination function Phi explicitly flagged as a theoretical construction, not a theorem measure theory itself supplies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-18] If a target variable X has a probabilistic model: Pi_t=L(X|F_t) ... Pi_t != K_t. ... Epistemic uncertainty: U_t=U(K_t) may use probability, confidence intervals, likelihood, possibility, belief functions, intervals, qualitative states, logical alternatives, evidence strength. Probability subsetneq EpistemicAssessment.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-18] Probability as an optional, regime-dependent conditional law Pi_t=L(X|F_t), explicitly Pi_t != K_t; separately defines a general epistemic uncertainty function U_t=U(K_t) that MAY be realized by probability, confidence intervals, likelihood, possibility, belief functions, intervals, qualitative states, logical alternatives, or evidence strength, giving Probability as a proper subset of EpistemicAssessment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-19] Epistemic requirement: EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t) ... $$\mathbb I(EC_t)=\{K\in\mathbb K: Sat(K,EC_t)\}$$ ... IdealState != AbsoluteKnowledge. It is purpose-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-19] Epistemic requirement: the epistemic contract EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t), used to define the admissible ideal REGION I(EC_t)={K in K : Sat(K,EC_t)} (a set of satisfying states, not one universal ideal state), giving IdealState != AbsoluteKnowledge -- it is purpose-relative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: [DEF-20] Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t). ... [DEF-21] Epistemic Gap: $$\Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)=\{r\in Req(EC_t):\neg Sat(K_t,r)\}.$$ This is the canonical v1.0 definition. Therefore: Delta_t=empty iff Adequate(K_t,EC_t).
b_rows_sample.statement: [DEF-20] Epistemic adequacy Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t); [DEF-21] Epistemic Gap declared as the CANONICAL v1.0 definition: Delta_t=Gap(K_t,EC_t)={r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)}, a requirement-set (not a subtraction of heterogeneous structures), with Delta_t=empty iff Adequate(K_t,EC_t) -- explicitly resolving the earlier mathematically-invalid K_t*-K_t formula.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Typed gap: $$\Delta_t=(\Delta^{content},\Delta^{uncertainty},\Delta^{model},\Delta^{observability},\Delta^{requirement})$$ ... In v1.0 we resolve the conceptual problem by making the **requirement-set representation canonical**, while allowing numerical projections later.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retains the five-component typed-gap vector (content, uncertainty, model, observability, requirement) as an optional further classification, but resolves the underlying representation problem by making the requirement-SET formulation Delta_t subset Req(EC_t) canonical, while allowing numerical projections of it to be defined later as needed.

b_aliases: KnowledgeOS Theory v1.0 -- Formal Definitions, Axioms, Theorems, Corollaries and Architectural Consequences

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 6 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \neq A Single Assertion ... K_t \neq A Set of Assertions ... K_t = A Structured Collection of Assertions + Their Relationships + Their Epistemic Status + Their History ... K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Knowledge State K_t as a 6-component structure: Assertions A_t, Relationships R_t, Evidence E_t, History H_t (all previous Knowledge States), Zero findings Z_t, and Lord candidates L_t; forms a Knowledge Graph G_t=(A_t,R_t) with Assertions as nodes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identical, Equivalent, Consistent, Contradictory, Causal, Temporal, Normative Conflict, Logical Contradiction ... R_j = (A_i, A_k, Type, Strength, Evidence)
a_rows_sample.statement: Types the Relationship edges of the knowledge graph with eight relation kinds spanning both the earlier Compare vocabulary (Identical/Equivalent/Consistent/Contradictory) and the newer conflict taxonomy (Causal, Temporal, Normative Conflict, Logical Contradiction), each carrying Strength and supporting Evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State_t = (K_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) ... I_t = (D_I, V_I, R_I, C_I) ... Compare(K_t, I_t) -> G_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the complete System State as (KnowledgeState,IdealState,Question/Intent,Context), formalizes the Ideal State I_t=(IdealDimensions,IdealValues,IdealRelationships,Constraints), and defines Compare(K_t,I_t)->G_t as the set of gaps between current knowledge and the ideal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Detection: Normative conflict between A_2 and A_3 ... Z_1 = (Normative Conflict, {A_2, A_3}, 'Family duty vs. war duty') ... Resolution... Zero Resolved: Z_1 is resolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traces the full Arjuna example through five knowledge states K_0..K_4, showing a Zero-detected NormativeConflict finding created when the opposing-side assertion is added and resolved once the moral-conflict assertion clarifies the relation between the grandfather and opponent assertions as Compatible rather than contradictory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Knowledge State should probably not be defined as 'everything KnowledgeOS has.' It should be defined as the epistemically structured state relevant to a particular observer, purpose, context and time... K_t = K(X,P,N,C,tau)
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects modelling K_t as an absolute, single global object; since the Observation model already parameterizes on Purpose/Observer/Context/Time, the Knowledge State must be similarly parameterized: K_t=K(X,Purpose,Knower,Context,tau), since two Knowers (Arjuna vs Dhrtarastra) observing the same reality do not share an identical Knowledge State.

type_signature.domain: Reality x Purpose x Knower x Context x Time

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t \supset Z_t but Z_t=Zero(K_t) which means the state contains the output of an operation that operates on the state itself... I would therefore define: K_t = CurrentKnowledgeState and separately H_{0:t}=KnowledgeHistory
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags a definitional circularity in the S0783 Knowledge State: embedding Z_t=Zero(K_t) and H_t={K_0,...,K_t} as components of K_t itself makes K_t contain the output of an operation applied to K_t, and makes each historical K_i recursively contain its own history; proposes separating CurrentKnowledgeState K_t from KnowledgeHistory H_{0:t} and computing Zero(K_t)/Lord(K_t) as derived views rather than stored fields.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion does not simply exist. It applies somewhere... Scope = (Context, Time, Subject, Boundary, ...) This is essential for avoiding false contradictions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Scope as a missing concept an assertion needs (e.g. Nexus.Version=3.69 applies to production but not test; a policy applies to one organization but not another), motivated as necessary to avoid false apparent contradictions between assertions that actually hold in different scopes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State \neq Conflict Free State ... Coherence = all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints ... A Knowledge State may contain unknowns, conflicts, competing interpretations, unresolved questions, normative tensions and still be coherent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Coherence away from 'no contradictions' toward 'all assertions are mutually interpretable under their dimensions, scopes, contexts and temporal constraints', explicitly allowing a coherent Knowledge State to contain unknowns, unresolved normative tensions and competing interpretations without being incoherent -- Knowledge State != Conflict-Free State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question 13: What is the formal structure of the Knowledge State? ... Is Knowledge State a set, graph, typed graph, labelled graph, relational structure, lattice, or some composite algebraic structure?
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses Question 13 as the prerequisite to formalizing distance: K_t must be given an exact formal structure (set/graph/typed-graph/relational-structure/lattice/composite) before any distance/measurement function over it can be mathematically meaningful.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State is the formal, typed, structured representation ... K_t = (A_t, R_t, E_t, H_t, Z_t, L_t, T_t, G_t, C_t, M_t) ... Knowledge State = A Structured Typed Graph with Epistemic Metadata
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a ten-component Knowledge State (Assertions, Relationships, Evidence, History, ZeroFindings, LordCandidates, Temporal structure, Knowledge Graph, Context, Metadata/provenance) formalized as a typed, directed, labelled graph, with immutability of History (new states appended, never overwritten) as a core invariant.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K contains things that are not knowledge ... Zero findings: No. Zero findings are observations about the Knowledge State. Lord candidates: Definitely no. History: Probably not part of the instantaneous Knowledge State. Knowledge Graph: probably a representation of the Knowledge State, not another independent component inside it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the ten-component K_t as a category error: Zero findings and Lord candidates are derived observations/hypotheses about the state, not the state itself; History is a temporal model over states, not a field within one state; the typed graph is a representation/projection of the state, not an ontologically independent component. Proposes a smaller canonical K_t=(Propositions,Assertions,Relationships,Evidence,EpistemicState,Context,Temporal,Provenance) with Z_t=Zero(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), L_t=Lord(K_t,I_t,Q_t,C_t), and H_t=History(K_0,...,K_t) all computed externally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Contained in' is not the right mathematical relation. Entity not-subset Proposition ... use Participates In / Referenced By / Forms instead.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the typed-universe diagram's 'contained in' arrows (Entity/Dimension/Value -> Propositions) which are not subset relations: an entity participates in a proposition, a dimension is referenced by it; recommends participates-in/referenced-by/forms relations instead, consistent with the earlier containment-vs-set-inclusion correction from Question 7.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SystemState_t = (K_t, U_t, X_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, Z_t, L_t, H_t) ... K_t = Knowledge State only
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the complete runtime SystemState as wrapping the (now smaller) Knowledge State K_t together with Understanding U_t, Domain X_t, Ideal I_t, Intent/Question Q_t, Context C_t, Knower N_t, and the derived Z_t/L_t/H_t, cleanly separating what KnowledgeOS knows from what it also tracks about the Knower and the epistemic journey.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Question 14 — What is the Ontology of Knowledge? Is a Proposition a value object? Is an Assertion an entity or value object? Is Evidence itself knowledge? Is a Relationship a proposition? Is an Epistemic State part of an assertion or external? Is a Gap part of knowledge or a finding about knowledge? Is Zero part of the domain model or an operation over it? Is the Knowledge Graph the ontology or merely one representation?
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses Question 14 (Ontology of Knowledge) listing eight unresolved ontological-status questions (Proposition as value object? Assertion entity or value object? Evidence itself knowledge? Relationship a proposition? EpistemicState internal or external to Assertion? Gap knowledge or finding? Zero domain-model or operation? Graph ontology or representation?) to be resolved before implementation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: There is no component of K holding the set of recognised dimensions. ... D_t is the smallest missing component. With it, 'not assessed' is D in D_t AND not exists a in A: a.P.D=D -- decidable in O(n). Without it, the statement has no truth-maker.
a_rows_sample.statement: An executed probe (MISSINGNESS-NOT-ASSESSED in THEORY-CONSTRUCTION-TEST.md) shows a never-assessed dimension and an assessed-with-no-result dimension both render identically in K=(A,R) as 'no assertion mentioning that dimension', proving them provably indistinguishable; introducing D_t (the set of currently recognised dimensions) as a component of K makes 'not assessed' decidable in O(n) and is identified as the smallest missing component to close the missingness gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A construction score is not a proof of adequacy. A scoring exercise establishes RELATIVE rank among the candidates enumerated; it establishes nothing about whether any candidate is sufficient, and it cannot detect a capability that NO candidate was scored on.
a_rows_sample.statement: The claim that K=Set(Assertion) x R is correct because it scored highest (15/19) against six candidates is challenged on methodological grounds: a comparative score establishes only relative rank among enumerated candidates, never absolute sufficiency, and cannot detect capabilities no candidate was scored on -- exactly the three (uncertainty, non-identifiability, missingness) later shown to be missed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K is a representation whose referent is undeclared. That is why adequacy could only be argued by SCORING AGAINST CAPABILITIES, never by FIDELITY TO A REFERENT.
a_rows_sample.statement: Testing five possible classifications of what K 'is' (ontology, mathematical state, representation, abstraction, domain-specific projection), only 'representation' is defensible, but its referent (the W it represents) is never named in the theory, so adequacy can currently only be judged by capability-scoring rather than fidelity to a declared referent; once Omega:W->O exists, adequacy becomes answerable, but not before.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three of eleven have no body: dedup (does not exist), Sigma's strength rule, delta's commit case.
a_rows_sample.statement: A table of eleven operations over K (member, add, merge, supersede, contradicts, dedup, Sigma, Gamma, delta, History, Lineage) with signatures, preconditions, postconditions, determinism and failure modes shows three have no defined body: dedup does not exist as an operation, Sigma's strength rule is absent, and delta's body is undefined for the commit case.

a_rows_sample.anchor: id before withdrawal : 86a0330e2b65 / id after withdrawal : a9d84e7a43d8 / SAME? False / R edge (...) now dangles: True ... The theory's identity rule and its mutability rule cannot both hold.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executing kaudit.py shows that because id is declared derived as H(P,e,c,t,Pi) while e.state is declared mutable, withdrawing one evidence item re-keys the assertion's id and breaks every R edge pointing at the old id, violating StructuralValid's own no-dangling clause -- an internal contradiction between the identity rule and the mutability rule in the same field table, worsened by the audit's own addition of a mutable state field to e.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Because Pi is inside id, the same fact from two sources is two assertions. ... K grows without bound under re-observation ... R is not maintained by merge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Executing kaudit.py shows two assertions of the identical proposition from two different sources get distinct ids (because Pi/provenance is inside id), so merge-as-union cannot deduplicate: corroboration becomes indistinguishable from duplication, K grows unboundedly under repeated observation of the same fact, merge's idempotence holds only for byte-identical assertions, and cross-state relations between semantic twins are never created by merge, silently dropping information.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The corpus says 'nobody ever asked'. ... Seven of eight are directly covered; the eighth is partial. The audit reported zero of five.
b_rows_sample.statement: A six-way Zero-lens dimension/value taxonomy (known / unknown Zero-A / not-assessed / absent / not-applicable / unresolved Zero-B) with five non-collapse laws (UNKNOWN!=ABSENT, UNRESOLVED!=INVALID, NOT_ASSESSED!=LOW_CONFIDENCE, NOT_APPLICABLE!=UNKNOWN, NO_EVIDENCE!=INVALID_EVIDENCE) plus a sixth boxed law (UnknownValue(D)!=UnknownDimension(D)), together with an independently-committed Abhava ontological absence typology (Pragabhava/Pradhvamsabhava/Atyantabhava/Anyonyabhava) and an AbsenceClaim record shape, jointly cover seven of the mandate's eight missingness cases directly and one partially -- versus the audit's report of zero of five covered.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is no component of K holding the set of recognised dimensions. ... D_t is the smallest missing component. With it, 'not assessed' is D in D_t AND not exists a in A: a.P.D=D -- decidable in O(n). Without it, the statement has no truth-maker.
b_rows_sample.statement: An executed probe (MISSINGNESS-NOT-ASSESSED in THEORY-CONSTRUCTION-TEST.md) shows a never-assessed dimension and an assessed-with-no-result dimension both render identically in K=(A,R) as 'no assertion mentioning that dimension', proving them provably indistinguishable; introducing D_t (the set of currently recognised dimensions) as a component of K makes 'not assessed' decidable in O(n) and is identified as the smallest missing component to close the missingness gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: VERIFIER RECOMMENDS -- not CORPUS ESTABLISHES. K = (D_t, A, R) ... with id = H(P, e_refs, c, t, Pi) where e_refs projects out the mutable state. ... Nothing here is adopted. This is a proposal, and it is smaller than the three the corpus already contains -- which should be consumed first (ES-005.4).
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes (explicitly labelled VERIFIER RECOMMENDS, not adopted) a minimal repair K=(D_t,A,R) adding the recognised-dimension set D_t and redefining id=H(P,e_refs,c,t,Pi) to project out the mutable state field, arguing this closes the missingness gap (7/8 cases), removes the identity/mutability contradiction, and makes a dedup operator definable by unioning Pi and e on (P,c,t); explicitly states this does not repair non-identifiability (needs a W,Omega layer beneath K) or uncertainty (needs U(H)), and that the corpus's own existing three constructions should be consumed first per ES-005.4.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Empty != ContradictoryEvidence. ... Missing != False. ... EvalPolicy may need a third result: Undetermined.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues no-evidence must be distinguished from conflicting-evidence when assigning Sigma=Unknown, and that a missing required measurement (x=?) cannot be inferred as False; proposes a candidate three-valued policy-decision output {Permit, Deny, Undetermined} as a bridge between missingness and policy, explicitly marked as a candidate requiring corpus confirmation, not a final decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The three exclusions were a discovery failure, not a mathematical limit. They are absent from the AUTHORIZED MODEL v0.2 ... so the finding is real, and it is a GOVERNANCE finding: the constructions exist and were never promoted.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a prior verdict ('THEORY CLOSED AGAINST THE STATED CRITERIA -- NOT COMPLETE IN EVERY RESPECT', with 'a theory that cannot say nobody ever asked is closed, not finished') by showing the corpus does say 'nobody ever asked' (the not-assessed Zero-lens dimension state, committed one day before this programme began) and does have formal, typed constructions for non-identifiability and uncertainty; reclassifies the three exclusions as a discovery failure rather than a mathematical limit, and as a governance finding since these constructions are measured absent (zero grep occurrences of unknown/absent/not assessed/uncertain/identifiab) from the authorized v0.2 model despite existing in the raw corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: - **`Missingness` — 0.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Three concepts have exactly zero definitional occurrences corpus-wide: Missingness (the concept exists richly under other names — Zero, abhāva, Missing, 'not assessed' — so this is a vocabulary gap masquerading as a theory gap), Admissibility (its two laws are cited constantly, 42.9/42.41, but the term itself is never defined), and AuthorityAct (confirming, by whole-corpus scan rather than targeted grep, that the object the entire governance model turns on has no type).

b_rows_sample.anchor:
**First, the vocabulary fact that explains why this looked unresolved:** the word **`Missingness`
 has 0 definitional occurrences corpus-wide**
b_rows_sample.statement: 8 of 9 mandated missingness distinctions (not-asked, asked-but-no-answer, unknown, absent, no-evidence-found, searched-but-insufficient, deliberately-omitted, deleted; only 'never existed'/Prāgabhāva lacks one) have a named corpus construct across the Zero taxonomy and the Sanskrit abhāva typology, and 4 of them (unknown, absent, insufficient, not-applicable) are executable, tested, passing code in zero_reference.py (8/8 tests); the word 'Missingness' itself has 0 definitional occurrences, so searching for the word finds nothing while the capability exists richly under other names.

b_rows_sample.anchor: With D_t: "not assessed" is D ∈ D_t ∧ ¬∃a ∈ 𝒜 : a.P.D = D — decidable in O(n).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A representation is adequate for a question only if the distinctions required to answer that question are preserved by the representation. b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy for this experiment: a candidate representation R:S->D is adequate iff for every required distinction pair (x,y) in R_req, x≠y implies R(x)≠R(y); a structured representation may satisfy this even when two conditions share the same primary 'value' field, so uniqueness of the primary value is not required.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structural causal model X_i=f_i(Pa_i,U_i); CausalEdge != GenericRelationship; need for G_C
b_rows_sample.statement: Represents a structural causal model conceptually as X_i = f_i(Pa_i, U_i) (Pa_i = causal parents, U_i = exogenous factors), a mechanism-oriented representation rather than a purely correlational graph. Argues KnowledgeOS needs a distinct causal graph G_C alongside the existing knowledge-relationship graph G_K -- relatedTo does not mean causes, dependsOn does not necessarily mean causes -- formalized as CausalEdge != GenericRelationship.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CausalClaim tuple; causal generalization scope; causal edges are knowledge assertions not metaphysical truth
b_rows_sample.statement: A causal claim should carry a GeneralizationScope (e.g. {BusinessUnit, Technology, Environment, Time}) so an agent can judge whether it applies to the current situation. Gives the full CausalClaim tuple: (Cause, Effect, Mechanism, Evidence, StudyDesign, Assumptions, Scope, Time, EffectSize, Uncertainty, Model) -- 'a powerful domain object'. Distinguishes the causal graph G_C from the provenance/dependency graph G_P: a causal edge A->B should itself have provenance (Evidence -> CausalClaim(A->B)); the causal graph is not metaphysical truth -- an edge A->B is a knowledge assertion supported by evidence, so CausalEdge is in K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 43 verdict, six core principles, and G_C as a new graph type alongside G_K/G_I/G_P
b_rows_sample.statement: Declares STEP 43 -- PASS and restates six core principles: Correlation != Causation; Observation != Intervention; Temporal precedence != Causality; Prediction != Explanation; Counterfactual != Observation; Causal claims require assumptions. Adds a new mathematical layer G_C (causal graph) to the architecture's existing graph family: G_K (knowledge relationships), G_I (identity relationships), G_P (provenance/dependency), and now G_C (causal relationships) -- 'these graphs interact but have different semantics'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance and Causality reduced to typed relations; Supports != Causes != DependsOn
b_rows_sample.statement: Provenance Prov(C)={E_1,...,E_n}, generalized to a DAG-shaped Prov(x); reduced to a relation, not a primitive object: Supports(E,C), DerivedFrom(C1,C2). Causality is another relation Causes(A,B), explicitly not to be conflated with Supports(A,B): Supports != Causes. Software dependency DependsOn(A,B) is yet another relation, and DependsOn != Causes -- a system may technically depend on a component without that component being the causal reason for a given outcome. Consolidates a typed relation set R={Supports, DependsOn, Causes, Identifies, MapsTo, Contradicts, Precedes} that must remain typed: collapsing everything into a generic RelatedTo(A,B) loses semantics and could let an AI infer RelatedTo=>Causes, 'recreating one of the fundamental problems we eliminated in Step 43'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge version graph G_K=(V,E); RevisionGraph != CausalGraph; candidate partial order tested for reflexivity/antisymmetry/transitivity
b_rows_sample.statement: Represents legitimate branching K1->K2^A and K1->K2^B (competing hypotheses) as a version graph G_K=(V,E) with V=KnowledgeStates and E=RevisionRelations, more general than a simple version chain; argues a revision graph should normally be acyclic (a revision should not causally depend on itself) while a domain may separately represent cyclic feedback elsewhere, distinguishing RevisionGraph from CausalGraph. Defines the candidate partial order K_A⪯K_B (K_B is a valid successor/refinement of K_A) and tests it for reflexivity (K_A⪯K_A), antisymmetry (K_A⪯K_B ∧ K_B⪯K_A ⇒ K_A=K_B under the chosen equivalence), and transitivity (K_A⪯K_B ∧ K_B⪯K_C ⇒ K_A⪯K_C).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structural causal model re-derived (do(X=x) replaces the mechanism); generic-edge-collapse experiment FAILs, reinforcing typed relations
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-derives structural equations X=f_X(U_X), Y=f_Y(X,U_Y) with do(X=x) replacing X's mechanism (experiment 9: observing X=x does not block Z->Y, but do(X=x) removes the incoming mechanism into X -- DifferentCausalSemantics -- PASS), and the G_K (knowledge/dependency) vs G_C (causal) graph distinction. Experiment 10: using one generic 'A->B' edge type for dependency, provenance, temporal order, and causality simultaneously yields SemanticFailure -- explicitly FAIL, reinforcing the requirement for explicit relation types (DerivedFrom, DependsOn, Precedes, Supports, Contradicts, Causes, Authorizes) that must never be reduced to one generic arrow.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Trust non-transitivity; multi-graph model (G_K,G_P,G_D,G_A,G_T) not collapsible (generic-relation-schema FAILs)
b_rows_sample.statement: States trust transitivity is not universally valid: Trust(A,B)=High and Trust(B,C)=High does not license Trust(A,C)=High -- experiment 20 rejects that inference -- PASS, 'prevents dangerous trust propagation through agent networks'. Extends the multi-graph family with a Trust graph G_T alongside Knowledge (G_K), Provenance (G_P), Dependency (G_D), and Authority (G_A) graphs, which 'should not be collapsed into one universal graph'. Experiment 21: representing all relationships as one generic relation(source,target,type) with no bounded semantics yields SemanticAmbiguity -- explicitly FAIL, 'the relationships have different invariants' -- while noting a higher-level system may still correlate G_K/G_P/G_A while each retains its own domain semantics.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero is not an algebraic zero element. It is an algebraic/operational judgment of eliminability relative to a transformation and preservation contract.
b_rows_sample.statement: Renames the proposed 'Algebraic Zero' to Transformation-relative Zero, rejecting the term 'algebraic zero' as colliding with additive-identity/kernel meanings; freezes Zero_{T,Pi}(x) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(D\x)) as the definition to preserve, over a general preservation contract Pi rather than the narrower (O_I,B_I) pair, motivated by cases such as governance-inquiry contracts Pi=(O,B,A_u) needing authorization constraints.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A direct sum requires substantial structure ... T_R(D) -> (Inv_T(D), Delta_R(D), Rem_T(D)) ... a structural decomposition, not yet an algebraic direct sum.
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the proposed algebraic claim T_R(D)=Inv_T(D)⊕Delta_R(D)⊕Rem_T(D) as too strong for a general corpus/graph/logical-theory/epistemic-state domain (a direct sum presupposes a common carrier, defined sum, independence, existence and uniqueness of decomposition), replacing it with a weaker structural mapping to a triple of observables, with the direct sum retained only as a possible special case in a particular mathematical regime.

b_rows_sample.anchor: But mathematically, projection normally has an idempotence property ... elimination can change the context for subsequent eliminations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against calling the elimination/retention operator L_{T,I} a 'projection operator' before idempotence L(L(D))=L(D) is established, illustrating with a three-element example (removing a makes b redundant, then removing b makes c redundant) where one-pass and iterative elimination differ; proposes testing three possible outcomes for L^2 vs L: idempotent, order-dependent (L_a L_b != L_b L_a), or a fixed-point/normalization process D_{n+1}=L(D_n).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Kalamana Rekha, or time-measurement lines ... features that are thought to develop/change over time from more stable primary structures ... If the inquiry itself asks about temporal evolution, the temporal dimension cannot be Zero. Zero(timestamp | Q1) != Zero(timestamp | Q2).
b_rows_sample.statement: Draws on the book's explicit Kalamana Rekha (time-measurement lines) and its distinction between features that develop/change over time versus stable primary structures to propose a Structural-state-plus-Temporal-state distinction for KnowledgeOS, arguing this supplies a conceptual counterexample to the current KR-REP-REDUCTION experiment's R5 timestamp removal: while timestamps were safely eliminable for that toy inquiry, an inquiry about temporal evolution would make the temporal dimension non-Zero, reinforcing the contract-relative principle Zero(timestamp|Q1) != Zero(timestamp|Q2).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero_{T,\Pi}(x;K_t) but after a challenge ... \neg Zero_{T,\Pi}(x;K_{t+1}). Then Zero is clearly state-relative and time-relative: Zero_t(x) \neq Zero_{t+1}(x).
b_rows_sample.statement: Time-indexes the existing Transformation-relative Zero, extending it with an explicit temporal argument on top of the already-established transformation/observable/contract relativity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation as a projection; observational equivalence S_1~_H S_2; indistinguishable-states experiment (Experiment 1)
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the central Step 81 question: can KnowledgeOS actually determine the relevant system state from what it observes -- the boundary between having data and having sufficient information. Formalizes O_t=H(S_t) as a projection from the real state space into a much smaller observable space, so O_t is generally only a partial representation of S_t. Defines observational equivalence: S_1 ~_H S_2 iff H(S_1)=H(S_2), meaning KnowledgeOS cannot distinguish them from current observations. Experiment 1: S_1 (compliant architecture with one unmanaged dependency) and S_2 (compliant with no hidden dependency) produce identical telemetry O(S_1)=O(S_2) -- expected KnowledgeOS must not claim to distinguish S_1 from S_2 -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identifiability defined and demonstrated as a major safeguard against false certainty; observability for dynamic systems (Experiments 2-3)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a property Q(S) as identifiable from observations iff H(S_1)=H(S_2) implies Q(S_1)=Q(S_2); otherwise Q is NotIdentifiable. Experiment 2: KnowledgeOS wants Q(S)='no unauthorized dependency exists' but two states with H(S_1)=H(S_2) have Q(S_1)=True, Q(S_2)=False -- expected Q is NotIdentifiable -- PASS, 'a major safeguard against false architectural certainty'. Extends to dynamic-system observability: whether internal state S_0 can be reconstructed from O_0:T and known actions u_0:T-1. Experiment 3: two different internal states produce identical observations for every currently monitored signal -- expected FullStateObservability=False -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No observation -> no justified claim; absence-of-evidence ≠ evidence-of-absence in architecture governance (Experiment 4)
a_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle: no observation -> no justified claim; more precisely, if the evidence cannot distinguish relevant states, the corresponding knowledge claim must remain uncertain. Worked example: KnowledgeOS checks the dependency graph, finds A->B, but does not observe dynamically loaded dependencies -- it can legitimately conclude 'no violation was found in the observed dependency graph' but not 'no dependency violation exists'. Experiment 4: observed NoViolationFound, system concludes ViolationDoesNotExist -- expected Rejected unless the observation mechanism is sufficiently complete for that claim -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence coverage warned against arbitrary percentage metrics; measurement design (adding observations) to restore identifiability, tied to Step 75's Value of Information (Experiments 5-6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Coverage(Q,O) -- how much of the relevant state space is constrained by observations -- warned against automatic reduction to a single percentage. Experiment 5: system reports Coverage=94% with no formal definition of coverage -- expected UnsupportedMetric -- PASS: 'a precise number without a defined measurement model is not mathematical rigor.' Proposes measurement design: if O_1 cannot distinguish S_1,S_2, adding O_2 can make (H_1(S_1),H_2(S_1))≠(H_1(S_2),H_2(S_2)), restoring distinguishability. Experiment 6: initial telemetry O_1(S_1)=O_1(S_2), adding runtime dependency tracing O_2 gives O_2(S_1)≠O_2(S_2) -- expected IdentifiabilityImproved -- PASS. Gives the loop Uncertainty -> ObservationDesign -> NewEvidence -> ImprovedKnowledge, 'connects directly to Step 75's Value of Information'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation design as a decision-driven filter, not maximal telemetry collection; irrelevant-signal ObservabilityGap example (Experiment 7)
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames which signals to collect as itself a design decision: ObservationDesign=f(DecisionNeeds,Uncertainty,Cost,Risk), because we want observations that reduce uncertainty about relevant decisions, not everything. Experiment 7: KnowledgeOS collects CPU temperature, screen resolution, process count, but cannot determine whether architecture boundaries are violated -- expected ObservabilityGap -- PASS: 'more telemetry does not necessarily mean more observability.' Restates the correct question as 'does this observation discriminate between states that matter?', more rigorous than 'do we have enough monitoring?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Taxonomy of architecture-relevant observation types; multi-source observation conflict must not be silently resolved (Experiment 8)
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists relevant architecture-governance observation types, each a different projection of system state: SourceDependencies, RuntimeDependencies, APIContracts, DeploymentTopology, Configuration, InfrastructureState, SecurityControls, ChangeHistory. Experiment 8: repository analysis says A-/->B while runtime tracing shows A->B -- expected ObservationConflict, and importantly the system should not simply choose whichever observation arrived last -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multiple observation sources can disagree without contradiction; source-specific authority (CommittedState≠DeployedState) resolves apparent conflicts (Experiments 9-10)
a_rows_sample.statement: Names multiple observation sources O^repo, O^runtime, O^infra, O^governance, O^human that can disagree. Experiment 9: repository says Version=3, deployment environment says Version=2 -- expected StateConflict rather than silently overwriting one with the other -- PASS. Introduces source-specific authority: Runtime is authoritative for CurrentlyRunningVersion, Git for CommittedVersion -- the two statements are not contradictory, they answer different questions (CommittedState≠DeployedState). Experiment 10: Git Version=3, Runtime Version=2, system concludes OneSourceMustBeWrong -- expected NotNecessarily -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Ubiquitous-language collision: undifferentiated 'version' collapsing four distinct domain concepts is a FAIL; formal Observation record with provenance (Experiment 11)
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a DDD ubiquitous-language collision: the word 'version' can mean SourceVersion, BuildVersion, DeploymentVersion, or RuntimeVersion -- distinct domain concepts that should not be collapsed merely because they share a string. Experiment 11: system stores a bare version="3.2" field without distinguishing source/artifact/deployment/runtime -- expected SemanticAmbiguity -- result FAIL (explicit confirmed failure). Requires every observation to ideally be a record Observation=(Source,Timestamp,Context,Method,Value,Confidence,Provenance), not necessarily every field in every implementation but semantically these dimensions matter.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation staleness and context-dependent freshness thresholds; temporal validity of observations (Experiments 12-14)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 12: observation RuntimeVersion=2 was captured yesterday while current deployment is 3 -- expected ObservationStaleness must be considered -- PASS. Defines Age(O)=t_now - t_observation, noting acceptable freshness is property-dependent (seconds matter for CPUUsage, days may not matter for ArchitecturePrinciple) -- FreshnessThreshold is context-dependent. Experiment 13: system declares a universal Freshness<24h for every observation type -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Introduces temporal validity: an observation can be ValidAt(t_o) without being ValidAt(t_now), reinforcing the earlier temporal epistemic model. Experiment 14: DatabaseHealthy=True observed at 10:00, database fails at 10:05; at 10:10 the old observation is not necessarily false historically, it is StaleForCurrentState -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: State estimation must preserve uncertainty rather than collapsing to a point estimate; decision-aware state estimation and DecisionRelevantObservability (Experiments 15-18)
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires KnowledgeOS to preserve uncertainty (e.g. P(S_1|O)=0.7, P(S_2|O)=0.3) rather than storing S=S_1 unless the decision context permits that approximation. Experiment 15: a 51/49 split is stored as CurrentState=S_1 with certainty -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Introduces decision-aware state estimation: if both possible states produce the same decision D(S_1)=D(S_2)=A, the uncertainty may be irrelevant for that decision -- 'an important optimization'. Experiment 16: P(S_1)=0.6, P(S_2)=0.4 but D(S_1)=D(S_2) -- expected decision can remain stable despite state uncertainty -- PASS. Concludes we need DecisionRelevantObservability rather than FullObservability, 'a much more practical architectural target'. Experiment 17: unknown state dimension Z has no effect on policy/risk/decision/authorization -- expected NoNeedToObserveZ unless future decisions depend on it -- PASS. Experiment 18: P(S_1)=P(S_2)=0.5 but D(S_1)=A≠D(S_2)=B -- expected AdditionalEvidence may be required before action -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The value of observability is determined by how uncertainty affects decisions, connecting observability to decision theory; a material-vs-immaterial architecture-governance example (Experiments 19-20)
a_rows_sample.statement: States the rule: the value of observability is determined by how uncertainty affects decisions, connecting Observability to DecisionTheory. Architecture example: if an uncertain dependency A->B is harmless (Decision(A)=Decision(B)) no urgent investigation is required, but if it violates a constitutional architecture rule (Decision(A)≠Decision(B)) the uncertainty is material. Experiment 19: unknown dependency affects no security/governance/architectural constraint -- expected LowDecisionImpact -- PASS. Experiment 20: unknown dependency could cross a forbidden bounded-context boundary -- expected HighDecisionImpact, therefore InvestigationRequired -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationQuality distinct from ObservationQuantity; correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation (Experiments 21-23)
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ObservationQuality (accuracy, freshness, completeness, provenance, independence, resolution) from ObservationQuantity. Experiment 21: 100 telemetry signals all derive from the same underlying sensor, system claims EvidenceStrength=100x -- expected Rejected -- PASS, 'echoes our earlier independence analysis'. States correlated observations O_1,O_2,O_3 from one source should not be treated as three independent pieces of evidence, particularly important for AI systems that may repeatedly summarize the same source. Experiment 22: five agents independently repeat the same repository finding, all using the same repository snapshot -- expected EvidenceCount=1 in the relevant independence sense, not five independent confirmations -- PASS. Requires an observation-provenance graph (O_1<-Source_X, O_2<-Source_X) to identify CommonSource(O_1,O_2), preventing artificial confidence inflation. Experiment 23: ten agents produce identical conclusions from one document while one independently measured runtime signal contradicts them -- expected SourceIndependence must be considered -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Formalization pipeline ArchitecturePrinciple->FormalProperty->RequiredObservations->Verifier->GovernanceDecision demonstrated end-to-end; not-machine-verifiable rules identified explicitly (Experiments 24-25)
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses the question 'what observation makes an architecture rule machine-verifiable?' -- if no such observation exists, the rule cannot be fully automated. Experiment 24: rule 'services must not bypass the domain boundary' has no repository/runtime/dependency observation able to establish it -- expected NotMachineVerifiable -- PASS. Defines the chain ArchitecturePrinciple -> FormalProperty -> RequiredObservations -> Verifier -> GovernanceDecision, 'exactly the bridge we need between architectural intent and executable governance'. Experiment 25: principle formalized, required observation defined, verifier evaluates the property, violation creates a governed finding -- expected ExecutableArchitectureControl -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ComplianceUndetermined when a required observation is unavailable; three-valued (True/False/Unknown) and four-valued (+NotApplicable) governance logic; Unknown≠Failure (Experiments 26-28)
a_rows_sample.statement: States that when a required observation is unavailable, the correct result is not Compliant but ComplianceUndetermined -- 'may become one of the most important KnowledgeOS states'. Experiment 26: architecture rule requires runtime evidence which is unavailable -- expected Compliance=Unknown, not Compliance=True -- PASS. Proposes three-valued governance logic (True/False/Unknown), since not every governance property is binary, with Violation=False not necessarily implying Compliant=True: insufficient evidence gives Status=Unknown. Experiment 27: no evidence of violation and no sufficient evidence of compliance -- expected Unknown -- PASS, 'epistemically much more honest'. Extends to a four-state possibility (Compliant/NonCompliant/Unknown/NotApplicable), NotApplicable being important because not every rule applies to every component, and a genuine DDD domain semantic distinct from null or false. Experiment 28: rule 'database encryption must use algorithm X' applied to a component with no database -- expected NotApplicable, not NonCompliant -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ObservabilityDebt and a self-improving GovernanceRule->ObservationRequirement->EngineeringCapability->Evidence->Governance loop (Experiment 29)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ObservabilityDebt: when important governance properties cannot currently be observed, the organization has a gap between DesiredGovernance and AvailableEvidence. Experiment 29: critical architecture rule I_critical has no existing required observation -- expected ObservabilityDebt -- PASS. Shows the system can generate an ObservationRequirement engineering item (worked example: rule 'domain must not depend on infrastructure', required observation 'static dependency graph', current coverage 'missing', action 'build dependency extractor'), giving the loop GovernanceRule -> ObservationRequirement -> EngineeringCapability -> Evidence -> Governance, making architecture governance self-improving.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 81 deeper result: a governance claim is only as strong as the observability/identifiability of the property it asserts; five new invariants; verdict PASS; True/False/Unknown reasoning pattern formalized
a_rows_sample.statement: States the Step 81 deeper result: a governance claim is only as strong as the observability and identifiability of the property it asserts -- 'one of the most important mathematical principles we have reached so far'. Names five invariants: I_Identifiability (KnowledgeOS must not assert a state property as determined when multiple observationally-compatible states produce different values of that property); I_Unknown (insufficient evidence produces Unknown, not implicit compliance); I_ObservationProvenance (material observations retain source, time, method, and contextual provenance); I_DecisionRelevantObservability (observability investment should prioritize uncertainties capable of changing governed decisions); I_EvidenceIndependence (correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation). Declares STEP 81 -- PASS, distinguishing Unknown from False and True as architecturally enormous: contrasts conventional 'if not violation: compliant' logic against the required 'if violation is proven: NON_COMPLIANT; elif compliance is proven: COMPLIANT; else: UNKNOWN' pattern -- the difference between absence of detected failure and evidence of correctness.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Preview of Step 82 (uncertainty propagation through Observation->Measurement->Inference->CausalModel->Decision), outside batch B0023 scope
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes by posing the next problem: given observations O_1,O_2 with uncertainties sigma_1,sigma_2, deriving K=f(O_1,O_2) and Decision=g(K), how should uncertainty propagate through the chain Observation->Measurement->Inference->CausalModel->Decision without producing 'High uncertainty -> False precision'. Names the needed toolkit: error propagation, Bayesian updating, confidence intervals, posterior distributions, dependence between uncertainties, sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty-aware decision thresholds. This is Step 82's problem statement; its file lies outside batch B0023 and is not further read or extracted here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS never observes the whole world ... W\rightarrow O\rightarrow M(O) ... M(O)\neq W. That is unavoidable ... know precisely what the model represents, what it does not represent, and under which conditions its conclusions are valid
b_rows_sample.statement: States KnowledgeOS never observes the whole world, formalizing W->O->M(O) with M(O)≠W as unavoidable, reframing the goal from a perfect reality-copy to explicit knowledge of what the model represents/omits/when it's valid.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \pi:W\rightarrow O ... W_1\neq W_2 while \pi(W_1)=\pi(W_2) ... one of the deepest sources of uncertainty
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes observation as a projection pi:W->O, noting distinct world states can map to the same observation — 'one of the deepest sources of uncertainty.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: W_1\sim_O W_2 if \pi(W_1)=\pi(W_2) ... Observationally indistinguishable\neq identical
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines observational equivalence W1~_O W2, giving Observationally indistinguishable ≠ identical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CPU=40%, Memory=50%, HTTP=200 ... Reality A: Database healthy. Reality B: Database degraded but traffic is currently low ... O_A=O_B but W_A\neq W_B
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: a healthy-database reality and a degraded-but-low-traffic reality produce identical monitoring observations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: WorldState=Underdetermined ... another form of Zero. Not the system failed. Rather the available observations do not identify the relevant world state
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines WorldState=Underdetermined as another form of Zero when multiple materially different states remain consistent with observations, explicitly not a system failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X is identifiable from O if \pi(W_1)=\pi(W_2) always implies X(W_1)=X(W_2) ... X is not identifiable from the available observations
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines identifiability of a property X from observations O.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I am 95% confident ... structurally unidentifiable ... service returned HTTP 200 ... Is the database transaction durable? ... Confidence cannot compensate for missing information
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues identifiability outranks confidence: a high-confidence AI claim can be unjustified if the property is structurally unidentifiable, worked with an HTTP-200/transaction-durability example — 'confidence cannot compensate for missing information.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: RandomUncertainty from StructuralUncertainty. Random uncertainty may be reducible by more observations. Structural uncertainty may arise because the relevant variable is not observed at all. This is much more serious
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes random uncertainty (reducible by more observations) from structural uncertainty (unobserved relevant variable), the latter more serious.

b_rows_sample.anchor: X\rightarrow Z\rightarrow Y ... EngineerExperience ... DeploymentMethod ... FailureRisk ... if we ignore experience, we may attribute the wrong causal effect to deployment
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked latent-variable example: an unobserved EngineerExperience variable jointly driving deployment method and failure risk risks wrong causal attribution if ignored.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z\rightarrow X and Z\rightarrow Y ... observing X\leftrightarrow Y does not establish X\rightarrow Y ... reinforces the result from 25Z
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates confounding: observed correlation does not establish causation, explicitly reinforcing the Step 25Z causal result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ModelBoundary ... variables represented; variables omitted; assumptions; applicable contexts; temporal validity; data sources; known limitations
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a required ModelBoundary specifying seven components a model must make explicit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ModelContract=(Inputs,Outputs,Assumptions,Scope,Validity,Limitations,Version) ... analogous to the ActionContract from 25Z
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-field ModelContract explicitly analogous to the ActionContract from Step 25Z.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NetworkLatency<100ms ... ModelApplicable\Rightarrow AssumptionsSatisfied. This should be a deterministic check where possible
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked example: violating a model's stated assumption (network latency bound) invalidates applicability, giving ModelApplicable => AssumptionsSatisfied as a deterministic check.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal D_{valid} ... outside it we should not silently extrapolate ... x\in[0,100] trained, x=500 received ... Computability\neq Validity
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a model validity region D_valid; a model can still compute an out-of-region output, but that does not establish validity — Computability ≠ Validity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CanCompute(x) from CanJustify(x) ... a model may technically compute f(x) while epistemically Justified(f(x))=False
b_rows_sample.statement: States the profound distinction CanCompute(x) vs CanJustify(x): technical computability does not imply epistemic justification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ValidInference=Inference+ApplicabilityProof
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines ValidInference as Inference plus an ApplicabilityProof spanning context/data/time/identity/semantics/model assumptions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: T(E) ... P(E\mid T(E),\theta)=P(E\mid T(E)) ... sufficient statistic ... KnowledgeOS must be careful
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces the concept of a sufficient statistic T(E) retaining all information relevant to a parameter, with a caution against careless reliance.

This revises a prior lineage-map verdict of 'DISPLACED -> ABANDONED' to a three-way split: Omega-a ABSORBED, Omega-b DROPPED, Omega-c DISPLACED.

b_rows_sample.statement: Concludes the two 'Lord' concepts (Omega-c's analytical observer and R5's action-selector) can coexist and never actually competed, since R5-Lord consumes EC (Omega-a's formal descendant) -- the apparent conflict is a purely nominal ubiquitous-language collision across the R4->R5 boundary, resolvable by renaming rather than by redesigning the model, because the responsibilities were already separated. b_rows_sample.statement: Restates and extends the 2B-5 Lord/Omega investigation's finding (Omega-a's ideal-reference responsibility transformed via Ideal State into the Epistemic Contract, feeding Zero(K_t,G,EC)) and reframes the old-Lord/new-Lord naming collision as the responsibility changing while the name stayed the same -- 'exactly the sort of DDD/Ubiquitous-Language collision that should be recorded rather than silently merged.' Poses as a clean, not-yet-answered research question whether Omega-b's unboundedness is mathematically required for K_t/Ideal-State/Delta_t, or was merely an unnecessary property of the earlier model; introduces the distinction 'Ideal State != complete Knowledge Space' (the Knower needs only what is sufficient for the goal, not everything) as a possible explanation for why unboundedness may not be needed.

a_rows_sample.statement: Two mission statements found in canon: M-A (AIP-14/ADR-AIP-02/R-23), 'the platform exists solely to improve delivery of PublicDigit; every iteration produces measurable progress on a PublicDigit feature; platform-only iterations are exceptional and require explicit ARB approval' — ADOPTED. M-B (Product Discovery Charter), 'there is a market for an AI-native Knowledge Operating System for software engineering whose core promise is preserving architectural knowledge, enforcing engineering governance, and enabling AI agents to reason consistently across complex software systems' — PROPOSED, UNAPPROVED, explicitly a hypothesis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mission, as adopted ... KnowledgeOS exists to improve the delivery of PublicDigit by governing how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified and evolved — in a form that is independent of project, programming language and execution provider
a_rows_sample.statement: The adopted mission combines two observed halves: the purpose from AIP-14 (improve delivery of PublicDigit) and the form from the Reference Architecture section 1 (governs how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified, and evolved, independent of project, programming language, or execution provider). The apparent contradiction between 'solely for PublicDigit' and 'independent of project' is resolved: AIP-14 constrains WHY work is undertaken, the Reference Architecture constrains WHAT is built — build portable things only when doing so advances this product; AIP-14's enforcement is an iteration-cost metric and an over-evolution review, a cost control, not a scope boundary. M-B is a different mission with a different customer ('organizations' rather than 'the engineering team'), not adopted, gate shut.
