a_rows_sample.statement: Eight responsibilities, each traced to an artifact: R-1 govern the engineering lifecycle (EEP); R-2 hold the authority model (ES-001); R-3 hold the method (Round39-MC, Round47-OP, workbooks); R-4 define the shape of a capability (Platform_Capability_Pattern FROZEN, PGP-01..05); R-5 make governed knowledge retrievable and enforceable (Knowledge-Constitution, 18 lint rules, portal); R-6 harvest reusable knowledge from operational evidence (ES-006.4/ES-006.1 — the responsibility exists, but 0 traversals); R-7 keep runtime vocabulary out of governance (asserted, artifact missing); R-8 refuse to approve its own work (EEP: automation does not approve itself).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 3 — Non-responsibilities (N-1..N-10) ... N-1 is breached today. Recording the breach is this document's act; repairing it is not
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten non-responsibilities, each traced: N-1 business/domain knowledge (elections, voters, adjudication) — BREACHED: ES-005.1 names PublicDigit and hard-codes .claude/; N-2 a product's evidence records; N-3 any register's contents (only the governing rule); N-4 a runtime's vocabulary; N-5 its own approval; N-6 governance defined by automation; N-7 duplicated knowledge (ES-005.4); N-8 materialized consolidations (BRM-1 retired extraction-by-copy); N-9 a product's PKS; N-10 orchestrators/workflow engines/state machines (Reference Architecture section 1: deliberately, and not forever, until operational evidence demonstrates insufficiency). N-1's breach is recorded but not repaired here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-1 | Which mission governs — M-A (adopted, PublicDigit-serving) or M-B (proposed, product-seeking)?
a_rows_sample.statement: MQ-1: which mission governs, M-A or M-B — they have different customers and are not reconcilable by drafting — authority: sponsor + DA.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-2..MQ-7 | Who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole? ... Is N-1's breach to be repaired ... Is PD-3's individual ownership intentional ... is the harvest responsibility even required ... Does N-10 still hold ... What would falsify M-A?
a_rows_sample.statement: Six further open questions: MQ-2 who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole, given three authority systems none of which spans them (sponsor+DA+ARB jointly); MQ-3 is N-1's breach to be repaired or is the invariant wrong (ARB); MQ-4 is PD-3's individual ownership intentional/a succession risk (DA); MQ-5 under M-A is the harvest responsibility (R-6) even required, since a reuse loop may be out of mission if the platform serves one product (ARB); MQ-6 does N-10 still hold or has evidence of insufficiency accumulated (ARB); MQ-7 what would falsify M-A, since a mission with no falsifier is not a mission (sponsor).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The finding ... KnowledgeOS has TWO missions. One is adopted; the other is what everyone has been designing for ... Almost every architectural difficulty in this track is a symptom of designing under M-B while governed by M-A
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's headline finding (before its own later withdrawal, recorded above): almost every architectural difficulty in the track is a symptom of designing under M-B (organizations as customers) while governed by M-A (serve PublicDigit): under M-A, extraction is premature and 'knowledgeos init' is out of mission, while under M-B they are the goal/the product; under M-A the harvest loop is optional (MQ-5) while under M-B it is essential; under M-A 'no second adopting product' is not a gap while under M-B it is the blocker; under M-A platform-only iterations need ARB approval while under M-B they are normal work. MQ-1 is not a documentation question — until answered, the same evidence supports opposite conclusions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
a_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — D-9 · Derive the Platform Cost metric; run the AIP-14 over-evolution check (FIRST — it gates the docket itself)
a_rows_sample.statement: Package 1 (D-9): compute the AIP-14 Platform Cost metric for recent iterations and rule whether the over-evolution review fires, since the tripwire cannot fire if the metric is never computed. Supporting: ~48h produced 20+ platform-only documents and zero PublicDigit feature progress in this track (self-declared). Opposing: dense real product delivery ran in parallel; the platform work was commissioned, not drift. Downstream: whether Packages 2-10 are worked now at all. Authority: ARB. Recommendation: ADOPT, run the check before anything else on this docket.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — AMENDMENT (REV 2): the metric must be DEFINED before it is RUN ... D-9 therefore splits into D-9a (DEFINE) and D-9b (RUN)
a_rows_sample.statement: A PA review challenge is accepted: should AIP-14 measure platform work by document count, engineering effort, elapsed time, or delivered capability, since document count can be misleading? This corrects the docket's own defect: Package 1's supporting-evidence line presupposed document count as the metric, exactly the undecided question — that line is downgraded from trigger evidence to illustration pending metric definition. D-9 splits: D-9a defines the Platform Cost measurement basis (recommend delivered-capability + effort, reject raw document count, since one strategic decision may produce many small governance documents while a large implementation may produce few); D-9b runs the over-evolution check using the defined basis, immediately after D-9a. Package 1 stays first on the docket; what changed is that the gate must be built before it can be closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package 2 — D-5 · Ratify the enacted mission (one signature; unblocks the frame)
a_rows_sample.statement: Package 2 (D-5): ratify (or amend and ratify) the mission the machinery already enacts ('provide a reusable engineering platform that improves the development of software systems through governed engineering knowledge'). Supporting: ES-005.3's litmus, ES-006.4's harvest, the pre-positioned Platform=Adoption split, blind convergence A-1/A-2. Risk of adopting is low; risk of rejecting is that the vacancy keeps pulling constraints upward into mission-shaped misreadings. Authority: sponsor. Recommendation: ADOPT.

a_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — "VACANT" WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME I HAVE MADE THIS EXACT ERROR ... ARTIFACT ABSENCE ≠ CONCEPT ABSENCE
a_rows_sample.statement: A recurring error pattern is named: artifact absence != concept absence — looking for a document, not finding one, and declaring the concept missing. Three instances: (1) 'there is no strategic-DDD method' (it existed, unindexed); (2) 'there is no capability pattern' (it existed, FROZEN); (3) 'the Mission layer is vacant' (it exists, implicit, enacted in machinery). Strategic DDD asks why a system exists, not whether a document titled Mission Statement exists — Linux and PostgreSQL have no mission statements and unmistakable missions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE OBJECTION IS UPHELD, AND MY ERROR IS MORE SPECIFIC THAN "WRONG FRAMING" ... I mislabelled a CONSTRAINT as a MISSION, then reported a conflict between a constraint and a hypothesis — which are not comparable things
a_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's objection is upheld with a more specific diagnosis: AIP-14 was mislabelled as a mission, then reported as conflicting with a hypothesis (M-B), which are not comparable categories. The document's own prior text already disproved the label, calling AIP-14 'a cost control, not a boundary' four paragraphs after calling it a mission — both cannot be true.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Platform Lifecycle (Idea→Knowledge→PKS→Implementation→Evidence→Evolution) ... B-1 correction: software→evidence OBSERVED · back-edge n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal · KnowledgeOS→PKS n=0 · Genesis has NO route
b_rows_sample.statement: The platform lifecycle is graded link-by-link: software-to-evidence is observed; the back-edge is n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal; KnowledgeOS-to-PKS generation is n=0; and the Genesis stage has no route at all. Individual grades are confirmed; the loop as a whole remains a hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PKS Boundary — P1 method/binding/evidence ... I-7 (PKS never contains reusable method — stated AND breached)
b_rows_sample.statement: P1 defines PKS content as method/binding/evidence (cognate of Round38C-04); I-7 states a PKS never contains reusable method, yet this rule is both stated and breached in the current corpus. PKS contains artifacts; a projection claim is falsified for existing artifacts (authored, ARB-endorsed 9.9/10). The boundary rule is confirmed; the breach remains open, routed to D-8.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What does not survive — registers' contents · all records/reports · every PKS instance · Round-corpus case law · governed-registers.yaml · .claude/settings.json · election domain knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Elements that do NOT survive removal of the single product: registers' contents, all records/reports, every PKS instance, Round-corpus case law, governed-registers.yaml, .claude/settings.json, and election domain knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-6 | KnowledgeOS —creates→ PKS | UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven inside and outside
b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-6: KnowledgeOS creates PKS. External support: scaffolding/generators (Spring Initializr-class) are implementation guidance only; context-engineering platforms that auto-assemble context are adjacent. Challenge: no external instance of generating a governed knowledge space is found; internally n=0. Confidence: UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven both inside and outside the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Corrections applied to the concept matrix — PKS = Context Engineering softened
b_rows_sample.statement: Three corrections applied to the (external) concept matrix: (1) 'PKS = Context Engineering' softened to 'PKS addresses the same problem space as context engineering and extends it with governance, lifecycle, authority and engineering semantics' — not an identity claim, since the governed form has no demonstrated external instance; (2) Jansen & Bosch elevated to primary validation, since it validates the PROBLEM (knowledge vaporizes), and problem validation outranks solution fashion (Gartner-era context engineering); (3) the admission rule adopted as a standing header rule on both matrices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship pass sharpens the concept pass's conclusion: the platform's EDGES are almost all standard engineering — what is uniquely unproven is ONE edge (creates → PKS) and ONE layer name (DP-n)
b_rows_sample.statement: Aggregate result: externally supported (>=HIGH) relationships are R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, and R-2's separation; medium relationships are R-1, R-7, R-9; the unique, operationally-unproven items are R-6 (creates->PKS) and DP-n as a named layer. The distinctive bet of KnowledgeOS is now precisely locatable as R-6; everything else is either validated or a naming choice, and R-6 is exactly what the charter's gated stages and the docket's doors already refuse to assume.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — R-6 BROADENED per review: the bet is the INTEGRATION, not one edge
b_rows_sample.statement: Challenge accepted: 'KnowledgeOS is not merely a generator. It is the platform that governs the ENTIRE PKS lifecycle.' R-6 is restated as a composite chain: KnowledgeOS discovers/models/governs/generates/evolves PKS, guides PRODUCT ENGINEERING (the actor — work, not magic), which engineers software, collects evidence, and improves KnowledgeOS. The actor (product engineering) was already implicit in the work-execution progressions (P-7/P-8) and 'the producing track' as records-owner, but the composite chain had omitted it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PKS — governed, machine-readable context for AI ... "context engineering" 2025–26
b_rows_sample.statement: PKS as governed, machine-readable AI context converges with industry 'context engineering' (Gartner July 2025: 'context engineering is in, prompt engineering is out', predicted in 80% of AI tools by 2028); enterprise practice defines governed, machine-readable context any AI agent can use reliably. Challenge: the field is platform-vendor-led, young, terminology unstable. Confidence: HIGH for the need; the governance framing (authority, lifecycle, bindings) remains rarer and partially ours.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The enforcement finding (governed context + advisory capabilities) ... 86% of enterprises are assembling rich, semantically grounded context — and handing it over with no governance
b_rows_sample.statement: The industry-wide finding that 86% of enterprises assemble rich context but hand it over with no governance over agent actions, and 89% say governance is critical while ~50% have it, is convergent with this platform's own governed-context-plus-advisory-capabilities gap. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS→PKS generation (n=0) ... UNIQUE HYPOTHESIS — operational proof only
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS generating a PKS (n=0) has only adjacent external support (context-engineering platforms generate context from metadata, not the same as generating a governed PKS); it remains a unique hypothesis needing operational proof only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
b_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concept relationships — the reviewer's example chain, validated ... KnowledgeOS creates PKS contains Engineering Knowledge organized by Ontology used by Capabilities executed through Runtime produces Evidence improves KnowledgeOS
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two corrections to the Addendum's own positioning ... "KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain" ... Contradicts a DA ruling
b_rows_sample.statement: Two corrections to an Addendum's positioning: (1) 'KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain' contradicts AIP-14/DA ruling 2026-07-27 that the Election System is the Core Domain and the platform is a Supporting Subdomain; the Reference Model records only the conditional (engineering knowledge would be Core Domain if the gate opened, and it has not). (2) 'PKS is a generated projection' was falsified last round: existing PKS artifacts carry Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS, a Commission, and ARB endorsement 9.9/10 — they are authored, not derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-3 · "PKS is a projection" — FALSIFIED for every existing PKS artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: The claim 'PKS is a projection' is falsified for every existing PKS artifact: examined fields (Authority: Generated, human-asserted; Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS; a Disposition History with ARB reviewer endorsement 9.9/10; a Commission) are incompatible with a projection, which would carry authority:derived (machine-checkable), no acceptance (regenerated, not accepted), a source and regeneration command, and no Commission. A mechanical grep for authority:derived|generated across docs/pks, docs/knowledgeos, docs/implementation returns 10 files, every one a prose mention of the vocabulary, not an application of it — those paths sit outside knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include. This sharpens a prior Ontology Classification finding ('blocked in practice') to stronger: existing PKS artifacts are positively authoritative — authored, commissioned, reviewed, disposed, and accepted — incompatible with 'derived'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-4 · D-7 "Context Type" was inferred from a single instance
b_rows_sample.statement: D-7's 'Context Type' claim (one PKS instance per product) was inferred from a single instance (PublicDigit's), with zero instances generated from the type; 'one instance per product' is an observation of one case restated as a rule — a type never instantiated is a description, not a discovered construct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 5. REJECTED — falsified, with the falsifying pass cited (R-1..R-12)
b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve rejected/falsified claims listed with falsifying pass: R-1 the flat A-G category list as a meta-model; R-2 Governance/Product as kinds, Knowledge Asset as one thing; R-3 Domains own Capabilities; R-4 the single-stack hierarchy (Purpose->...->Artifact); R-5 KnowledgeOS is the Core Domain/the real product; R-6 the MVK 15-file extraction boundary; R-7 'two missions'/'mission layer vacant'/the INTENDED evidence grade; R-8 '0 of 11 responsibilities enforcing'; R-9 '0 traversals' of the evidence back-edge as a generalization; R-10 I-4 as falsified, and LG-1; R-11 a second Engineering Decision Model; R-12 'one owner => one context' as stated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The six concepts ... MISSION · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE · ENGINEERING CAPABILITY · ENGINEERING ARTIFACT · PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE · PRODUCT
b_rows_sample.statement: Six concepts defined by responsibility/lifecycle/owner/dependencies, none defined by a folder: MISSION (why the platform exists; enacted->candidate->ratified, currently enacted-unratified; owner: sponsor; depends on nothing, the root); ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (rules/methods/decisions that transfer between products; ES-006.1 ladder; owner DA for policy, sponsor+ARB for method; depends on MISSION); ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (protect exactly one invariant; observed->...->promoted; shape frozen under PGP-01..05; depends on MISSION+KNOWLEDGE); ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (carry knowledge in a representation, never the knowledge itself; statuses.yaml 8 states lint-enforced; owner field; depends on KNOWLEDGE); PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE (hold one product's concepts/language/contexts/bindings; authored today, generated as hypothesis n=0; owner product team; depends on KNOWLEDGE method + PRODUCT subject); PRODUCT (deliver business value; own delivery lifecycle; owner product team; depends on PKS + CAPABILITY).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
a_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

a_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
a_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
a_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
a_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

a_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
a_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
a_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: what there is ≠ what a discourse says there is.
a_rows_sample.statement: Quine's ontological-commitment criterion: a theory is committed only to entities that must occur among the values of its bound variables for its assertions to be true — determined by quantification, not by surface nouns/names/predicates. Argument A formalizes this: names can be paraphrased away, predicates need not name entities, but bound variables do range over entities, so ontological commitment is best assessed through what must be values of bound variables — 'a formal method for detecting hidden commitments instead of inferring them from surface vocabulary'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: theory of meaning ... versus ... theory of reference
a_rows_sample.statement: Quine separates a theory of meaning (synonymy, significance, analyticity, entailment) from a theory of reference (naming, truth, denotation, extension, values of variables), illustrated by Evening Star/Morning Star and 9/'the number of planets' — same reference, different meaning; called 'one of the strongest KnowledgeOS-relevant findings in the book'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the unit of empirical significance is the whole of science.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the analytic/synthetic dogma (every attempted definition of analyticity — logical truth, synonymy, definition, interchangeability, semantic rules, verification — eventually depends on the concept it was meant to explain) and radical reductionism (Carnap's sense-data construction of physical objects leaves 'is at' undefined rather than eliminating it, and Carnap abandoned the program). States epistemic holism: 'the unit of empirical significance is the whole of science' — the scientific system is a network whose boundary conditions are experience; experience forces change somewhere but does not uniquely determine where. Argument B: since statements form an interconnected system and experience constrains the whole, a given conflict can be accommodated by revising different parts, so 'evidence constrains a system ≠ evidence uniquely determines which proposition changes'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: revisability ≠ equal revisability.
a_rows_sample.statement: No statement is absolutely immune to revision (even logic can become a candidate for revision under sufficiently radical circumstances) but statements are not equally likely to be revised — peripheral statements (directly tied to experience) vs central statements (deep theoretical principles, logic, ontology) — giving 'revisability ≠ equal revisability'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Giorgione = Barbarelli.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argument D (referential opacity): Giorgione=Barbarelli, yet some statements containing 'Giorgione' become false under substitution of 'Barbarelli', so not every occurrence of a name is purely referential — identity of reference does not guarantee substitutability inside every context (the basis of Quine's 'referential opacity'). Argument C: dictionary definitions report antecedent usage rather than explaining why a synonymy exists, so definition normally does not explain synonymy. Argument E: quantifying into modal contexts treats necessity as a property of the object itself, requiring privileging some ways of specifying the object over others — 'something resembling Aristotelian essentialism', which Quine rejects.

a_rows_sample.anchor: truth ≠ linguistic expression of truth ... truth ≠ semantic interpretation merely because interpretation is necessary to formulate the statement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Quine introduces 'true-in-L' (truth relative to a specified language L) rather than treating a string as simply true independent of interpretation, favoring Tarski's semantic treatment as admitting formal treatment where 'analytic-in-L' does not. Distinguishes truth, truth of a predicate, naming, reference, and language-relative truth attribution, giving truth ≠ linguistic expression of truth and truth ≠ semantic interpretation-as-such.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Limit 1 — Individual empirical content is not sharply isolatable
a_rows_sample.statement: Six explicit epistemic limits: (1) individual empirical content is not sharply isolatable to one statement; (2) experience underdetermines revision; (3) synonymy lacks a satisfactory general criterion (proposed criteria become too weak, circular, or question-begging); (4) translation becomes increasingly conjectural as it moves from directly observable situations; (5) alien conceptual schemes may resist ontological translation (no firm analogue of quantification/'there is' may exist); (6) self-reference creates structural problems — a language cannot contain an unrestricted self-referential truth predicate without generating paradox.

a_rows_sample.anchor: identity in a discourse ≠ unrestricted metaphysical identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Quine's river example (river-stage a, river-stage b vs 'the river containing a and b') generalizes into 'identification of indiscernibles relative to a discourse': objects indistinguishable within a discourse can be reconstructed as one object FOR PURPOSES OF THAT DISCOURSE only, giving identity in a discourse ≠ unrestricted metaphysical identity. Also: general predicates ('is white') need not name universals the way singular terms ('the class of white things') can — 'one of the clearest anti-reification principles in the book'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Failure Case 1 — Reductionism
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven failure cases with research lessons: (1) Reductionism — physical-world statements cannot be translated into a proposed primitive experiential language, so a system should not assume every higher-level claim has a unique primitive evidential decomposition; (2) Analyticity-by-definition — 'bachelor=unmarried man' reports rather than explains synonymy; (3) Extensional-equivalence-mistaken-for-synonymy — 'creature with a heart'/'creature with kidneys' share extension but differ in meaning (same extension ≠ same meaning); (4) Referential-identity-mistaken-for-substitutability (Giorgione/Barbarelli again); (5) Predicate reification — treating predicates as class-variables introduces unneeded ontological commitment; (6) Quantification into opaque contexts (quotation, belief, necessity) can produce meaningless/unintended statements; (7) Semantic self-reference — unrestricted self-reference about truth/naming produces paradoxes (strengthened Epimenides).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Boundary A\n\nmeaning | reference
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten labeled boundaries relevant to KnowledgeOS research: meaning|reference, statement|world, evidence|total theory, predicate|entity, schema|sentence, name|object, referential|non-referential occurrence, language|metalanguage, ordinary language|formalized scientific language, identity|indiscernibility within a discourse — explicitly noted as not all absolute metaphysical boundaries; some are logical/methodological distinctions whose validity depends on context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reification should be treated as a consequential operation
a_rows_sample.statement: Six potential-relevance research directions marked RESEARCH HYPOTHESIS/QUESTION/LENS-OBSERVATION (not conclusions): evidence should not automatically be modeled as one-to-one support; revision may need explicit system-level dependency context; vocabulary normalization must not be mistaken for epistemic equivalence; ontological commitments should be auditable (what entities does a representation actually commit to); reification is a consequential operation ('when KnowledgeOS represents a distinction as a first-class object, what ontological commitment is introduced, and is it necessary?' — flagged HIGH-VALUE); semantic interpretation may have a hard epistemic boundary as observational constraint weakens.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Challenge 1 — "Every claim has identifiable evidence"
a_rows_sample.statement: Six explicit challenges to assumptions a KnowledgeOS architecture program might take for granted, each with a falsification target: (1) every claim has identifiable evidence — can a claim have a well-defined evidence boundary independent of surrounding theory?; (2) conflicting evidence identifies the wrong claim — can multiple internally coherent revision paths exist for one contradiction?; (3) canonical terminology establishes shared meaning — can two actors share a term while differing materially in inferential/referential commitment?; (4) a representation of X is effectively X — does promoting a representation to a first-class object silently change the model's ontology?; (5) identity is independent of modelling context — can two objects be indistinguishable under one model but distinguishable under another?; (6) the semantic layer can freely reason about itself — what happens when a system treats its own assertions/truth-conditions/validation-rules as ordinary objects at the same semantic level?

a_rows_sample.anchor: F1 — Unique evidence mapping
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven falsification-opportunity templates (F1-F7), each pairing a hypothesis to test against a Quinean challenge and a concrete test design: F1 unique evidence mapping (test: same observation compatible with multiple coherent revisions); F2 evidence uniquely selects rejection (test: two models accommodating the same evidence via different revised claims); F3 vocabulary convergence=semantic convergence (test: identical terminology, different extension/usage/consequences); F4 representation is ontologically neutral (test: compare predicate-only vs quantified-entity representation consequences); F5 identity is model-independent (test: two objects indistinguishable under one vocabulary, distinguishable under another); F6 self-certification is unrestricted (test: self-referential truth assertions, attempt consistency); F7 every semantic interpretation has a determinate truth value (test: translation cases with multiple observationally-compatible interpretations).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Quine provides a set of philosophical and logical arguments. He does not provide a KnowledgeOS specification.
a_rows_sample.statement: Mandatory 19-item disclaimer list of what the book does NOT establish (no KnowledgeOS architecture, domain model, bounded context, aggregate, entity/value object, Kernel capability, persistence/event model, governance mechanism, evidence schema, claim lifecycle, or ontology for KnowledgeOS; not that KnowledgeOS should adopt Quine's philosophy wholesale, that all knowledge is holistic in exactly Quine's sense, that truth is relative/merely linguistic, that semantic interpretation is impossible, that deterministic systems cannot exist, that philosophical underdetermination implies computational nondeterminism, or that DDD boundaries should follow Quine's distinctions). Final research recommendation: HIGH VALUE as a 'strong adversarial epistemological lens' — its value is destabilizing implicit assumptions (claim->evidence, term->meaning, name->object, predicate->entity, identity->substitutability, revision->one rejected claim, representation->ontology, interpretation->determinate meaning, validation->self-contained certification), not confirming an architecture; cross-lens notes flag Gödel (certification-outside-the-system), DDD (bounded-context relevance without establishing it), and deterministic assurance (epistemic underdetermination vs computational determinism as possibly different categories) as CROSS-LENS RESEARCH QUESTIONS only, with no claims made about Williamson/Davidson/Nyāya/Viveka/Dharma/Ṛta/Pāṇinian-Vāṇī from this book alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Source -> Lens -> Observation -> Architectural usefulness -> Forbidden collapse -> Candidate invariant -> Kernel verdict
b_rows_sample.statement: Quine's Word and Object is used as a deliberate stress test of the existing multi-lens research method (Source->Lens->Observation->Architectural usefulness->Forbidden collapse->Candidate invariant->Kernel verdict, not 'Philosophy->beautiful idea->kernel primitive'), reaffirming that lenses are Tier-3 conceptual inputs subordinate to EKS/PKS/AIP evidence and that lenses reveal separation requirements, not necessarily new kernel dimensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not mistake the linguistic/conceptual apparatus we use to describe reality for reality itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Quine's book structure (language/truth, evidence, translation/meaning, observation sentences, synonymy, indeterminacy, reference, vagueness, ambiguity, referential opacity, regimentation, ontology, ontic commitment) is read as a catalogue of KnowledgeOS boundary problems, centered on the caution 'do not mistake the linguistic/conceptual apparatus we use to describe reality for reality itself,' reinforcing the already-identified cross-family convergence Representation!=Knowledge, Knowledge!=Reality, Expression!=Meaning, Model!=Reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Unresolved interpretation must remain distinguishable from falsity, absence, rejection, or invalidity.
b_rows_sample.statement: Zero lens applied to Quine's indeterminacy of translation (no privileged meaning-correlation beyond publicly accessible evidence, hence no unique correct translation): 'evidence insufficient to uniquely determine X' != 'X is false', and 'no unique interpretation' != 'no interpretation exists'; candidate principle: unresolved interpretation must remain distinguishable from falsity/absence/rejection/invalidity -- verdict: strong confirmation of existing UNKNOWN-first-class Zero work, not a new kernel object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: same expression != necessarily same interpretation
b_rows_sample.statement: Vani/Expression-Meaning lens applied to Quine (language as a social art, learned through intersubjectively available cues, publicly constituted meaning rather than private fixed meaning; ambiguity vs vagueness distinguished): Expression->Interpretation->Meaning, not Expression=Meaning; same expression does not necessarily yield the same interpretation depending on context/use/linguistic system -- verdict: strong confirmation of Expression/Meaning/Interpretation/Context as separable concerns, no new dimension, mapped to existing INV-KOS-002 territory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is relationally situated; provenance must preserve how the knowledge relation arose.
b_rows_sample.statement: Vedanta/Tripuiti (Knower-Knowing-Known) lens applied to Quine's correlating-perspectives problem (different people encounter the world through different perceptual/linguistic structures; understanding another requires correlating perspectives, remaining tentative/revisable through publicly accessible evidence): Knower->observes/interprets->Evidence->Understanding->Known; supports 'Knowledge is relationally situated; provenance must preserve how the knowledge relation arose,' mapped to an existing Knowledge Relationship Integrity hypothesis; forbidden collapse: KnownObject->DetachedTruth or Claim->AutonomousTruth -- verdict: strong confirmation/deepening, no new dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the relationship topology carries meaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Nyaya/Pramana lens (Claim->Evidence->Interpretation/Hypothesis, not Claim->Truth; forbidden collapse Statement->Knowledge merely because a statement exists) and Topology lens (Quine's semantic holism: sentences form a connected fabric across science; the relationship topology itself carries meaning, so KnowledgeOS should not model isolated KnowledgeObjects with relationships as decoration) both verdict as strong confirmation of the Evidence dimension and of Knowledge Relationship Integrity respectively.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A term does not have to have one globally perfect definition to be useful.
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD/Bounded Context lens: Quine's treatment of ambiguity resolved by containing sentence/circumstances of utterance supports 'contextual semantic contract' over 'global universal meaning' -- the same word ('Authority') in Context A and Context B is possibly related but not necessarily identical; forbidden collapse: Same word->Same concept; verdict: very strong architectural support for bounded semantic contexts, explicit terminology, semantic identity, no silent vocabulary merging.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity must survive representation and state transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Aggregate/Invariant lens: Quine's tracking of objects through changing descriptions supports Identity != Properties != Description, so a new representation/description must not silently become 'new object'; principle: identity must survive representation and state transformation -- verdict: strong confirmation of Dimension Independence / Semantic Continuity, no new content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Superseded -> False
b_rows_sample.statement: Lifecycle lens: Quine's view that meanings can change when important beliefs about the world change means Knowledge->Revision->Changed understanding does not imply 'original knowledge never existed'; existing Superseded/Contested/Withdrawn/Invalid/Unknown distinctions are reinforced; forbidden collapse: Superseded->False, since a knowledge state can be historically valid within its prior epistemic context and later revised -- verdict: strong support for lifecycle/history preservation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: an LLM may generate "the architecture baseline" but KnowledgeOS must not silently assume which object that expression refers to
b_rows_sample.statement: Semantic/Identity lens: Quine's reference/identity/relative-terms/divided-reference/vagueness/ambiguity/referential-opacity material supports Term != Reference != Identity, and Reference ambiguity != Object ambiguity; concrete AI risk: an LLM generating 'the architecture baseline' must not have KnowledgeOS silently assume which object it refers to -- verdict: strong support for an explicit identity/reference boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not reify a concept merely because the language makes it convenient to talk as though it were an object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Ontology lens (Quine's 'Ontic Decision' section: nominalism/realism, ontic commitment, entia non grata, semantic ascent; canonical quantification = what the bound variables range over) produces the architectural question 'what entities does the Kernel actually commit itself to existing?' and an anti-bloat rule: 'do not reify a concept merely because the language makes it convenient to talk as though it were an object' -- e.g. Knowledge/Evidence/Claim/Meaning/Truth/Confidence/DecisionPower/Interpretation do NOT all need to become kernel entities; Useful concept != Kernel entity, Useful distinction != New dimension -- verdict: very strong confirmation, strengthening the 'smallest kernel' strategy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A representation or linguistic formulation must not be treated as uniquely determining the knowledge it expresses when the available evidence does not warrant that determination.
b_rows_sample.statement: Quine's strongest contribution formulated as a kernel boundary rule: 'A representation or linguistic formulation must not be treated as uniquely determining the knowledge it expresses when the available evidence does not warrant that determination' (UNDERDETERMINED != DETERMINED); a pipeline Evidence->possible interpretations->KnowledgeOS preserves the distinction is proposed instead of Evidence->AI interpretation->'the meaning', directly relevant to LLM-based engineering and framed as an anti-hallucination epistemic invariant: 'Interpretation is a candidate transition, not automatic knowledge admission,' with a diagram Expression->Interpretation candidate->Evidence->Compatibility->Unresolved/supported/rejected.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontological Commitment != Governance Decision Authority
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision lens applied to Quine's 'Ontic Decision': ontic decision (what ontology a theory commits to) is distinct from governance decision authority (who has authority) -- Ontological Commitment != Governance Decision Authority; KnowledgeOS may still need to preserve explicit statements like 'this model assumes entities of type X' for Architecture Decision/Knowledge Model/Ontology/Domain Model use, but kept outside the immutable kernel unless EKS evidence demands otherwise.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the most interesting result is that Quine does NOT add a new dimension
b_rows_sample.statement: Multi-lens convergence table across twelve lenses (Zero/Vani/Tripuiti/Nyaya/Topology/DDD/Identity/Lifecycle/Ontology/Siva-Sakti/Godel/Decision) each rated confirmation-strength against Quine, concluding Quine strengthens existing boundaries (Meaning!=Expression, Evidence!=Truth, Interpretation!=Reality, Identity!=Description, Unknown!=False, Context!=Universal Meaning, Model!=Ontology, Ontology!=Authority) rather than adding new dimensions (explicitly rejecting a 'QuineDimension'/'SemanticIndeterminacyDimension'/'OntologyDimension'/'TranslationDimension'); final provisional classification: six strong confirmations (C-1..C-6: Expression!=Meaning, Representation!=Knowledge, Unknown/Underdetermined!=False, Knowledge preserves provenance, Identity survives representation change, Semantic interpretation is contextual) and five architectural warnings (W-1..W-5: do not reify every useful concept; do not infer ontology from ordinary language; do not collapse ambiguity into certainty; do not treat one interpretation as uniquely warranted when evidence underdetermines it; do not confuse semantic agreement with ontological identity); explicit conclusion: probably no new constitutional invariant, Quine strengthens the existing invariant family instead -- treated as research extraction only under the current research freeze, requiring EKS/PKS/AIP validation before any constitutional law.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confirmation, not a new invariant. We should not manufacture a "Quine-Godel principle."
b_rows_sample.statement: Godel lens applied cautiously: Quine does not give Godel's incompleteness theorem itself, but supports the pattern System's descriptions != ultimate reality and Theory<->evidence rather than Theory=final truth, compatible with an existing Godel-derived external-grounding principle; explicit self-restraint: this is confirmation, not a new invariant -- 'we should not manufacture a Quine-Godel principle.' Similarly the Siva-Sakti persistent/transformable distinction (Identity/Origin/Provenance persistent; State/Expression/Assessment/Interpretation/Confidence transformable) is confirmation, not new kernel content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Quine's Word and Object is not a formal knowledge model, but a philosophical stress test for exactly the kind of hidden assumptions that can accidentally become KnowledgeOS architecture. ... Quine does not add new dimensions to the kernel. Instead, he strengthens existing boundaries and provides architectural warnings against premature reification, semantic collapse, and ontology inflation. ... Do not mistake the linguistic/conceptual apparatus we use to describe reality for reality itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Quine's Word and Object as a philosophical stress test (not a formal knowledge model) whose central challenge is: do not mistake the linguistic/conceptual apparatus used to describe reality for reality itself; converges with the project's existing principles Representation!=Knowledge, Knowledge!=Reality, Expression!=Meaning, Model!=Reality. The key finding is that Quine does not add new dimensions to the kernel -- he strengthens existing boundaries and warns against premature reification, semantic collapse, and ontology inflation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence insufficient to uniquely determine X != X is false. No unique interpretation != No interpretation exists. Unresolved interpretation must remain distinguishable from falsity, absence, rejection, or invalidity. ... same expression != necessarily same interpretation. ... Ambiguity: A term can have clearly different applications. Vagueness: The boundaries of application are unclear.
b_rows_sample.statement: Through the Zero lens, Quine's indeterminacy of translation gives: evidence insufficient to uniquely determine X != X is false, and no unique interpretation != no interpretation exists -- unresolved interpretation must remain distinguishable from falsity/absence/rejection/invalidity. Through the Vani/Expression-Meaning lens: same expression != necessarily same interpretation, and ambiguity (a term with clearly different applications) is distinguished from vagueness (unclear boundaries of application) -- expression, meaning, interpretation, and context must be preserved as separable concerns.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Understanding another person requires getting into their perspective and correlating it with one's own. ... Knowledge is relationally situated; provenance must preserve how the knowledge relation arose. ... The relationship topology carries meaning. Knowledge Relationship Integrity: relationships and transformations are architectural concerns. ... A term does not have to have one globally perfect definition to be useful. Context can determine usage. ... Resist creating a universal ontology merely because two contexts use the same word.
b_rows_sample.statement: Through the Tripuiti lens: knowledge is relationally situated (knower-evidence-understanding-known), provenance must preserve how the knowledge relation arose. Through Topology: relationship topology (support/contradiction between statements) carries meaning, supporting Knowledge Relationship Integrity as an architectural concern. Through DDD/Bounded Context: a term need not have one globally perfect definition -- context determines usage; two contexts using the same word (e.g. 'Authority') are possibly related but not necessarily identical -- resist creating a universal ontology merely because of shared vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Term != Reference != Identity. Reference ambiguity != Object ambiguity. An LLM may generate "the architecture baseline," but KnowledgeOS must not silently assume which object that expression refers to. ... Superseded != False. A knowledge state can be historically valid within its prior epistemic context and later revised.
b_rows_sample.statement: Through the Identity lens: Term != Reference != Identity, and reference ambiguity != object ambiguity -- an LLM generating an expression like 'the architecture baseline' must never have KnowledgeOS silently assume which object it refers to; explicit identity/reference boundary must be preserved. Through the Lifecycle lens: Superseded != False -- a knowledge state can be historically valid within its prior epistemic context and later revised, without the original ever having been false.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ontic Decision: What entities does the formal language actually quantify over? ... Do all of these need to become kernel entities? Answer: No. Do not reify a concept merely because the language makes it convenient to talk as though it were an object. ... Meaning: important architectural dimension but NOT necessarily a standalone kernel object.
b_rows_sample.statement: Through the Ontology lens: Quine's ontic-decision question ('what entities does the formal language actually quantify over?') is applied to KnowledgeOS candidates (Knowledge, Evidence, Claim, Meaning, Truth, Confidence, DecisionPower, Interpretation) -- answer: no, not all of these need to become kernel entities; do not reify a concept merely because language makes it convenient to talk as though it were an object. Worked through a ten-lens test on the concept 'Meaning' specifically: it is an important architectural dimension but not necessarily a standalone kernel object -- exactly the type of conclusion the lens methodology is meant to produce.

a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the historical 8-primitive candidate set K8=(E,S,V,O,P,R,Pi,A) as heterogeneous by category (mixing objects, states, occurrences, relations, normative constraints, and executable activities), not yet a homogeneous primitive type set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Could many proposed primitives be reconstructed from relations? [Identity, Supports, DerivedFrom, Supersedes, Causes as relations] This suggests Relation may be a mathematical construction mechanism, rather than a domain primitive. ... representable != semantically equivalent. ... a_rows_sample.statement: States a critical mathematical/DDD principle: a universal relation encoding can technically represent many proposed primitives (Identity, Supports, DerivedFrom, Supersedes, Causes) without preserving their specific semantics (occurrence, temporal identity, causal interpretation, replay semantics) -- representability is not proof of ontological reducibility, so Relation is reclassified as a possible mathematical construction mechanism rather than a domain primitive in its own right.

Policy -> Constraint on operations rather than Policy -> Knowledge object. ... knowledge informs action, but does not execute it. Action !in K is a strong candidate
a_rows_sample.statement: Reclassifies Policy and Action as unlikely K-primitives: Policy is better modeled as a constraint on operations rather than a knowledge object; Action is likely outside the epistemic substrate entirely (knowledge informs action but does not execute it), though this does not diminish Action's importance elsewhere in the architecture.

Structural primitives [Relation, Identity, Ordering, Time]. These should not automatically be placed in one set. Primitive Ontology != Mathematical Structure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a fundamental 2-way primitive taxonomy: ontological primitives (things the theory says exist -- Entity, Observation, Event, Proposition) versus structural primitives (mathematical organizing mechanisms -- Relation, Identity, Ordering, Time), arguing these must never be placed in one undifferentiated primitive set.

a_rows_sample.statement: Poses 4 mathematically coherent but mutually exclusive candidate ontologies for the carrier of K (Knowledge-as-primitive-object, risking circularity; Knowledge-as-structured-configuration over (objects,relations,qualifications,history), risking unproven reinvention of an earlier kernel; Knowledge-as-typed-graph, conflating representability with ontological necessity; Knowledge-as-opaque-algebraic-state, elegant for transitions but silent on the primitive-object question), none yet justified as canonical by the corpus.

b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the ideal minimal sufficient Knowledge State via a biconditional: F(H1)=F(H2) if and only if H1 and H2 are indistinguishable by every mandatory future operation -- a mathematically precise target (coarsest operationally valid equivalence) replacing the vaguer question of how many fields K should contain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Aggregate boundary must retain every piece of information required to enforce its invariants and execute its domain behaviors correctly. b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the counterexample-class methodology (from S1621) to 4 specific classes -- provenance, revision history, identity-vs-content, identity-vs-status -- each showing content-only or identity-only state abstractions fail whenever some mandatory operation actually observes the discarded distinction, with each case's status remaining conditional on which operations are mandatory.

a_rows_sample.anchor: center and periphery are job descriptions rather than fixed locations. A discipline or epistemic object can move between them depending on the task. ... ZoomIn = dynamic re-orientation of epistemic roles relative to an inquiry, rather than merely traversal.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Sher's claim that center and periphery are task-relative job descriptions rather than fixed locations to reinterpret ZoomIn not as graph traversal/reduction but as dynamic re-orientation of epistemic roles relative to an inquiry, illustrated by GitLab Runner moving from background context to active investigation target while other entities simultaneously acquire different investigative roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t != I_t. ... I_t = active structure through which the system investigates K_t. ... ZoomIn: (K_t,I_t,Q) -> I_{t+1} ... while preserving the underlying K_t unless and until fact-finding/integration changes it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new candidate Inquiry State I_t distinct from the existing E_t and K_t (E_t != K_t != I_t): K_t is what the system currently represents/attributes as stable epistemic state, I_t is the dynamic relational workspace (active questions, candidate dimensions, hypotheses, evidence targets, relational routes, active agenda, epistemic roles) through which K_t is investigated; corrects ZoomIn:K_t->I_t to ZoomIn:(K_t,I_t,Q,C)->I_{t+1}, preserving K_t unmutated unless fact-finding/integration later changes it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would remove independent ... Sher supports multiple routes and a rich network of routes, but that does not establish statistical or epistemic independence. ... this is especially important because our previous N_eff research showed how dangerous assumed independence can be.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a proposed cognitive-routes formulation that required routes to be 'independent structural, observational and evidentiary paths' to R_Q={R1,...,Rn} where routes are merely distinct (R_i != R_j), not necessarily independent (not R_i perp R_j), since routes may share instruments, observations, assumptions, models, sources, evidence, or hypotheses, explicitly connecting to the corpus's own prior N_eff research on the danger of assumed independence (over-counting correlated evidence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: no single route can assert a state determination unless cross-route warrants remain uncontradicted. That is too strong. ... Determination not-implies cross-route convergence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects a proposed requirement that determination requires uncontradicted cross-route convergence as too strong (a single exceptionally strong, direct, trustworthy source can suffice, making a second route irrelevant); Determination does not imply Cross-Route Convergence, with whether convergence is required left as inquiry-relative, depending on Determine(K,Q,C,E_C,S,R).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Freedom and Friction are not two operators ... freedom and constraint are complementary structural conditions of knowledge ... EpistemicFreedom <-> space of admissible inquiry transformations, and EpistemicFriction <-> constraints governing admissible epistemic transitions. Then Zoom-In is one possible mechanism through which freedom operates. Fact-Finding is one region where friction is imposed. Neither is identical to either principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an overly literal mapping 'Freedom=ZoomIn, Friction=FactFinding' to a more robust one: EpistemicFreedom is the space of admissible inquiry transformations and EpistemicFriction is the constraints governing admissible epistemic transitions, both complementary structural conditions of knowledge per Sher; Zoom-In is one mechanism through which freedom operates and Fact-Finding is one region where friction is imposed, but neither operator is identical to either principle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Role_t(x | Q,C,S,R) ... Background, Focus, Candidate, EvidenceTarget, Hypothesis, Constraint, Context, Alternative, Defeater, DecisionRelevant ... Entity discovery != Epistemic role discovery.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces dynamic epistemic role attribution Role_t(x|Q,C,S,R) with candidate values (Background, Focus, Candidate, EvidenceTarget, Hypothesis, Constraint, Context, Alternative, Defeater, DecisionRelevant), giving Entity discovery != Epistemic role discovery: GitLab Runner may already exist in the Knowledge Graph but only becomes important (Role transitions from Peripheral to Focus) after the egress inquiry, without being a newly discovered entity.
