a_rows_sample.anchor: Cross-Boundary Role Discovery ... versus New Dimension Discovery. Those are not the same experiment. ... Type 1 -- New entity/dimension ... Type 2 -- Existing entity, new epistemic role ... Type 3 -- New relation ... the fact finding may actually discover relational structure, not a new dimension.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines ZF2/ZF3's binary discovery test into three distinct possible outcomes for the KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 experiment: Type 1 new entity/dimension (d not-in K_t -> d in D^cand); Type 2 existing entity gaining a new epistemic role (Role_t(d|Q)=Peripheral -> Role_{t+1}(d|Q)=Focus); Type 3 new relation activated between already-known entities (Relation(d1,d2) newly instantiated), illustrated by GitLabRunner->DockerPull->Repository->Network->70GB/day being a relational discovery rather than a new-dimension discovery.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the model is not an 'anything goes' methodology: theories remain subject to veridical norms as well as other norms such as simplicity, unity, generality and fruitfulness. ... Open exploration != Unconstrained acceptance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Sher's foundational-holism methodology (rejecting rigid predetermined grounding order without permitting 'anything goes'; theories remain subject to veridical and other norms such as simplicity/unity/generality/fruitfulness) as philosophical justification for why open-ended Zoom-In followed by evidence/assessment/determination is architecturally correct, whereas open-ended Zoom-In leading directly to automatic knowledge would not be: Open exploration != Unconstrained acceptance, i.e. EpistemicFreedom + EpistemicFriction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sher: How can holism remain structured? versus Zero: How can reduction preserve required structure? These are complementary research questions. But they are not dual operators mathematically yet.
a_rows_sample.statement: Draws a structural parallel (not a proof) between Sher's question (how can a complex holistic knowledge system remain structured rather than becoming amorphous) and the Zero Lens question (how can reduction preserve required structure), explicitly noting these are complementary but not yet mathematically dual operators.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the immediate priority remains the already-authorized KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01: determine whether the original ZF2/ZF3/ZF5 experiment actually detects dimension discovery, relational discovery, or merely traversal behavior. That distinction should be an adjudication issue for the existing experiment, not a reason to alter its frozen protocol.
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes that the Sher-derived Type-1/2/3 discovery typology should be used as a post-execution adjudication lens for the already-frozen KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 protocol (distinguishing dimension discovery, relational discovery, or mere traversal behavior in the results) rather than as grounds to alter the frozen experimental design; registers KR-EPISTEMIC-FRICTION-LENS-2026-09 (FR-A Epistemic Freedom, FR-B Epistemic Friction, FR-C Dynamic Epistemic Roles, FR-D Structured Holism) in the master governance ledger alongside the other external lenses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sher begins with a dual condition: Epistemic Freedom + Epistemic Friction ... freedom to ask questions ... choose subjects ... But it simultaneously requires friction -- constraints imposed by both the world and the cognitive/normative structure of inquiry.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Sher's foundational dual condition Epistemic Freedom + Epistemic Friction as the central idea of the book: knowledge requires both freedom (asking questions, choosing methods, designing experiments, revising theories) and friction (constraints from the world and from cognitive/normative structure), mapped onto Epistemic Agency -> ZoomIn -> discover dimensions -> Fact-Finding as 'freedom to investigate under epistemic constraints'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: knowledge should not be modeled as a simple bottom-up chain ... multiple knowledge elements can stand in rich relationships with one another and with reality ... Q_t^DAG subseteq I_t ... I_t = (Q_t, D_t^cand, H_t, E_t^target, R_t^rel, A_t^agenda, C_t, S_t) where the DAG is only the decomposition structure, not the entire inquiry topology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Sher's rejection of strict foundational linearity in favor of relational/network holism to argue that the Inquiry State's question decomposition should be only one component of a richer tuple I_t=(Q_t,D_t^cand,H_t,E_t^target,R_t^rel,A_t^agenda,C_t,S_t), with Q_t^DAG subseteq I_t rather than I_t=Q_t^DAG.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Revisable != Arbitrarily Revisable ... universal revisability does not mean arbitrary revisability. A theory can remain open to revision while requiring compelling reasons for revision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Sher's point that universal revisability does not license arbitrary revisability (revisions require compelling reasons to constitute progress rather than capricious change), proposing Revisable != Arbitrarily Revisable as a candidate KnowledgeOS invariant connecting to Factivity, Evidence Assessment, Epistemic Standards, Revision, Provenance, and Governance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a theory must have enough substantive content to actually encounter constraints. An empty or trivial theory is effectively frictionless ... Research Claim must expose itself to possible failure. ... O-F* can be understood as one engineering realization of a broader epistemic-friction principle.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extracts Sher's substantiveness requirement (a theory must have enough content to actually encounter constraints; an empty/trivial theory is frictionless) as an explicit philosophical rationale (the analysis's own inference, not Sher's) for the corpus's existing O-F* estimand-nondegeneracy gate: a research claim must expose itself to possible failure, connecting to the discovered O-F* near-misses in KR-ZOOM-03/KR-ZOOM-OUT-01.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FR-SHER-1 -- Epistemic Friction ... FR-SHER-7 -- Substantive Constraint ... STRUCTURAL CORRESPONDENCE MATRIX (SHER EPISTEMIC FRICTION <-> KNOWLEDGEOS ARCHITECTURE) ... Cognitive Route -> Candidate Path/Evidence Route (R_i) ... Model Redundancy/Elimination -> Zero Lens Elimination Test
a_rows_sample.statement: Registers the original seven-item FR-SHER-1..FR-SHER-7 lens (Epistemic Friction, Holistic Grounding, Dynamic Epistemic Position, Multiple Cognitive Routes, Revision with Continuity, Open-Ended Inquiry, Substantive Constraint) and an explicit Sher-to-KnowledgeOS correspondence matrix mapping Cognitive Route->candidate evidence route R_i, Epistemic Freedom->ZoomIn/Agency, Epistemic Friction->Evidence Assessment & Determination, Holistic Network Relations->R^rel_t, Dynamic Contextual Role->Role_t(x|Q), Universal Revisability->K_t transitions ([FROZEN] Theory v1.2 core), Non-Arbitrary Constraint->epistemic standard/warrant W_t ([FROZEN] core), and Model Redundancy/Elimination->Zero Lens.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_1: Network Telemetry Route ... R_2: Application Log Route ... R_3: Artifact & Package Route ... R_4: Infrastructure & CI/CD Route ... GitLab Runner Container Cache is instantly re-oriented from peripheral background context to the central target of inquiry ... the inquiry converges when evidence across distinct cognitive routes cross-verifies.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the most operationally concrete worked example in the whole Sher thread: four competing cognitive routes for the Nexus 70GB/day egress anomaly (R1 Network Telemetry: NAT/proxy masking friction; R2 Application Log: missing-header friction; R3 Artifact/Package: archive-decompression friction; R4 Infrastructure/CI-CD: detached-job friction), each with named domain hypotheses, observational channels, and warrants; illustrates ZoomIn's role-reorientation (GitLab Runner Container Cache moving from peripheral background to central investigation target once R3 evidence implicates it) and a cross-route consistency requirement for determination Delta K_t=f(F_1,...,F_n) where Consistency(F_i,F_j)=True (later corrected in this same thread to make convergence non-mandatory).

b_rows_sample.anchor: At every observation you have infinite possible dimensions to be discovered. ... the projection to different observation field by zooming in can be the fact finding process about an event or process
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that at every observation there is a potentially unbounded discoverable dimension space, and that zooming into different observation fields to find causes/situations/sources of an event constitutes the fact-finding process about that event, using a Nexus egress=70GB/day example with potentially relevant dimensions {Network,Backup,Repository,CI/CD,GitLabRunner,Configuration,Users,Traffic,Logs,Storage,Time,Security,Deployment,...}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D_t subseteq D* and potentially D* -> open/unbounded discovery space. ... Don't claim literally that the dimensions are mathematically infinite unless the model establishes such a domain. Instead: the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the informal 'infinite possible dimensions' claim to a precise formulation: the currently represented dimensions D_t are a subset of a potentially discoverable D*, and the discoverable dimension space is open-ended relative to the current representation (D_t -Inquiry-> D_{t+1}), without D_{t+1} necessarily being a superset of D_t since dimensions can also become irrelevant/superseded/out-of-contract.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q) -> FocusedInquirySpace ... The dimensions explored by Zoom-in need not have been present in the original observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates Zoom-in from the earlier K_t->Subgraph(K_t) (found inadequate) to ZoomIn(K_t,O,Q)->FocusedInquirySpace, where focus is not deletion of the rest of K_t and the explored dimensions need not have been present in the original observation -- a discovery operation rather than a within-representation detail operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Graph Traversal != Epistemic Investigation ... KnowledgeGraph = representational substrate ... ZoomIn = inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates Graph Traversal (a Knowledge Graph can represent an edge like GitLabRunner-causes->Egress) from Epistemic Investigation (KnowledgeOS asks why the edge should exist, requiring Evidence, Provenance, Time, AlternativeHypotheses, Assessment, Determination), giving KnowledgeGraph=representational substrate while ZoomIn=inquiry-directed exploration over that substrate and its discoverable extensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t) = Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t) rather than simply FocusedState -> OriginalState. ... this is exactly why our previous Zoom-out experiments struggled: we were trying to classify Zoom-out before clearly separating restoration from integration.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Zoom-out from mere restoration (FocusedState->OriginalState) to Integration: ZoomOut(F_t,K_t)=Integrate(Finding,F_t,K_t), diagnosing that prior Zoom-out experiments struggled because they attempted to classify Zoom-out before separating restoration from integration.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn = search for potentially relevant structure ... Zero = test eliminability of represented structure. ... ZoomIn discovers and Zero tests.
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes Zoom-in and Zero as complementary operations relative to the same (Q,C,Pi,S): Zoom-in searches for potentially relevant structure (discovers), Zero tests eliminability of represented structure (tests); a candidate pipeline ZoomIn->ExpandedRepresentation->ZeroLens->RelevantSubspace->FactFinding is proposed but explicitly not assumed to be a fixed order, tagged [PROP] not axiom.

b_rows_sample.anchor: projection to different observation field ... I would be careful. ... Unless we have pi^2=pi or an appropriate semantic projection definition, don't call every Zoom-in a projection. Use inquiry-relative view transformation ... or focus transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against calling every Zoom-in operation a mathematical 'projection' unless an established idempotent projection structure (pi^2=pi) or semantic-projection definition is demonstrated; recommends 'inquiry-relative view transformation' or 'focus transformation' as neutral terminology, consistent with the Zero Algebra lesson to discover the algebra rather than impose it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn: Where should I investigate? EpistemicAgency: What should I do next? FactFinding: What does the evidence establish? ZoomOut: How does the finding change the broader state?
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates four distinct research questions into a coherent architecture: ZoomIn (where should I investigate), Epistemic Agency (what should I do next), Fact Finding (what does the evidence establish), Zoom-out (how does the finding change the broader state), combined into Observation->Relevance->ZoomIn->DimensionDiscovery->FactFinding->Determination->ZoomOut->Integration->K_{t+1} with a feedback loop from DimensionDiscovery back to NewObservation->NewZoomIn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 ... ZF1 -- Context preservation ... ZF2 -- Dimension expansion ... ZF3 -- Cross-boundary discovery ... ZF4 -- Determination dependence ... ZF5 -- Investigation != determination ... ZF6 -- Zoom-out integration ... ZF7 -- Resource/agency interaction
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-2026-09 with seven candidate hypotheses: ZF1 ZoomIn(K_t,Q) does not imply Delete(K_t); ZF2 D_t subseteq D_{t+1} can occur through investigation; ZF3 a relevant dimension need not be contained in the initial observation's representation; ZF4 newly discovered dimensions can change Determine(Q); ZF5 ZoomIn != Determine; ZF6 a finding discovered during Zoom-in can modify the broader state; ZF7 the next investigated dimension depends on K,Q,Delta,Resources,Context,Contract,Risk.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Backup -> large transfer, GitLab Runner -> large transfer, Replication -> large transfer ... the system must not say I found GitLab Runner, therefore GitLab Runner is the cause. ... No Determination Without Alternative Space.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses a multi-cause Nexus-egress failure case (Backup, GitLab Runner, and Replication all plausibly producing large transfer) to argue against single-hypothesis-collapse ('I found X, therefore X is the cause'), requiring the full hypothesis set H_Q to undergo Evidence Assessment before Determination, stated as the principle 'No Determination Without Alternative Space.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: O_t -> ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q) -> D_t subseteq D_{t+1} -> Acquire -> Assess -> Determine -> ZoomOut(Finding,K_t) -> K_{t+1} ... Terminology Correction: View Transformation vs. Projection
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a four-level Decoupled Dimensional Expansion & Integration Pipeline (1. Observation Entry O_t={d_0}; 2. Dimensional Discovery ZoomIn(K_t,O_t,Q)->D_t subseteq D_{t+1}; 3. Fact-Finding Acquire->Assess->Determine; 4. Integration ZoomOut(Finding,K_t)->K_{t+1}), and replaces the term 'projection' with 'Inquiry-Directed View Transformation' to avoid assuming idempotence (pi^2=pi) prior to empirical discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t <=_O Focus(K_t,Q) where <=_O means that the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable. ... ZF1 -- Context Preservation: Zoom-In changes inquiry focus without itself removing or invalidating surrounding Knowledge State.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF1's undefined comparison ZoomIn(K_t,Q)!=Delete(K_t) to K_t<=_O Focus(K_t,Q), where <=_O means the focused view does not make previously available contract-relevant observations unavailable, avoiding accidentally turning Zoom-In into an undefined representation-theoretic operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Discovery of a dimension != acceptance of that dimension into Knowledge State. ... exactly analogous to your existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge. ... ZF2 -- Dimensional Expansion: Inquiry-directed investigation can introduce candidate explanatory dimensions not represented in the initial active representation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF2's D_t subset D_{t+1} (which conflates dimension discovery with state evolution) by introducing D_t^cand as candidate dimensional space distinct from D_t^rep (accepted into Knowledge State), giving D_t^rep subseteq D_{t+1}^cand and a later integration D_{t+1}^cand -> D_{t+1}^rep, analogous to the existing Candidate != Determined != Knowledge chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(I_t) ... ZF3 currently risks becoming tautological ... GitLab Runner may already exist somewhere in the Knowledge Graph but not be connected to the egress observation. That is not dimensional discovery.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF3's under-specified d* not-in Rep(O_t) (risking tautology) by distinguishing not-observable-in-O_t, not-represented-in-K_t, and genuinely-discovered-during-investigation, requiring d* not-in Rep_active(O_t,K_t) AND d* in Discover(investigation trace I_t), noting a dimension already present elsewhere in the graph but unconnected to the observation does not count as dimensional discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) != Determine(K'_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) with K'_t = Expand(K_t,d*). ... Otherwise a change in determination could simply result from changing standards, evidence, inquiry, or reasoning regime.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF4 (Determine(Q|D_t)!=Determine(Q|D')) to hold the full determination signature Q,C,EC,S,R fixed and intervene only on the discovered dimensional representation, giving Determine(K_t,...)!=Determine(K'_t,...) with K'_t=Expand(K_t,d*), so the change is attributable to dimensional expansion alone rather than confounded with standards/evidence/inquiry/reasoning-regime changes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Zoom-In that discovers ... has succeeded even if Fact-Finding concludes: Cause remains underdetermined. So: DiscoverySuccess not-implies Determination should probably become a candidate invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Retains and operationally sharpens ZF5 (ZoomIn:(K_t,O_t,Q)->D^cand versus FactFinding:(D^cand,E,H_Q,M,S)->Standing->Determination), proposing the candidate invariant DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination: Zoom-In can succeed in surfacing candidates even when Fact-Finding concludes the cause remains underdetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomOut should not be defined as ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t. That would recreate the old restoration model. Instead: ZoomOut(F,K_t) = Integrate(K_t,F) -> K_{t+1} ... ZoomOut = integration of finding rather than: ZoomOut = inverse(ZoomIn).
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly forbids defining Zoom-Out as the inverse of Zoom-In (ZoomOut(ZoomIn(K_t))=K_t would recreate the old restoration model); Zoom-Out is Integrate(K_t,F)->K_{t+1} where F may contain newly discovered dimensions, assessed evidence, determined relationships, rejected hypotheses, unresolved alternatives, provenance, and temporal information, so K_{t+1}!=K_t may occur even though Zoom-In itself deleted nothing.

b_rows_sample.anchor: d* in ArgMax_{d in D^cand} E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d) as a candidate agency policy, not a kernel law. ... ZoomIn != Agency. Agency selects the next investigation; Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects ZF7's dimension-selection formula (which assumed Adeq is measurable, candidate dimensions are comparably valued, costs are scalarizable, and an argmax exists) to an explicitly candidate agency policy d* in ArgMax_{d}E[V_Delta(d|K,Q,C,S,R)]/Cost(d), not a kernel law, reaffirming ZoomIn != Agency (Agency selects the next investigation, Zoom-In executes the inquiry-directed focus).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZF8 -- Representation Boundary Non-Closure ... An initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions. ... ZF3 asks: Can the relevant dimension cross the initial boundary? ZF8 asks: Is the initial dimensional representation itself epistemically non-closed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds ZF8 (Representation Boundary Non-Closure): the initial observation representation must not be assumed to contain all relevant explanatory dimensions, distinguished from ZF3 (can a relevant dimension cross the boundary) by asking instead whether the initial representation is itself epistemically non-closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zoom-In != Zero != Fact-Finding ... Determination ... Zoom-Out ... Epistemic Agency ... This is much more promising than trying to make Zoom-In or Zoom-Out kernel primitives.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a six-way functional separation as the architectural conclusion: Zoom-In (expand/search the inquiry space) != Zero Lens (determine what can be eliminated while preserving contract) != Fact-Finding (establish what evidence supports) != Determination (establish what can be decided under the epistemic regime) != Zoom-Out (integrate finding into broader state) != Epistemic Agency (select what to investigate/do next); recommends testing ZF2+ZF3+ZF5 first as the foundational experiment before the rest of the architecture is tested.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contr(p,K) iff Phi_conflict(p,P(p),K) = true. Where Phi_conflict evaluates positive under any of: Direct Negation Intersection (p and not-p asserted within identical context bounds); Inference Rule Clash (two derivation paths yield mutually exclusive conclusions via valid deduction); Source Provenance Incompatibility (mutually distrusted authority frames support opposing claims without a resolving meta-frame); Scalar Support Overlap (FDE Symptom): S+(p)>=tau_accept+ and S-(p)>=tau_refute-.
a_rows_sample.statement: Redefines Contr structurally: Contr(p,K) holds iff a conflict predicate Phi_conflict evaluates true over p, its provenance DAG P(p), and the knowledge state K, positive under any of four distinct conflict types -- Direct Negation Intersection, Inference Rule Clash, Source Provenance Incompatibility, or Scalar Support Overlap -- explicitly relabeling the last (the old S+/S- threshold test) as merely one observable FDE 'symptom' of conflict rather than the definition itself, correcting the earlier over-identification of Contr with scalar FDE arithmetic.

type_signature.domain: proposition p, provenance DAG P(p), knowledge state K

a_rows_sample.anchor: Scope(Contr(p),Gamma) = {p} union Dependents(p,K) union ConflictingSources(p,P(p)) ... EVal(q,K,Q,Gamma) piecewise: ContradictionTrapped if q in Scope(Contr(p),Gamma), else StandardEVal ... Non-Explosion Principle: forall q not-in Scope(Contr(p),Gamma), EVal(q,K,Q,Gamma) is completely immune to the conflict at p.
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the parameterized isolation scope Scope(Contr(p),Gamma) (conflict node plus its dependents plus conflicting sources) and evaluation behavior under isolation: queries inside the scope return ContradictionTrapped, queries outside execute StandardEVal completely unaffected -- restated as the Non-Explosion Principle, now marked as a [PROPOSED] parameterized candidate rather than an immutable universal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSERT(p,v,src) appends new ground node with initial standing and source provenance ... LINK(n1,n2,rel) appends directed relational edge ... REVISE(p,p',reason) appends p', adds supersedes link p'->p, leaving p immutable ... RETRACT(p,scope) appends retraction tombstone node linked to p; adjusts active standing ... ISOLATE(p,boundary) constructs Epistemic Firewall F(p) blocking graph propagation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives each of the five O_core primitives a formal signature and state-transformation effect: ASSERT appends a new ground node with initial standing/provenance; LINK appends a directed relational edge; REVISE appends a new claim with a SUPERSEDES link to the old claim, which remains immutable; RETRACT appends a tombstone node and adjusts active standing rather than deleting; ISOLATE constructs an Epistemic Firewall blocking graph propagation for a proposition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Final Kernel Reduction Matrix: With the execution of Closure Packages C1 through C4, the KnowledgeOS Kernel reduction is complete ... C1 Truth & Evidence Space ... C2 Contradiction & Scope ... C3 Operations Algebra ... C4 Equivalence & Adequacy ... PACKAGE C4 FALSIFICATION TEST: PASSED (EA and Equivalence verified)
a_rows_sample.statement: Issues the file's culminating claim: 'With the execution of Closure Packages C1 through C4, the KnowledgeOS Kernel reduction is complete', supported by a final matrix summarizing each package's formal result and a Python test (test_c4_adequacy_and_equivalence) reported PASSED for both Executable Adequacy and Semantic Equivalence on a small synthetic three-operation example; status self-declared [RATIFIED -- FINAL CLOSURE PACKAGE] for C4 specifically, versus [RATIFICATION CANDIDATE] for C2 and C3 in the same file.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the document silently introduces a quantitative theory: S+,S- in R_>=0 and thresholds tau. We have not established: how weights are assigned, how source reliability enters, whether weights are comparable, how independent evidence aggregates, how correlated evidence is handled, what the threshold means, whether threshold changes are semantic or contextual. This is exactly where our earlier composition experiments remained underdetermined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State(p) piecewise: ACCEPTED if S+(p)>=tau+ and S-(p)<tau- ; REFUTED if S+(p)<tau+ and S-(p)>=tau- ; CONTRADICTION if S+(p)>=tau+ and S-(p)>=tau- ; UNDERDETERMINED if S+(p)<tau+ and S-(p)<tau- ... Property 1 Non-Destructive Composition: EVal(p,R1 union R2,C).Standing = (S+_R1+S+_R2, S-_R1+S-_R2). No evidence combination operation is permitted to subtract or cancel out opposing support dimensions directly. Property 2 Non-Monotonicity of Standing ... Property 3 Scope Isolation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Derives a four-way EpistemicState (ACCEPTED, REFUTED, CONTRADICTION, UNDERDETERMINED) from Standing via context-defined thresholds tau+/tau-, and states three operational laws: Non-Destructive Composition (standings from unioned state graphs ADD rather than cancel: no combination operation may subtract opposing support dimensions), Non-Monotonicity of Standing (new evidence updates Standing without invalidating prior evaluation history), and Scope Isolation (a CONTRADICTION state in one context does not force CONTRADICTION in an orthogonal context).

b_rows_sample.anchor: SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 Compliance if it passes two core verification constraints: 1. Tuple Completeness: Querying any claim p returns all 5 fields of the evaluation tuple without null/empty dropouts on valid data. 2. Standing Independence: Injecting S- does not alter S+, proving no scalar subtraction or net collapse occurred. SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 is hereby RATIFIED as the formal Evaluation Semantics for KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Issues a self-contained ratification sign-off for SPEC-EVAL-2026-v1.0 conditioned on two compliance checks (Tuple Completeness -- all 5 EVal fields always returned; Standing Independence -- injecting S- does not alter S+), declaring it 'hereby RATIFIED as the formal Evaluation Semantics for KnowledgeOS' -- the fourth self-contained ratification act in this single file, none tied to an external governance-ledger record.

b_rows_sample.anchor: tau = <tau_accept+, tau_refute-, tau_margin, omega_prov> ... d_state(E,tau) piecewise: DETERMINED_TRUE if S+>=tau_accept+ and S-<tau_refute- and (S+-S-)>=tau_margin ; DETERMINED_FALSE symmetric; DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION if S+>=tau_accept+ and S->=tau_refute- ; UNDERDETERMINED if both below threshold ; AMBIGUOUS otherwise.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the decision threshold vector tau=<tau_accept+,tau_refute-,tau_margin,omega_prov> and the piecewise d_state mapping from Standing (S+,S-) and tau into five discrete determination states (DETERMINED_TRUE, DETERMINED_FALSE, DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION, UNDERDETERMINED, AMBIGUOUS), requiring a margin of dominance |S+-S-|>=tau_margin to resolve TRUE/FALSE ambiguity.

States as a constitutional distinction that EVal must not be identified with a simple Standing-to-four-state function.

Replaces it with the weaker, correct statement: evidence addition MAY change evaluation; it need not -- with the specific behavior (monotone/non-monotone/revisionary/retracting/context-sensitive) to be investigated per evidence-operator rather than asserted as a universal law.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 'monotonic delta' claim is mathematically misleading ... Nodes(K_t) subseteq Nodes(K_{t+1}) ... is not the same thing as monotonic knowledge. a_rows_sample.anchor: Contract 1: ASSERT ... Preconditions: p not-in V(K_t) OR p in V(K_t) with status RETRACTED. Postconditions: p in V(K_{t+1}) ACTIVE ... a_rows_sample.statement: Gives each of the five O_core primitives a complete precondition/postcondition/failure-semantics contract with named failure outcomes not present in earlier versions: ASSERT returns NO_OP_DUPLICATE on a redundant active node; LINK raises UNMAPPED_NODE_EXCEPTION (aborting with no state change) if either endpoint is missing; REVISE raises REVISION_ON_RETRACTED_NODE_ERROR if the target is already retracted; RETRACT sets standing to fully-ambiguous <0,0,1.0> and returns NO_OP_NOT_FOUND if the target does not exist; ISOLATE defaults to single-node scope if no explicit scope is given.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 equiv_sem^{Q,Gamma,O} K2 iff forall q in Q, forall o in O, Det(EVal(K1,q,Gamma),q,Gamma) = Det(EVal(K2,q,Gamma),q,Gamma) ... Non-Commutativity (General Case): o2 o o1 != o1 o o2, example RETRACT(p) o ASSERT(p) != ASSERT(p) o RETRACT(p). Orthogonal Commutativity: if Target(o1) intersect Target(o2) = empty, then o2 o o1 equiv_sem o1 o o2. Idempotency of Isolation: ISOLATE(p) o ISOLATE(p) equiv_sem ISOLATE(p).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines parameterized semantic equivalence K1 equiv_sem^{Q,Gamma,O} K2 as agreement of Det(EVal(...)) results for every query and operation, and specifies three composition-algebra properties: Non-Commutativity in the general case (with a concrete counterexample, RETRACT-after-ASSERT differs from ASSERT-after-RETRACT), Orthogonal Commutativity (operations with disjoint targets commute up to semantic equivalence), and Idempotency of Isolation (isolating the same proposition twice is semantically equivalent to isolating it once).

a_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Prior-family acknowledgement in Step 209: NONE. ZERO.
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-i): machine grep of Step 209 for the corpus's prior invariant-naming families (INV-n, AFR-0n, GT-0n, GG-/GE-/GC-/GA-, IR-0n, CM-0n, LA-0n, AAI, PLP, and bare C1-C7/S1-S6/K1-K7/V1-V10/I1-I20) finds zero matches of any kind; Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208, in its opening line) and nothing else. The prior families are independently confirmed present and locatable in the corpus (AFR-0* in 3 files, INV-1* in 1, GT-0* in 1, AAI in 2, PLP in 1, IR-0* in 1, CM-0* in 1, LA-0* in 1); none is reconciled, mapped, superseded, or mentioned. Also uncited: Step 048 (global invariants), Step 092 (invariant preservation), Step 025N (a prior 'algebra' -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra), Step 091 (safety/liveness ground for Step 209's own Sections 209.35-37).

a_rows_sample.anchor: IS IT AN ALGEBRA? NO.
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-ii): an algebra requires a carrier set, closed operations, and laws. Step 209 supplies none of the three properly: the carrier ('an invariant') is never typed and is used interchangeably as a predicate on states (I(s)), a proposition (I_1 ∧ I_2), and a named object (I_identity) within one file; the only operation is unqualified conjunction (I_global = AND of I_i), imported from propositional logic and never defined on the carrier; no laws are stated (no associativity, commutativity, identity element, closure, absorption, or distributivity). The only other algebraic-looking object, A = {C,I,S,T,R} (Section 209.34), is ill-typed: written in set-brace notation for what the surrounding text treats as an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, so it cannot support the componentwise access the text assumes. Verdict: Step 209 is a taxonomy plus a conjunction, mislabelled an algebra -- a useful, well-organised three-level taxonomy of invariants (local/context/system), not an algebra.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Satisfiability is declared and never tested
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.32 declares that I_global = AND(I_1..I_n) 'is only valid if the invariants are jointly satisfiable' and states SAT(I_1 ∧ I_2 ∧ ... ∧ I_n) 'is an important next mathematical direction' but never tests it: COMPUTABILITY verdict DEFINED, not CONSTRUCTIBLE (the I_i are natural-language predicates, not formulas in any decidable logic), not COMPUTED, not TESTED. Section 209.33 constructs a hypothetical unsatisfiable pair (Action->Approval vs Action->ImmediateExecution) and does not check it against the actual I_KOS set.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
a_rows_sample.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: I_L(A), I_C(BC), I_S(System); Execution cannot manufacture authority; Semantic Laundering; I_KOS 8-set
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 ('Invariant Algebra') stratifies invariants into local/context/system levels (I_L, I_C, I_S); defines Verified(E)⇒Provenance(E)∧Integrity(E), Valid(A)⇒EvidenceBasis(A)∧ModelVersion(A), Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D), Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X) boxed as 'Execution cannot manufacture authority'; an epistemic partial order and knowledge lattice; 'Semantic Laundering' (a downstream context losing provenance/uncertainty of an upstream claim and treating the result as stronger than warranted); 'Determinism != Correctness'; architecture-as-CSP A={C,I,S,T,R}; safety properties P1-P4 and liveness properties L1-L2; and the boxed 8-member frozen set I_KOS={I_identity,I_version,I_provenance,I_temporal,I_epistemic,I_authority,I_decision,I_execution}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION VERDICT: REFRAMES; DEFINITION VERDICT: PARTIALLY_CLEAR with one ILL-TYPED object
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 reframes scattered '!=' observations into a stratified system but does not resolve the SAT question it raises nor reconcile with any prior invariant family. CLEAR: the three-level stratification, Executed(X)⇒Authorized(X), semantic laundering, determinism!=correctness. ILL-TYPED: A={C,I,S,T,R} uses set-brace notation for an ordered heterogeneous 5-tuple, which has no positional structure though the surrounding text requires componentwise access. NOT_DEFINED: the type of 'an invariant' itself, used as a predicate on states, a proposition, and a named object within one file. INCOMPLETE: I_KOS's eight members are one-word labels with no formulas, unlike the file's own worked examples.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 209.32 (conjunction written as established, satisfiability tested after, never run)
a_rows_sample.statement: I_global = AND_{i=1}^n I_i (Section 209.32) is written as an established equality, and the satisfiability precondition (SAT test) is stated only afterward, as future work, never run. If the I_i are not jointly satisfiable then I_global is identically false and the boxed I_global = AND(I_KOS) is an assertion of contradiction. Everything downstream that treats I_global as a satisfiable target -- Step 210's matrix, Step 211's AAG, Step 212's gap register -- is conditional on repairing this. Secondary: Section 209.14's determinism claim (SameState+SameCommand⇒SameDomainResult) is used inconsistently as assumption, requirement, and derived property without saying which.

a_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: nothing reaches CONSTRUCTIBLE; TEST VERDICT: NOT_EXECUTED
a_rows_sample.statement: I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is DEFINED; I_KOS's 8 members are DEFINED but not INPUTS_KNOWN (unformalized); SAT(I_1∧...∧I_n) and SAT(A) are DEFINED but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (natural-language predicates, no decidable-logic encoding, and A is ill-typed); P1-P4/L1-L2 are DEFINED, self-described as 'candidates, not yet final requirements'; delta(A_t,c), Pre, Post are DEFINED with no aggregate instantiated. The file's own Section 209.34 concedes 'this is not yet a complete formal verification system.' Test verdict NOT_EXECUTED -- P1-P4 are called 'excellent candidates for deterministic assurance tests', none written or run.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG; MEASUREMENT VERDICT: MIXED with a good refusal and a violation
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's separation of probabilistic inference from deterministic governance (Section 209.15), Determinism!=Correctness (Section 209.16), InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence (Section 209.17, a genuinely important distinction between model misspecification and wide posteriors), HighUncertainty!=KnownIncorrect / LowUncertainty!=GuaranteedTrue (Section 209.18), and ObservedCorrelation⇏Causation (Section 209.29, uncited against Step 074) are all statistically correct. Measurement: Section 209.21 correctly declines to universalize a total order on epistemic strength (Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported, 'should not be interpreted as a universal total ordering') -- a good refusal -- but Section 209.25 then writes S(T(x))>S(x), a strict comparison requiring exactly the order just declined, four pages later with no reconciliation. KnowledgeState=(EvidenceStrength,Consistency,Uncertainty) is correctly presented as a partial order/lattice admitting incomparable elements, with no arithmetic attempted (correct). I_global=AND(I_KOS) conjoins a nominal set of one-word labels that are not propositions -- a type gap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: STRONG on structure, WEAK on consistency boundaries; UL: 'Semantic Laundering' the best-defined new term
a_rows_sample.statement: The I_L/I_C/I_S stratification is textbook-correct and the clearest statement of the aggregate/context/system-invariant distinction in the corpus; Section 209.6 correctly identifies Decision.AssessmentRef⇒Resolvable(AssessmentRef) as crossing aggregates, but DDD's standard remedy (a consistency-boundary decision -- strong vs eventual consistency, process manager/saga) is never offered, despite the corpus already containing '# Step 166 — Process Managers, Sagas' (uncited). 'Semantic Laundering' (Section 209.24: 'a downstream context loses the provenance or uncertainty of an upstream claim and treats the transformed result as stronger than its source warrants') is judged the single best-defined new term in the band; against this, I_KOS's eight members enter the language as labels without definitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS: conjunction cannot express the dependency graph the file itself draws
a_rows_sample.statement: Stated assumptions: invariants are propositions closed under AND; a single global conjunction is the right composition; governance transitions can be made deterministic. Hidden: that conjunction is the only composition operator needed, despite Section 209.31's dependency graph showing invariants depending on one another (a relation AND cannot express) -- Sections 209.31 and 209.32 are structurally inconsistent, a dependency graph is not a flat conjunction (Internal Contradiction #B); that the I_i are mutually independent, contradicted by 209.31; that I_KOS's eight members cover the space, with no completeness argument (Step 210 immediately produces 15). Undefined symbols: Integrity(E), EvidenceBasis(A), AssessmentMethod(A), DecisionBasis(D), ApplicablePolicy(D), Resolvable(.), Traceable(D,Basis(D)), Basis(D), S(x), EvidenceStrength/Consistency components, Eventually(.), and every member of I_KOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 209
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: the three-level invariant stratification; Semantic Laundering; Determinism!=Correctness; InvalidModelApplication!=LowConfidence; Execution cannot manufacture authority; identity continuity independent of state continuity; the safety/liveness lens; the insight that a constitution should constrain invariants, not technologies. Does not survive: the title (it is not an algebra); A={C,I,S,T,R} as typed; SAT(A) as computable; I_global=AND(I_KOS) as a verified-satisfiable object (unverified, and structurally at odds with the dependency graph of Section 209.31); S(T(x))>S(x) as a well-formed comparison.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Evidence/Test ordering is reversed between files, and Step 210's own boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own tuple
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209's tail agenda for 210 orders Invariant->Owner->EnforcementPoint->Test->Evidence->FailureMode; Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple orders enforcement, monitoring, test, failure (test before the implied evidence); but Step 210's own boxed Section 210.40 conclusion states Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance (evidence before test); Step 211 Section 211.2 (boxed) and Step 214 Section 214.2 (boxed) both revert to Test before Evidence. Four sources agree that Test precedes Evidence; Step 210's one boxed conclusion disagrees with all of them, including with its own tuple -- the direction matters (Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test; Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout). This is Contradiction #5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
a_rows_sample.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #2 — Provenance composition (208) excludes the authority Step 209 requires
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 Section 208.25 asserts as an equality P(G)=P(A)∪P(E), boxed as 'provenance must be closed under semantic transformation.' Step 209 Section 209.4 requires Final(D)⇒DecisionBasis(D)∧Authority(D). Since Authority(D), the governance grant that made a decision final, is in neither P(A) nor P(E), a governed decision's provenance under Section 208.25 cannot contain its own authority, yet Step 209's own traceability requirement (Basis(D) including authority) demands that it does -- the two cannot both hold. Independently checked, the equality is additionally vacuous if closure holds (P(A)⊇P(E) implies the union is just P(A)) and self-refuting if it does not. Severity HIGH.

a_rows_sample.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

b_rows_sample.anchor: F | D | P | U ... F = Fact ... D = Derived ... P = Proposed ... U = Unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way epistemic classification for every architectural statement: F=Fact (directly supported by engineering evidence), D=Derived (logically derived from facts/observations), P=Proposed (a recommendation or future design), U=Unknown (insufficient evidence).

b_rows_sample.anchor: We designed the system according to this architecture from the beginning ... That would be misleading. The intellectually stronger story is: Experience -> Problem -> Observation -> Experiment -> Pattern -> Abstraction -> Theory -> Architecture
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against retrospectively rewriting the book's history as if the system had been designed according to the derived architecture from the beginning, calling this misleading; proposes instead the causal chain Experience->Problem->Observation->Experiment->Pattern->Abstraction->Theory->Architecture as the intellectually stronger and more honest narrative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How can this artifact support our current theory? We should ask: What does this artifact actually establish?
b_rows_sample.statement: States the archaeological method's central mindset shift: treat prior artifacts (prompts, AI outputs, architecture docs, ADRs, code, tests, rejected ideas, contradictions, revisions) as evidence to be asked 'what does this actually establish', never 'how does this support our current theory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E(A_j)={Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions} ... Artifact -> Evidence -> Interpretation. Not: Theory -> selective evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines evidence extraction per artifact E(A_j) as the set {Facts,Observations,Decisions,Assumptions,Experiments,Failures,Questions}, to be connected to architectural concepts only afterward (Artifact->Evidence->Interpretation), explicitly rejecting the reverse flow Theory->selective evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance enforcement could not yet be established from the available evidence ... unless we have evidence of absence
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that absence of knowledge about whether a property (e.g. provenance) exists in an implementation be written as Unknown ('could not yet be established from the available evidence'), never as an assertion of absence ('is missing') unless positive evidence of absence exists.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Prov(C)={A_1,A_2,...,A_n} ... provenance of architecture itself
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes giving architectural claims themselves a provenance set Prov(C)={A_1,...,A_n} of supporting artifacts, so a reader can trace Claim->Evidence -- termed 'provenance of architecture itself'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ADL = Decision -> Problem -> Evidence -> Alternatives -> Rationale -> Consequence
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an Architecture Decision Lineage ADL = Decision->Problem->Evidence->Alternatives->Rationale->Consequence, proposed to eventually become part of the KnowledgeOS architecture itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Failure -> Knowledge ... some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches ... What did not work ... alongside ... What eventually worked. Otherwise the final architecture looks inevitable
b_rows_sample.statement: States the negative-result principle: a failed experiment (Hypothesis H tested, Result=not-H) is Failure->Knowledge, not useless, and some of the strongest architectural principles may originate from failed approaches; the book should explicitly record what did not work alongside what eventually worked, because otherwise the final architecture looks falsely inevitable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ChosenPattern ... RejectedPattern ... ReasonForRejection
b_rows_sample.statement: Connects the negative-result principle to the corpus's Chapter 4 theme: knowledge includes discrimination between Valid and Invalid, so the architecture should preserve not only the ChosenPattern but sometimes the RejectedPattern and ReasonForRejection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_{t+1}=E(A_t, Evidence_t) ... Architecture is not merely documentation growth. It is knowledge evolution
b_rows_sample.statement: Models architecture evolution as A_{t+1}=E(A_t,Evidence_t) driven by new evidence, explicitly rejecting the weaker model A_{t+1}=A_t+more documentation; calls architecture 'knowledge evolution', not documentation growth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ΔA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an architecture-evolution tuple DeltaA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact) as the architecture's evolutionary provenance record for each change.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stage 1 ... What problem was first recognized? ... Stage 7 What remains unverified?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing an 'epistemic chronology' (not necessarily calendar chronology) in seven stages: problem recognized, assumptions made, experiments challenging them, patterns emerged, abstractions introduced, resulting architecture, and what remains unverified -- proposed as the backbone of the eventual book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed Reality ... Architectural Interpretation ... Normative Design
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates three reconstruction layers: Observed Reality (what happened), Architectural Interpretation (what it means), and Normative Design (what should be built), illustrated with an AI-code-inconsistency example running observation->derived-knowledge->proposal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O=observations ... D=g(O)=derived knowledge ... P=h(D)=proposed architecture ... P ⇏ O
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes O->D->P (observations, derived knowledge via D=g(O), proposed architecture via P=h(D)) with the explicit non-implication P does-not-imply O: a proposal cannot retroactively become evidence for the observation that motivated it, protecting the book from circular reasoning (e.g. avoiding 'we need deterministic assurance because KnowledgeOS is a deterministic assurance platform').

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_fact=High if directly supported by primary implementation evidence ... C_derived=Medium if the inference depends on assumptions ... avoid false numerical precision
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a qualitative confidence label (e.g. C_fact=High, C_derived=Medium) attached to F/D/P/U claims only when justified, again warning against false numerical precision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Primary ... source code; configuration; database schema; test result; runtime behavior; direct experiment ... Secondary ... AI analysis; architecture summary; meeting notes; retrospective explanation. Secondary evidence ... should not silently override primary evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Primary evidence (source code, configuration, database schema, test result, runtime behavior, direct experiment) from Secondary evidence (AI analysis, architecture summary, meeting notes, retrospective explanation), warning that secondary evidence must not silently override primary evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AIClaim -> Hypothesis. Then: ImplementationEvidence -> Fact ... AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States that an AI-generated statement (e.g. Claude or DeepSeek claiming 'the system uses invariant-driven architecture') is not itself proof but a hypothesis, only becoming Fact once corroborated by implementation evidence; boxes the AI epistemic boundary AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence as one of the book's strongest intended methodological principles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We are using AI to reconstruct an architecture for an AI engineering platform ... The architecture is therefore being used to validate the method by which it is being reconstructed ... The method is correct because it follows the architecture [is circular]
b_rows_sample.statement: Notes the self-referential situation of using AI to reconstruct the architecture of an AI engineering platform (a useful meta-level experiment), then explicitly warns against circular validation ('the method is correct because it follows the architecture'); the reconstruction method must independently satisfy Evidence+Reproducibility+Traceability before it can be said to exemplify the architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) ... Invariant -> Test -> Evidence. This creates a closed assurance loop
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Architecture Assurance Graph into an Evidence-Architecture-Graph EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) with edges Evidence->Claim->Decision->Architecture->Invariant and potentially Invariant->Test->Evidence, closing the assurance loop, then generalizes to the full cycle Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge, calling architecture 'a learning system'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Learning -> ArchitectureDrift ... Architecture evolution must itself be governed
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that ungoverned architectural learning becomes ArchitectureDrift, boxing the principle that architecture evolution must itself be governed, and lists six questions a software change should answer (what changed, why, which invariant is affected, which bounded context owns it, what evidence justifies it, how was it verified) as a stronger Software Change Governance model.
