a_rows_sample.anchor: A_{t+1}=E(A_t, Evidence_t) ... Architecture is not merely documentation growth. It is knowledge evolution
a_rows_sample.statement: Models architecture evolution as A_{t+1}=E(A_t,Evidence_t) driven by new evidence, explicitly rejecting the weaker model A_{t+1}=A_t+more documentation; calls architecture 'knowledge evolution', not documentation growth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ΔA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an architecture-evolution tuple DeltaA=(Trigger,Evidence,Decision,Rationale,Impact) as the architecture's evolutionary provenance record for each change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stage 1 ... What problem was first recognized? ... Stage 7 What remains unverified?
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes reconstructing an 'epistemic chronology' (not necessarily calendar chronology) in seven stages: problem recognized, assumptions made, experiments challenging them, patterns emerged, abstractions introduced, resulting architecture, and what remains unverified -- proposed as the backbone of the eventual book.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observed Reality ... Architectural Interpretation ... Normative Design
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates three reconstruction layers: Observed Reality (what happened), Architectural Interpretation (what it means), and Normative Design (what should be built), illustrated with an AI-code-inconsistency example running observation->derived-knowledge->proposal.

a_rows_sample.anchor: O=observations ... D=g(O)=derived knowledge ... P=h(D)=proposed architecture ... P ⇏ O
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes O->D->P (observations, derived knowledge via D=g(O), proposed architecture via P=h(D)) with the explicit non-implication P does-not-imply O: a proposal cannot retroactively become evidence for the observation that motivated it, protecting the book from circular reasoning (e.g. avoiding 'we need deterministic assurance because KnowledgeOS is a deterministic assurance platform').

a_rows_sample.anchor: C_fact=High if directly supported by primary implementation evidence ... C_derived=Medium if the inference depends on assumptions ... avoid false numerical precision
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a qualitative confidence label (e.g. C_fact=High, C_derived=Medium) attached to F/D/P/U claims only when justified, again warning against false numerical precision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Primary ... source code; configuration; database schema; test result; runtime behavior; direct experiment ... Secondary ... AI analysis; architecture summary; meeting notes; retrospective explanation. Secondary evidence ... should not silently override primary evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Primary evidence (source code, configuration, database schema, test result, runtime behavior, direct experiment) from Secondary evidence (AI analysis, architecture summary, meeting notes, retrospective explanation), warning that secondary evidence must not silently override primary evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AIClaim -> Hypothesis. Then: ImplementationEvidence -> Fact ... AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States that an AI-generated statement (e.g. Claude or DeepSeek claiming 'the system uses invariant-driven architecture') is not itself proof but a hypothesis, only becoming Fact once corroborated by implementation evidence; boxes the AI epistemic boundary AI Interpretation != Engineering Evidence as one of the book's strongest intended methodological principles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We are using AI to reconstruct an architecture for an AI engineering platform ... The architecture is therefore being used to validate the method by which it is being reconstructed ... The method is correct because it follows the architecture [is circular]
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes the self-referential situation of using AI to reconstruct the architecture of an AI engineering platform (a useful meta-level experiment), then explicitly warns against circular validation ('the method is correct because it follows the architecture'); the reconstruction method must independently satisfy Evidence+Reproducibility+Traceability before it can be said to exemplify the architecture.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) ... Invariant -> Test -> Evidence. This creates a closed assurance loop
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Architecture Assurance Graph into an Evidence-Architecture-Graph EAG=(Evidence,Claims,Decisions,Invariants,Architecture) with edges Evidence->Claim->Decision->Architecture->Invariant and potentially Invariant->Test->Evidence, closing the assurance loop, then generalizes to the full cycle Observation->Knowledge->Architecture->Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->NewKnowledge, calling architecture 'a learning system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Learning -> ArchitectureDrift ... Architecture evolution must itself be governed
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns that ungoverned architectural learning becomes ArchitectureDrift, boxing the principle that architecture evolution must itself be governed, and lists six questions a software change should answer (what changed, why, which invariant is affected, which bounded context owns it, what evidence justifies it, how was it verified) as a stronger Software Change Governance model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What happened? ... What remained unknown? ... R(S_i)=(O_i,L_i,A_i,V_i,U_i)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-question per-step reconstruction record R(S_i)=(Observation,Learning,Architecture,Verification,Unknown) to be applied to each of Steps 1-182, explicitly changing mode from generating new theory to reconstructing the evidentiary basis of existing theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: StepCount ≠ KnowledgeCount ... exploratory; repetitive; corrective; validation; implementation; philosophical; mathematical; editorial; prompt-engineering; synthesis
b_rows_sample.statement: States that a conversational 'step' is not necessarily an architectural contribution (some are exploratory, repetitive, corrective, editorial, etc.), so StepCount != KnowledgeCount, requiring the reconstruction to discover the actual knowledge-bearing events rather than treat all 182 steps as equal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: OBS Observation ... UNK Insufficient evidence ... A single step can have more than one tag internally
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a 14-code step-type classification (OBS/EXP/MAT/DDD/ARC/GOV/AI/VER/FAIL/DEC/PHI/SYN/REP/UNK) allowing multiple tags per step, crossed with the F/D/P/U epistemic-status axis (Type x EpistemicStatus) so e.g. 'ARC+D' denotes an architectural derivation rather than an observed fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Which architectural principles appear independently more than once? ... Convergence(I) = NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) ... We should not immediately turn this into a numerical quality score
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a convergence test: if the same architectural principle emerges from multiple unrelated observations (P_1, P_7, P_31 all pointing to invariant I), that repeated independent emergence is treated as strong evidence the principle is fundamental, formalized as Convergence(I)=NumberOfIndependentEvidencePaths(I) but explicitly not reduced to a numerical quality score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity≠State ... Knowledge≠Authority ... Unknown≠False ... CurrentState≠History ... Generation≠Validation ... Validation≠Authorization ... Claim→Evidence ... Context_A≠Context_B ... These are candidate principles, not yet declared final conclusions
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists ten candidate recurring architectural distinctions to be tested against the actual Steps-1-182 evidence rather than accepted by default (Identity!=State, Knowledge!=Authority, Decision!=Execution, Execution!=Outcome, Unknown!=False, CurrentState!=History, Generation!=Validation, Validation!=Authorization, Claim->Evidence, Context_A!=Context_B), explicitly labelled candidates pending evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: They are all forms of: A ≠ B where software engineering frequently makes the mistake: A ≈ B ... restoring distinctions that had been collapsed
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a deeper common structure across the recurring principles: each is an instance of A!=B guarding against a common engineering mistake of collapsing A~=B (Identity~=State, Prediction~=Truth, Knowledge~=Authority, Execution~=Outcome), proposing this pattern-of-restoring-collapsed-distinctions as possibly one of the deepest architectural themes in the entire book.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving distinctions that carry semantic, temporal, epistemic or governance meaning ... SemanticIntegrity ∝ DistinctionPreservation ... a hypothesis, not a proven theorem
b_rows_sample.statement: States the 'distinction preservation' hypothesis (robust knowledge-centric software depends on preserving semantically/temporally/epistemically/governance-meaningful distinctions), formalized as SemanticIntegrity proportional-to DistinctionPreservation, explicitly labelled a hypothesis to be tested against the Steps-1-182 evidence rather than a proven theorem; connects this across DDD (Entity!=ValueObject), mathematics (x!=y), statistics (Observed!=Inferred, Correlation!=Causation), governance (Capability!=Authority) and AI engineering (Generation!=Verification) as convergent instances of one meta-principle: do not collapse distinctions that matter.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Krishna ~ Perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations ... What would a software system need if it were required to preserve continuity across changing states? ... Versioning, Provenance, History, Lineage, Context
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a careful literary (not architectural) interpretation of Krishna as 'a perspective possessing continuity across changing manifestations', translating this into the engineering question of what a system needs to preserve continuity across changing states (versioning, provenance, history, lineage, context), explicitly warning against the trivializing claim 'Krishna is the system's memory'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Philosophical Analogy ≠ Technical Proof ... Outcome A ... retrospective analogy ... Outcome B ... repeatedly influenced ... Outcome C ... independently emerged technically and philosophically ... the most interesting result
b_rows_sample.statement: States three possible historical outcomes for the Gita lens's actual role to be determined by the reconstruction rather than assumed: (A) it was purely a retrospective analogy applied after the fact, (B) it repeatedly and genuinely influenced engineering questions during development, (C) the same principles independently emerged both technically and philosophically -- rated the most interesting possible result, expressible as EngineeringObservation<->PhilosophicalReflection without either proving the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a technical invariant existed before the corresponding Gītā reflection ... TechnicalDiscovery -> PhilosophicalRecognition ... those are different histories. The Evidence Ledger will tell us which actually occurred
b_rows_sample.statement: States that chronology determines which of two different intellectual histories occurred (technical discovery preceding philosophical recognition, or vice versa) and that only the actual Evidence Ledger -- not narrative preference -- can establish which; reframes Step 215's most important task as determining 'when did the idea enter the reasoning', not merely what was concluded.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 182 Steps -> 43 SignificantEvents -> 17 CoreInsights -> 8 ArchitecturalPrinciples -> 4 MajorThemes. The exact numbers are unknown
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a compression pipeline reducing 182 raw steps to a small number of significant events, core insights, architectural principles, and major themes (illustrative counts only, explicitly not fixed), arguing the book should present the intellectual structure hidden inside the steps rather than the 182 steps themselves; proposes an intermediate 5-epoch structure (Problem Recognition -> Experimentation -> DDD/Domain Modeling -> Mathematical/Epistemic Formalization -> KnowledgeOS/AI-Engineering Architecture) explicitly not to be frozen before the evidence determines it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture_observed ... Architecture_designed ... Architecture_implemented ... Architecture_proposed ... Observed ≠ Intended ≠ Implemented ≠ Target
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that the single word 'architecture' conflates at least four distinct referents (observed, intended, implemented, target/proposed) that may differ from each other, proposing Observed!=Intended!=Implemented!=Target as a central reconstruction rule; separately notes that linguistic markers in generated text ('should' signals P, 'the code contains' signals F if verified, 'therefore requires' signals D) can help automatically classify epistemic status at scale.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step Source Artifact Date/Sequence Primary Topic Type Observation Fact Hypothesis Experiment Result Derived Insight Decision Rejected Alternative Architectural Principle Invariant Evidence Gita Connection Status [F/D/P/U] Confidence Open Question
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies the Step 215 Artifact: a 19-column Master Reconstruction Matrix schema intended as the master source for eventual book-writing, including a dedicated 'Gita Connection' column and 'Rejected Alternative' column.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not: rewrite the book; freeze the chapter structure; invent missing evidence; merge competing concepts; eliminate contradictions; assume implementation ... Reconstruct. Analyze. Synthesize. Write.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists nine things not to do before reconstruction is complete (rewrite the book, freeze chapter structure, invent missing evidence, merge competing concepts, eliminate contradictions, assume implementation, over-architect philosophical analogies, assign arbitrary percentages, create formulas for their own sake), sequencing the correct order as Reconstruct -> Analyze -> Synthesize -> Write.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Phase 1 — Archaeology ... Phase 2 — Separation of Concerns ... Phase 3 — Synthesis ... This is the correct point at which Claude should eventually begin chapter-by-chapter writing. Not before
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a three-phase book-production architecture: Phase 1 Archaeology (S1..S182 -> Evidence Ledger, understand what happened), Phase 2 Separation of Concerns (separate Facts from Derivations from Proposals from PhilosophicalInterpretations, preventing conceptual contamination), Phase 3 Synthesis (Evidence->Patterns->Principles->Architecture->Book), stating chapter-by-chapter writing is correct only after all three phases, not before.

b_rows_sample.anchor: B = Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection) ... ClaimStrength ≤ EvidenceStrength ... PhilosophicalReflection ≠ TechnicalEvidence ... CurrentArchitecture ≠ TargetArchitecture
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final synthesis equation for the whole book-generation process, B=Synthesize(Evidence,Experiments,Failures,Insights,Architecture,PhilosophicalReflection), subject to three boxed constraints (ClaimStrength<=EvidenceStrength, PhilosophicalReflection!=TechnicalEvidence, CurrentArchitecture!=TargetArchitecture), explicitly framed as protecting the book against retrospective rewriting, overclaiming, and confusing philosophy with engineering proof.

b_rows_sample.anchor: It should be the actual execution of the reconstruction ... I should not fabricate their contents from the current conversation ... Once they are available here, we can process them in batches
b_rows_sample.statement: Previews Step 216: not another theoretical step but the actual execution of the reconstruction, explicitly refusing to fabricate the contents of Steps 1-182 from memory/conversation and requiring the real historical artifacts to be brought in and processed in batches, after which Step 183 onward may need renaming or absorption into the synthesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

b_rows_sample.anchor: IT SPECIFIES A METHOD. It reconstructs nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Exhaustive machine count of every step-index token in Step 215 ('Reconstruct Steps 1-182'): of the 182 steps, only 6 are individually named (1, 2, 3, 73, 91, 182), 0 are quoted, 0 are given any content, 0 are given a substantive verdict, and 176 never appear at all. The file's only data matrix (Section 215.5) has 40 cells (8 columns x 5 rows): 28 are the placeholder '...' and 12 are filled, all with step index/type-tag/status-tag -- zero cells contain information about any of the 182 steps. Step 215 itself concedes 'the exact contents must come from the actual saved artifacts, not memory or invention,' and names its own future deliverable, the 'Step 215 Artifact — Master Reconstruction Matrix,' as not yet produced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the two live step indices used as notation examples do not match the real corpus steps they name
b_rows_sample.statement: Verifiable error in Step 215's notation examples: Step 91's real corpus file is titled 'Formal Specification and Refinement', but Step 215 tags it 'EXP + F' (an experimentally established fact); under Step 215's own taxonomy (Section 215.3) a formal-specification step should be tagged MAT or VER, not EXP. Step 73 ('Identity, Trust and Cryptographic Provenance') tagged 'ARC + D' is defensible and not called an error. The Step 91 mismatch's status is ambiguous as to intent (possibly pure notation demonstration) but unambiguous as to fact: the tag does not describe the step it names. Not silently repaired.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 9 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \text{Ontology} \supset \text{Kernel} $$ but: $$ \text{Ontology} \neq \text{Kernel} $$ This distinction explains why recovering Sañjaya does not require promoting `Sañjaya` itself to a new primitive.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a new distinction: the reconstructed ontology strictly contains the ratified 8-primitive kernel (Ontology ⊃ Kernel) but is not identical to it (Ontology ≠ Kernel) -- the ontology contains additional typed constructs (like W, Ω, O) above and around the ratified primitives, which is why recovering Sanjaya does not require promoting it to a new kernel primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### 21.1 No `Knowledge` primitive ... ### 21.2 No universal Knower inside KnowledgeOS ... ### 21.3 No `Θ_total` ... ### 21.4 No `𝒦_ātma` ... ### 21.5 No repaired Θ operators
a_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates an explicit five-item exclusion list stating what the reconstructed ontology does NOT contain: no Knowledge primitive (Jnana does not justify adding it), no universal Knower inside KnowledgeOS (the theological proposition is outside the formal falsification domain; the KnowledgeOS result is only that a universal Knower is not derivable as an architectural requirement), no Theta_total (rejected by typing), no K_atma (rejected, persistence already represented by existing provenance/lineage structures), and no repaired Theta operators (the R4 type-check failure is evidence against the construction, not a missing implementation feature).

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \mathcal K_{\text{ātma}} \text{ adds no independently required ontology} $$ ... $$ Lineage = \Pi \circ \mathcal R_{\mathrm{der}}^{*} $$ already supplying the required persistence structure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a formal justification for rejecting K_atma as a needed construct: every candidate persistence invariant tested reduces to either governance/provenance Π or the derivation relation R_der*, with Lineage = Π ∘ R_der* already supplying the required persistence structure, so K_atma adds no independently required ontology (classified RX).

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Concept | Ontological status | Step-286 result | ... | Qualify | Required projection function | **G1 / no body** |
a_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates ontological status and Step-286 result for 24 named concepts (W, Omega/Sanjaya, O, K_t, N, Proposition, Entity, Observation, Relation, Assertion, Pi, delta, Command, Jnana, Knowledge, Sanjaya_K, Arjuna_K, K_atma, Theta_total, semantic/observational/provenance-sensitive equality, Qualify), consolidating every recovery, rejection, and open-gap finding from the batch into one reference table.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Reality is not observation; observation is not knowing; knowing is not knowledge; knowledge state is not action; and action is not transformation.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Compresses the entire ontological reconstruction into one central statement: reality is not observation; observation is not knowing; knowing is not knowledge; knowledge state is not action; and action is not transformation — formally W≠O≠N, Observation≠Evidence≠Decision≠Action, Command≠Transformation, and Jñāna∼δ (correspondence, not identity).

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Step 286 closes the ontology reconstruction, but does not close the formal system.** The remaining formal blockers are: $$ \boxed{ Qualify } $$ and the incomplete decision procedures for the non-structural equality relations.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the final scope of Step 286: it closes the ontology reconstruction (the ontology is now structurally reconstructed and typed from the corpus, with the missing-layer finding reduced to a missing function body and incomplete decision procedures) but does not close the formal system — the remaining formal blockers are Qualify and the incomplete decision procedures for the non-structural equality relations; no new primitive is required by the recovered evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 286 answered: **What exists?** Step 287 asks: **What must remain true?**
a_rows_sample.statement: States the final boundary distinguishing consecutive steps: Step 286 (Ontology) answered 'what exists', Step 287 (Invariant Research) asks 'what must remain true', and only a future step ('Invariant Canonization') may promote I from a research construct to a canonical KnowledgeOS component, once candidates are typed, tested, falsified where possible, and classified.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **286 · Ontology** | **Research / reconstruction of the ontology** | ✅ Can and should be written now | | **287 · Invariants ℐ** | **Research / invariant derivation and audit** | ✅ Can and should be written now | | **D288 · Decision Procedures** | Governance-dependent closure | ⏸️ Scoped, not executed | | Canonical Ontology | Architecture/governance artifact | ❌ Not yet promotable |
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms both Step 286 (Ontology) and Step 287 (Invariants) should be written now as research artifacts, neither blocked by D288's scoped-not-executed status — doing them now is useful because they may reveal which D288 decisions are genuinely necessary versus derivable from the reconstructed model; a canonical/promoted ontology remains not yet promotable. Step 286 should answer 'what ontology can actually be reconstructed from the corpus, and which commitments remain unresolved', not 'what ontology should KnowledgeOS have' (the latter would cross the research/governance boundary).

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **286 · Ontology** | reconstruct the ontology **around the established `K_t → (𝒜,ℛ)` projection**, keeping `K_core` unresolved. ... | **287 · Invariants `𝓘`** | derive and audit `𝓘(K_t)` — **over the ratified `K_t`, not over an unresolved choice.** ... | **D288** | separate closure mechanism for the equality/qualification blockers | scoped, not executed |
a_rows_sample.statement: Hands explicit, binding mandates and status lines to the three downstream steps: Step 286 must reconstruct the ontology around the established K_t->(A,R) projection while keeping K_core unresolved, carrying the status line 'RESEARCH ARTIFACT — corpus reconstruction; normative promotion explicitly prohibited'; Step 287 must derive and audit the invariant universe I(K_t) over the ratified K_t (not an unresolved choice), tagging every invariant CORPUS/DERIVED/CANDIDATE/NORMATIVE/BLOCKED and testing dependence on ≡/≈/≅_λ/Qualify/Π/Sigma's component orders; D288 remains the separate closure mechanism, scoped not executed. States 286 must come first since 287's invariants should be derived against 286's ontology, and neither is blocked by D288.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E1 ... sup requires an ORDER on Ω ... E2 ... targets the superseded 2-tuple Σ₀=(D,S) ... E3 ... quantifies over 𝒯, which is UNENUMERATED
a_rows_sample.statement: Three checkable type errors in 'solved' Gita-chapter formalizations, invisible from the correspondence register (which lists terms, not formalizations): E1 (Ch13 3.3) K_supreme = sup(Omega) is ill-formed because sup requires an order on Omega, but 0 of 5 ratified Sigma axes carries an established order (per Step 291) and (Omega,F,P) does not exist (per gap G-22). E2 (Ch14 88-97) Sigma=(Supported,Strong)/(Unknown,Weak)/(Refuted,Unknown) uses values ('Supported','Refuted') that are not values of any of the five ratified Sigma axes (S is in {None,Weak,Moderate,Strong,VeryStrong}); the mapping actually targets the superseded 2-tuple Sigma_0=(D,S) from Step 275, not the ratified 5-axis 2240-state Sigma. E3 (Ch8 3.1) K_atma(K_t)=K_atma(T(K_t)) for all T in the transformation set T quantifies over T, which is unenumerated -- well-formed but inapplicable, the same shape as gaps 258.20/258.21.

a_rows_sample.anchor: T4: 2 (Ch 1, Ch 13) — unchanged. T0 rose from 8 to 14 once the chapters were read directly.
a_rows_sample.statement: Completed 18-chapter tier table: T4 KERNEL stays at 2 (Ch1 Sanjaya->Omega corpus-native; Ch13 Kshetrajna->N not-in-K, R5, FA-4[E], but also T0 for its rival 7-type ontology, K=f(F,A_t), and error E1); T3 stays 8; T2 rose 5->6; T1 correspondence fell ~37->~32; T0 refuted/RX rose 8->14. Final conclusion: new kernel primitives from the Gita = 0, canonical relations = 0; the Gita CONSTRAINS the kernel, it does not POPULATE it. Reading the chapters directly did not add candidates -- it moved six from T1 to T0, because the register listed terms while the chapters contained formalizations that type-check badly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: none of this changes Steps 288–291. All remain `R6`.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly scopes what the tiering-completion licenses: establishes the tiering is complete/unchanged at T4, the lane conflict is real and measured, three formalizations carry checkable type errors, and a fourth disjoint primitive-level vocabulary exists. Does NOT license deleting, correcting, or superseding the external_research artifacts -- that is a registry/governance act, not a research one (they are placed non-normatively, so have not contaminated the kernel result; the conflict is one of record, not of derivation). None of this changes Steps 288-291, which all remain R6 -- taken as evidence the discipline worked, since the research lane reached its verdicts without consulting a parallel lane that had declared victory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \boxed{ \text{Candidate invariant} \not\Rightarrow \text{Canonical invariant} } $$ Each proposed invariant must survive: 1. source interpretation, 2. KnowledgeOS translation, 3. formal typing, 4. equality specification, 5. independent derivation, 6. falsification, 7. classification.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Step 287 as explicitly a research/falsification step, not a canonical-invariant step: a candidate invariant does not imply a canonical invariant, and each proposed invariant must survive seven stages (source interpretation, KnowledgeOS translation, formal typing, equality specification, independent derivation, falsification, classification) before promotion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \boxed{ \mathcal I(P): \forall K,o. Admissible(o,K) \Rightarrow (P(K)\Rightarrow P(\delta(K,o))) } $$ ... These questions must be answered before calling \(P\) an invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives the generic invariant schema I(P): for all K,o, Admissible(o,K) implies (P(K) implies P(delta(K,o))), and states this schema itself requires answering: what is the state domain, what is the equality relation, what transitions are included, is P structural/semantic/provenance-sensitive/observational, and is P universal or scoped to a particular transition class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | I-01 | Knower identity persists | Identity | **Strong candidate** | | I-02 | Relevant provenance survives derivation | Transition / lineage | **Open** | | I-03 | Admissibility is outcome-independent | Governance / predicate | **Supported** | | I-04 | Command ≠ Transformation | Typing | **Supported** | | I-05 | Validity ≠ Outcome | Predicate separation | **Supported** | | I-06 | Knower ∉ observed state | Layer/ontology | **Supported candidate** | | I-07 | Reality ≠ Observation | Layer | **Supported** | | I-08 | Observation ≠ Interpretation | Layer | **Supported candidate** | | I-09 | Unknown/conflicting/unresolved are preserved at observation layer | Observation | **Candidate** | | I-10 | Semantic state preservation under selected transformations | Semantic | **Open** | | I-11 | Provenance-sensitive preservation | Provenance | **Open** | | I-12 | Universal state invariant independent of observer | Observation | **Open / likely too strong** |
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 12-item candidate invariant matrix (I-01 through I-12) spanning Identity, Typing, Transition/lineage, Governance/predicate, Predicate separation, Layer/ontology, Observation, Semantic and Provenance categories, each with a current status (Strong candidate / Open / Supported / Supported candidate / Candidate / likely too strong); explicitly states the final invariant set must not yet be inferred from this table.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identity invariants ... Typing invariants ... Transition invariants ... A fourth category may be required: Layer invariants
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a four-category invariant taxonomy under I: Identity invariants (N persistence, provenance), Typing invariants (Command≠δ, N∉K), Transition invariants (P(Kt)->P(Kt+1), admissibility, lineage), and Layer invariants (Reality≠Observation, Observation≠Knower, Observation≠Interpretation); explicitly frames whether these all legitimately belong to one mathematical object I as itself a Step-287 research question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **No invariant may be stated without a transition scope.** ... $$ \boxed{ \forall (K,o)\in T_P: P(K) \Rightarrow P(\delta(K,o)) } $$
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the equality-typing discipline to scope: no invariant may be stated without an explicit transition scope T_P (which transitions preservation is claimed over — every transformation, every admissible one, every authorized one, etc.), refining the invariant schema to quantify only over (K,o) in T_P.

b_rows_sample.anchor: $$ \boxed{ Invariant(P) \text{ is relation-relative where }P\text{ compares objects} } $$ For example, a transformation can preserve semantic state ... while changing ... structural
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues that any invariant comparing objects is relation-relative among the four equality relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ): a transformation can preserve semantic state (K_t ≡ K_{t+1}) while changing structurally (K_t ≠_structural K_{t+1}) because metadata/representation changed, and provenance-sensitive equality may distinguish states that semantic equality identifies.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 287 must distinguish: $$ \text{invariant} $$ from: $$ \text{conserved information} $$ ... This distinction prevents the persistence research from accidentally collapsing into state immutability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes an invariant (P(Kt) implies P(Kt+1)) from a conservation claim (a stronger statement about preserved content or quantity): the existence of Lineage does not imply every aspect of the previous state is conserved, and N persisting does not mean K_t=K_{t+1} — preventing identity-persistence research from collapsing into state immutability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: For every invariant: 1. establish that the antecedent can actually hold; 2. establish that the transition class is non-empty; 3. establish that the equality relation permits meaningful comparison; 4. only then evaluate preservation. Thus: **No vacuous invariant counts as substantively established.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes the D285-5 vacuity lesson into a mandatory four-step vacuity check for every candidate invariant: establish the antecedent can actually hold, establish the transition class is non-empty, establish the equality relation permits meaningful comparison, and only then evaluate preservation — no vacuous invariant counts as substantively established.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Independent ... ### Corroborated ... ### Philosophical analogy ... ### Unsupported ... This preserves: $$ \boxed{ \text{corroboration}\neq\text{derivation} } $$
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a four-way independence classification for each candidate invariant: Independent (KOS derivation alone), Corroborated (KOS derivation plus Gita correspondence), Philosophical analogy (Gita distinction without independent KOS necessity), Unsupported (no valid derivation) — preserving the rule that corroboration is not the same as derivation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 287 must not: * introduce new invariants because they appear philosophically attractive; * turn every architectural constraint into a mathematical invariant; * treat provenance as automatically immutable; * assume semantic equality includes \(\Pi\); * assume observational equality without defining the observation set; * use theological propositions as falsification results; * repair rejected \(\Theta\) constructions; * introduce \(\mathcal K_{\text{ātma}}\); * introduce a universal Knower into the formal KnowledgeOS model; * declare the invariant set complete merely because candidate tests have passed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists ten explicit prohibitions for Step 287: no introducing invariants merely because they are philosophically attractive; no converting every architectural constraint into a mathematical invariant; no treating provenance as automatically immutable; no assuming semantic equality includes Pi; no assuming observational equality without defining the observation set; no using theological propositions as falsification results; no repairing rejected Theta constructions; no introducing K_atma; no introducing a universal Knower into the formal model; no declaring the invariant set complete merely because candidate tests passed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### G-I1 — What is the exact carrier of \(\mathcal I\)? ... ### G-I2 — What counts as a transition? ... ### G-I3 — Which equality applies? ... ### G-I4 — Which invariants are independent? ... ### G-I5 — Which invariants are temporal versus ontological?
b_rows_sample.statement: States five open research gaps that Step 287 begins with: G-I1 (what is the exact carrier/domain of I — predicates over K_t only, or over (K_t,o,Pi,N,O)?), G-I2 (what counts as a transition delta — commands, events, human actions, system transformations, governance decisions?), G-I3 (which of the four equality relations applies to each preservation claim?), G-I4 (which invariants are independently required versus merely restating architecture?), G-I5 (which invariants are temporal preservation laws versus ontological/typing laws, e.g. N∉K is not obviously temporal while Command≠δ is fundamentally a typing law)?

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 286 answered: **What exists?** Step 287 asks: **What must remain true?**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the final boundary distinguishing consecutive steps: Step 286 (Ontology) answered 'what exists', Step 287 (Invariant Research) asks 'what must remain true', and only a future step ('Invariant Canonization') may promote I from a research construct to a canonical KnowledgeOS component, once candidates are typed, tested, falsified where possible, and classified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **We can write STEP 287 now, but we must not pretend that every proposed invariant is already a KnowledgeOS invariant.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Given D288's finding that several foundations (≡, ≈, ≅_λ decision procedures; Qualify; O enumeration; 8-primitive minimality) remain formally unresolved, argues Step 287 can establish which invariants are derivable from the current corpus and ontology, but cannot legitimately conclude these are the final invariants I of KnowledgeOS — doing so would prematurely promote research into architecture, exactly what D288 forbids.

b_rows_sample.anchor: distinguish state invariants from qualification invariants ... $$ Observation \rightarrow Qualification \rightarrow Evidence $$ cannot simply be collapsed into: $$ Observation \Rightarrow Knowledge $$ because `Qualify` remains unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues Step 287 should distinguish state invariants from qualification invariants: the chain Observation -> Qualification -> Evidence cannot be collapsed into Observation implies Knowledge, because Qualify remains unresolved; likewise the mere existence of an ontology does not automatically make every ontological relation an invariant.

b_rows_sample.anchor: if we encounter something of the form $$ K_1 \equiv K_2 \Rightarrow P(K_1)=P(K_2) $$ we cannot call that a final invariant until the semantics of `≡` are fixed. ... any invariant relying upon observational equality must carry that parameter. And provenance-sensitive invariants ... must remain conditional until "relevant provenance" is formally specified.
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires that any candidate invariant using an unresolved equality relation be marked explicitly conditional: a semantic-equality-based invariant is not final until ≡'s semantics are fixed; an observational-equality-based invariant must carry its query/observation-set parameter Q explicitly; a provenance-sensitive invariant must remain conditional until 'relevant provenance' is formally specified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Therefore 287 must distinguish: **"The structure permits this invariant"** from **"KnowledgeOS has adopted this invariant."**
b_rows_sample.statement: States a general principle for Step 287: a mathematical structure permitting a candidate invariant is not the same claim as KnowledgeOS having adopted that invariant — the new Q-series findings must not repeat the earlier mistake of treating an unresolved mathematical structure as an absence of structure.
